Through systematic preliminary studies, we find that (1) LLM embeddings contain bidding-relevant cues yet cannot replace numerical features, and (2) gains emerge only with careful semantic–numeric integration rather than naive concatenation. Motivated by these findings, we propose SemBid , a novel auto-bidding framework that injects LLM-encoded semantics into offline bidding trajectories at the token level. SemBid introduces three semantic inputs: Task , History , and Strategy . It injects these semantics as tokens alongside numerical trajectory tokens and uses self-attention to integrate them, improving controllability and generalization across objectives. Across diverse scenarios and budget regimes, SemBid outperforms competitive baselines from offline RL and generative sequence modeling, with more consistent gains in overall performance, constraint satisfaction, and robustness. Our code is available at: github.com/AlanYu04/SemBid-CIKM2026 (https://github.com/AlanYu04/SemBid-CIKM2026).

papers.title: PRO-Bid: Pareto-Prioritized Regret Optimization for Constraint-Aware Generative Auto-Bidding
papers.abstract: Auto-bidding systems strive to maximize marketing value while maintaining high compliance with efficiency constraints, such as Target Cost-Per-Action (CPA). While Decision Transformers offer powerful sequence modeling capabilities, their application to this setting faces two challenges: 1) standard Return-to-Go conditioning causes state aliasing by ignoring the cost dimension, preventing precise resource pacing; and 2) standard regression constrains the policy to mimic historical averages, limiting its capacity to optimize performance near the high-efficiency boundary. To tackle these challenges, we propose PRO-Bid, a constraint-aware generative auto-bidding framework featuring systematic redesigns across data, architecture, and training via two synergistic mechanisms: 1) Constraint-Decoupled Pareto Representation (CDPR) separates global constraints into recursive cost and value contexts to restore resource perception, while reweighting trajectories based on the empirical Pareto frontier to prioritize high-efficiency data; and 2) Counterfactual Regret Optimization (CRO) employs a global predictor to evaluate alternative actions and identify promising local adjustments. By utilizing these high-utility outcomes as weighted regression targets, the model overcomes mean regression and approaches the empirical high-efficiency boundary. Extensive experiments on two public benchmarks and online A/B tests show that PRO-Bid achieves better constraint satisfaction and value acquisition than state-of-the-art baselines.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Learning for Address Linkage in Tracking Ecosystems via Large Language Models
affiliations: Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract: User tracking aims to identify network activities belonging to the same user across websites and network environments, supporting applications such as personalized recommendation and targeted advertising. As dynamic address allocation and modern privacy protections constrain traditional tracking methods, traffic-based tracking techniques have emerged to link dynamic addresses through traffic patterns. However, existing methods usually rely on large-scale user labels for supervised training, while such labels are difficult to obtain in TLS encrypted traffic, severely limiting model generalization. In this paper, we propose SLATE, a self-supervised address linkage framework integrated with LLMs under limited labeled data. Specifically, SLATE introduces a homologous subgraph discrimination task based on address behavior partitioning, which encourages the encoder to capture stable behavior patterns across temporal evolution from large-scale unlabeled data. Moreover, SLATE develops a graph semantic projection module, which enables the LLM to better interpret behavior graph representations through graph-text matching and node semantic classification, and further leverages its reasoning capability to support address linkage decisions. We evaluate SLATE on two real-world user datasets. Experimental results show that SLATE substantially outperforms the strongest self-supervised methods, achieving an average improvement of over 15% in Hits@1, while remaining competitive with state-of-the-art supervised methods. These findings demonstrate the strong potential of combining self-supervised learning with LLMs for address linkage in tracking ecosystems.

papers.title: PrivDedup: Fully Outsourced Privacy-Preserving Multi-Party Deduplication
affiliations: The Hang Seng University of Hong Kong
papers.abstract: Multi-party data collaboration increasingly requires deduplicating datasets held by independent providers. Although multi-party private set union (MPSU) provides a natural privacy-preserving abstraction, existing protocols require substantial provider-side interaction, while delegated MPSU still relies on a provider for result reconstruction and incurs super-linear computation overhead. We propose PrivDedup, a lightweight and fully outsourced protocol for exact privacy-preserving multi-party deduplication. PrivDedup recasts deduplication as protected table aggregation: providers independently encode encrypted records into invertible bloom lookup tables (IBLTs), and the server reconstructs the deduplicated union by aggregating and decoding the submitted tables without online inter-provider coordination. To prevent leakage beyond the intended union, pseudorandom coefficient scaling hides cross-provider overlap counts, while pairwise bucket masking conceals provider-specific table contents and provenance. If primary peeling leaves a residual core, a compact auxiliary table under an independent hash family enables recovery of the remaining elements. Evaluated over dataset sizes from 2 10 to 2 20 and 3–10 providers, PrivDedup reduces communication by 1.39–8.92× and end-to-end computation time by 1.13–12.24× compared with representative state-of-the-art MPSU and delegated MPSU protocols.

papers.title: VeilKD: Scalable Dual-Private Prompt-Driven Distillation from Cloud LLMs via Secure Inference
affiliations: Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract: Cloud-hosted Large Language Models (LLMs) have become key knowledge sources for domain-specific model training. Prompt-driven Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows clients to leverage these models for student training, but client prompts often contain sensitive information that is exposed when sent in plaintext. Existing Differential Privacy (DP)-based methods protect teacher-side data rather than client prompts, while defenses that inject Gaussian noise into prompt embeddings remain vulnerable to reconstruction attacks and may degrade distillation utility. To address this gap, we propose VeilKD, a scalable framework for dual-private prompt-driven knowledge distillation that protects client prompts via secure inference while preserving server-side model confidentiality. VeilKD employs linear-attention to enable cross-prompt batching and homomorphic optimizations for linear and nonlinear layers, achieving high-throughput encrypted teacher inference. Experiments across representative teacher-student distillation workloads demonstrate that VeilKD effectively prevents prompt reconstruction, preserves student utility within 0.10 average points of plaintext KD without output-side DP and DP-KD under matched DP settings, and accelerates per-thousand-prompt teacher-signal generation by 43.03–179.96× over prior secure inference methods.

papers.title: PINS: A Pivot-based Intersection Noise Scheme for Dense Embeddings Privacy in Information Retrieval
papers.abstract: Modern Information Retrieval (IR) systems, including small and medium-scale ones, often search across millions of documents. In many cases, data owners outsource retrieval to a third-party host to keep the data accessible. Furthermore, IR has also moved toward semantic matching with dense embeddings; although these embeddings are less interpretable than sparse representations, they remain vulnerable to model inversion attacks. Sending document embeddings to a third-party retrieval provider can, therefore, create privacy risks. An honest-but-curious host may try to reconstruct the original documents and exploit their content. One option is to send encrypted or obfuscated embeddings instead of the original vectors. Existing methods, however, have important limits: Asymmetric Scalar Product-preserving Encryption (ASPE) is vulnerable to inversion, while homomorphic encryption is often too costly. Building on the ASPE literature, we propose the Pivot-based Intersection Noise Scheme (PINS), a noise-injection method designed for dense IR. PINS aims to preserve retrieval quality while reducing leakage from document embeddings. It selects a set of pivots to define an obfuscation space, then chooses or samples an obfuscation point in that space for each document embedding. When measuring privacy-utility trade-off in terms of AUC, PINS reaches up to twice the effectiveness of state-of-the-art embedding obfuscation methods and also works with asymmetric bi-encoders, overcoming the current state-of-the-art. To favour reproducibility, we release PINS at https://github.com/guglielmof/2026-CIKM-PINS.

papers.title: Learning to Erase Private Knowledge from Multi-Documents for Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
affiliations: Beijing Academy of Blockchain and Edge Computing
papers.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a promising technique for applying LLMs to proprietary domains. However, retrieved documents may contain sensitive knowledge, posing risks of privacy leakage in generative results. Thus, effectively erasing private information from retrieved documents is a key challenge for RAG. Unlike traditional text anonymization, RAG should consider: (1) the inherent multi-document reasoning may face de-anonymization attacks; (2) private knowledge varies by scenarios, so users should be allowed to customize which information to erase; (3) preserving sufficient publicly available knowledge for generation tasks. This paper introduces the privacy erasure task for RAG and proposes Eraser4RAG, a private knowledge eraser that effectively removes user-defined private knowledge from documents while preserving sufficient public knowledge for generation. Specifically, we first construct a global knowledge graph to identify potential knowledge across documents, aiming to defend against de-anonymization attacks. Then we randomly split it into private and public sub-graphs, and fine-tune Flan-T5 to rewrite the retrieved documents, excluding private triples. Finally, the PPO algorithm optimizes the rewriting model to minimize private triples and maximize public triples retention. Experiments on four QA datasets demonstrate that Eraser4RAG achieves a strong privacy--utility balance among document-level rewriting methods, outperforming GPT-4o-based rewriting in private knowledge erasure while preserving substantially more public knowledge than aggressive keyword- or entity-suppression baselines.

papers.title: Graph-Driven Context-Preserving Anonymization for LLM Scaling
papers.abstract: The scaling of Large Language Models (LLMs) heavily relies on high-quality proprietary data, yet strict privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR) render vast amounts of real-world text containing Personally Identifiable Information (PII) inaccessible. Existing sanitization techniques struggle with implicit reference leakage and contextual degradation. In this paper, we propose a paradigm grounded in the hypothesis that LLM reasoning capabilities stem predominantly from the invariant logical context rather than from specific PII entities. We introduce a Graph-Driven Context-Preserving Anonymization Framework comprising three phases: (1) Global Graph Construction to explicitly model dependencies, (2) Targeted Topological Knock-out to isolate and prune explicit subject nodes and implicit coreference edges, and (3) Contextual Re-alignment for autoregressive reconstruction. Across the proprietary CCC-500 corpus and the public Text Anonymization Benchmark (TAB), evaluated over three random seeds against 18 heuristic, transformer-based, differentially private, and LLM-driven baselines, our method reaches 100.0 ± 0.00% Deterministic Desensitization Rate on CCC-500 and 99.8 ± 0.10% on TAB under parser-completeness conditions, while preserving downstream Top-1 Accuracy within 0.1 percentage points of unsanitized text on identity-orthogonal multi-hop QA. An isolation ablation confirms that both the graph topology and the constrained regenerator contribute independently to the result. All improvements over the strongest generative baseline (GPT-4o Few-shot) are significant at p<0.001 on a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test.

papers.title: Quantized Contrastive Unlearning
papers.abstract: The defining question for approximate machine unlearning is not how strongly to perturb the model, but which signal in its representation to perturb. Existing methods perturb both at once: the sample-specific detail that identifies the forget set and the semantic structure that supports generalization. The result is a familiar trade-off, where forgetting and utility move in opposite directions, with no principled rest point. We separate the two signals through feature-map quantization: the quantized feature retains the semantic structure while shedding the identifying detail, and therefore specifies what an unlearned representation should look like for each forget sample. Quantized Contrastive Unlearning (QCU) uses the logit of this quantized feature as the positive anchor and the logit of the original feature as the negative in a contrastive objective, pulling the model toward a target that is, by construction, close to the retrained-from-scratch model. The closeness is not asymptotic. We provide an analysis showing that, under explicit small-drift and alignment assumptions, the QCU stage moves the model closer to the Retrain reference in expectation, yielding a tighter initialization-dependent convergence bound for subsequent retain-set fine-tuning. The same loss form, without modification, consistently closes the gap to the retrained reference on both utility and privacy across image classification (CIFAR-10/100, SVHN, ImageNet), LLM unlearning on TOFU, backdoor removal, LiRA-based privacy auditing, and prompt-level concept erasure in Stable Diffusion, while every baseline fails to close the gap along at least one axis. Code is available at https://github.com/hyunjoon0208/QCU.

papers.title: SPER: Accelerating Progressive Entity Resolution via Stochastic Bipartite Maximization
affiliations: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens
papers.abstract: Entity Resolution (ER) is a critical data cleaning task for identifying records that refer to the same real-world entity. In the era of Big Data, traditional batch ER is often infeasible due to volume and velocity constraints, which call for Progressive ER methods that maximize recall within a limited computational budget. However, existing progressive approaches fail to scale to high-velocity streams because they rely on deterministic sorting to prioritize candidate pairs, a process that incurs prohibitive super-linear complexity and heavy initialization costs. To address this scalability wall, we introduce SPER (Stochastic Progressive ER), a novel framework that redefines prioritization as a sampling rather than a ranking problem. By replacing global sorting with a continuous stochastic bipartite maximization strategy, SPER acts as a probabilistic high-pass filter that selects high-utility pairs in strictly linear time. Extensive experiments on eight real-world datasets demonstrate that SPER achieves significant speedups (3x to >6x) over state-of-the-art baselines, while maintaining comparable recall and precision.

papers.title: ComPrivDet: Efficient Privacy Object Detection in Compressed Domains Through Inference Reuse
affiliations: University of Science and Technology of China
papers.abstract: As the Internet of Things (IoT) becomes deeply embedded in daily life, users are increasingly concerned about privacy leakage, especially from video, which holds rich, sensitive information. While many techniques can protect privacy, frame-by-frame protection in large-scale video analytics (e.g., smart communities) introduces significant latency. A more efficient solution is to first detect frames containing privacy objects (e.g., faces) and then apply selective protection. However, pixel-domain detection requires fully decoding video frames, incurring decoding overhead. Compressed-domain approaches directly analyze compressed video streams to accelerate inference, but often sacrifice accuracy, and the per-frame processing remains inefficient. Therefore, we propose ComPrivDet, an efficient framework for detecting privacy objects in compressed video by reusing I-frame inference results. ComPrivDet provides a pixel-domain detector on I-frames and a lightweight compressed-domain detector on P/B-frames. Leveraging compressed-domain cues to determine the presence of new objects, ComPrivDet either reuses I-frame results to skip P/B-frame detections or refines them with a lightweight detector. We prototype ComPrivDet on an edge server with an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU. ComPrivDet maintains 99.75% accuracy for private face detection and 96.83% for private license plate detection while skipping over 80% of inferences. It averages 1.36% higher accuracy with 57.23% lower inference latency than pixel-domain baselines, and 10.93% higher accuracy with 44.65% lower latency than compressed-domain baselines.

papers.title: PolyphaseDet: Sampling-Aware Visual Information Aggregation for Dense Aerial Object Mining
papers.abstract: Large-scale aerial imagery provides fine-grained visual information for urban analytics, traffic monitoring, emergency response, and geospatial data mining. A central challenge is to reliably detect tiny objects in high-resolution, dense, and cluttered scenes. Existing detector pyramids commonly rely on stride-based downsampling to aggregate multi-scale features. When objects occupy only a few pixels, such reductions may discard or alias fine spatial cues and make object representations sensitive to the sampling phase. We propose PolyphaseDet, a neck-local aggregation design for sampling-aware aerial tiny-object detection. PolyphaseDet contains two components. Polyphase-Preserving Injection (PPI) preserves phase-specific stride-4 evidence through space-to-depth reindexing before injecting it into the stride-8 representation. Phase-Offset Downsampling (POD) aggregates responses from multiple sampling offsets before committing features to a coarser grid. The backbone, decoder, matching strategy, loss function, and inference procedure are kept unchanged, isolating the effect of the proposed neck aggregation design. On VisDrone2019-DET, PolyphaseDet improves a controlled baseline from 28.8 to 32.9 AP at 640 × 640 input resolution, and reaches 40.3 AP at 1280 × 1280. On AI-TOD, it achieves 28.1 AP. Ablation studies show that the gains are not simply due to forwarding P2 features, adding extra branches, or using generic blur-based downsampling. PolyphaseDet also improves prediction stability under one-pixel input translations while maintaining real-time efficiency comparable to that of the RT-DETR baseline.

papers.title: Lance: A LANGUAGE-ANCHORED CLOSED-LOOP ESTIMATOR for Bridging Low-Level Image Fusion and High-Level Semantic Understanding in Remote Sensing
affiliations: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract: Remote sensing image fusion and semantic interpretation are usually optimized separately, so reconstruction quality need not preserve downstream retrieval utility. We propose LANCE, which uses structured language as an explicit, indexable semantic state. A frozen vision–language model maps the input to a closed-vocabulary text record; a language-conditioned generator fuses the imagery; and a dense verifier with a differentiable continuous summarizer re-describes the output. Text–text consistency and anti-collapse contrastive text–mask losses with negative queries close the loop without dense annotations or VLM fine-tuning. A variational EM formulation yields a per-step contraction result under regularity assumptions, distinguishing semantic faithfulness from verifier overfitting. Across seven test sets on GF2, QuickBird, WorldView-III, and WorldView-II, LANCE improves reduced-scale reference metrics by up to 11.7% (median 2.1%) over the strongest learning baseline. Independent evaluation using a held-out VLM and a supervised aerial detector yields gains of +6.4 mAP and +0.072 open-vocabulary F1 over the closest competitor. Text perturbations, cross-verifier transfer, and pseudo-RGB ablations examine the mechanisms underlying these gains. The framework connects image fusion to verifiable semantic representations for multimodal retrieval and knowledge management.

papers.title: SWORD: Scene-Grounded Wasserstein Object-Relation Distance for 3D Scene Graph Prediction
papers.abstract: 3D scene graph prediction is commonly optimized with object-node and relation-edge classification losses. These objectives encourage exact object and relation label recovery, but they do not directly optimize semantic proximity to the ground-truth scene graph: two wrong graphs can receive comparable penalties even when one is much closer in object roles and relation contexts. A direct graph-distance loss is difficult in general, since graph matching and graph edit distance require correspondence search and edit-cost design. Our key observation is that prior supervised 3D scene graph prediction protocols are conducted on fixed object-node indices and supervised edge slots. This can turn a scene graph comparison into a well-defined aligned graph-distance problem. To this end, we propose SWORD, a Scene-Grounded Wasserstein Object-Relation Distance that builds block-normalized object and relation ground distance metrics from training scene graph annotations through a deterministic base-to-context order, without external semantic priors. SWORD lifts these metrics to Wasserstein distances over aligned node and null-augmented edge marginals, providing semantic graph-distance supervision beyond exact-label penalties while preserving the ground-truth graph as the unique zero-distance solution in aligned marginal probability space. We prove that SWORD is a strict metric on aligned marginal probabilistic scene graphs, preserves scene-graph-grounded substitution ordering, controls additive graph-grounded semantic observables, and yields a surrogate upper-bounding decoded semantic error.

papers.title: VISRA: Vision-Language Induced Supervision and Representation Alignment for Long-Tailed Generalized Category Discovery
papers.abstract: Generalized Category Discovery (GCD) aims to classify unlabeled data containing both known and novel classes, given only labels for known classes. Existing GCD methods typically assume a relatively balanced data distribution, an assumption that breaks down in realistic open-world scenarios. In this paper, we study Long-Tailed Generalized Category Discovery (LT-GCD), where both labeled and unlabeled data follow long-tailed distributions. Under such conditions, training signals are dominated by known categories; this imbalance biases representation learning and weakens novel-category discovery. To address these challenges, we propose VISRA, a semantic-driven framework for LT-GCD built upon a parametric GCD pipeline. Rather than relying solely on distribution debiasing, our framework leverages Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to provide additional semantic supervision for representative novel-class instances and guide visual representation learning. Experimental results on three long-tailed datasets demonstrate that VISRA achieves state-of-the-art performance, effectively alleviating novel-class supervision deficiency and learning more discriminative representations under severe imbalance. Our code and prompt are available at https://github.com/EileanZYZ/VISRA.

papers.title: Asymmetric Privileged Distillation for Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) and vision–language models have introduced richer semantic guidance into Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection (WS-VAD). However, video-dependent text generation or encoding during inference introduces substantial computational overhead and complicates deployment in resource-constrained scenarios. We propose APD-VAD, an Asymmetric Privileged Distillation framework that uses LVLM-generated descriptions as privileged information during training and deploys a visual student without dynamic text processing. A Privileged Language Cascade (PLC) supplies video- and snippet-level descriptions to the teacher, and a Background-Debiased Graph (BDG) attenuates scene-dominated relations before temporal graph reasoning. Semantic-distribution, feature, and topology distillation transfer the resulting class, snippet, and relational knowledge to the student. At inference, a dual-branch visual graph and Visual Prototype Memory (VPM) provide category-aware visual context through cached category prototypes and class-routed visual retrieval. Experiments on UCF-Crime and XD-Violence demonstrate competitive anomaly detection and improved fine-grained temporal localization, while deployment profiling confirms efficient inference without recurring LVLM processing. Code is available at https://github.com/cgao-comp/APD-VAD.

papers.title: FOCAL: Forgery-Centric One-Class Artifact Learning for Out-of-Distribution Deepfake Detection
papers.abstract: Existing deepfake detection methods learn facial representations that capture the identity, semantics, or geometric structure of real faces. We argue that such face-centric representations can introduce identity and semantic biases, encoding appearance attributes that correlate with a person’s identity rather than with the image’s manipulation, thereby limiting transferability to unseen forgery types. We propose Forgery-Centric One-Class Artifact Learning (FOCAL), a representation learning framework that models manipulation artifacts directly rather than generic facial semantics. FOCAL is trained exclusively on forged images: an encoder-decoder reconstructs spatial artifact maps from fake inputs, forcing the encoder to learn where and how manipulation has occurred. This reconstruction objective is complemented by spatial and frequency-domain contrastive losses that encourage invariance to input perturbations while preserving discriminative forgery cues. Because the encoder captures a compact forgery-artifact distribution, real faces unseen during training naturally fall outside. We exploit this property by proposing the Dynamic-Centroid Mahalanobis Distance (DCMD), which enables classifier-free, zero-shot detection with out target-domain adaptation. FOCAL surpasses state-of-the-art methods on standard cross-dataset benchmarks in both detection AUC and pixel-level forgery despite fake-only training. This clearly demonstrates that forgery-centric representations yield transfer- able features than approaches anchored to real-face distributions

papers.title: Closing Generalization Gaps in Continual Face Forgery Detection
papers.abstract: Deepfake manipulations evolve rapidly across digital media platforms, requiring continual detector updates as the distributions of face forgeries shift. Unlike general class-incremental learning, continual face forgery detection is a domain-incremental binary task in which new manipulations of the same fake class are introduced. We demonstrate that existing continual deepfake detectors remain tied to distribution-specific cues, preserving performance on seen datasets while struggling to generalize to unseen manipulation domains. This observation suggests that effective continual adaptation should preserve transferable representations while retaining prior knowledge under sequential domain shifts. We further find that SVD-based parameter-efficient tuning improves transferability but requires regularization against forgetting. Accordingly, we propose TASER, an exemplar-free framework that couples this transferable basis with transport-guided regularization. Asymmetric Class-Wise Partial Optimal Transport (AC-POT) aligns real and fake manifolds separately for class-aware adaptation, while OT-guided Contrastive Separation (OTCon) strengthens the real/fake boundary using transport-selected positives and opposite-class negatives. TASER achieves state-of-the-art intra-dataset retention and cross-dataset generalization, with a final average AUC of 0.9787, a 0.0123 average forgetting AUC, and an overall cross-dataset AUC of 0.8626 across challenging continual face forgery benchmarks.

papers.title: Unveiling Color-induced Emotions latent in Image-Text Expressions from Dual Perceptual Pathways
affiliations: Criminal Investigation Police University of China
papers.abstract: Image-text emotion detection (ITED) aims to identify the emotion expressed by a given pair of text and image. However, existing methods often overlook color, a fundamental visual cue that carries rich emotional information. From the perspective of human cognition, color expressions in images and texts can evoke emotions in both direct and indirect ways. Inspired by this observation, we design a D ynamic E motion S emantic E nhancement F ramework via D ual C olor-induced P athways for the ITED task. Specifically, our framework first builds a direct color-induced emotion (CIE) pathway based on general human color-emotion patterns and an indirect pathway through the generative imagination of color-similar scenes. Such rich CIE knowledge is then parameterized as multiple trainable experts within a mixture-of-CIE-experts module (MoCE) shared across the two modalities. However, as not all the color-induced emotions contribute positively to the final prediction, we design a dynamic expert selection mechanism that allows words in texts or regions in images to adaptively retrieve experts' knowledge consistent with the grounded emotions. Extensive experiments on three ITED datasets under different modality fusion strategies demonstrate the effectiveness, robustness, and generalization ability of the framework.

papers.title: Multimodal Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis via Evidence-Guided Region Calibration
papers.abstract: Multimodal Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (MABSA) aims to identify aspect-level sentiment from user-generated image-text posts. Although visual information can provide useful context for sentiment reasoning, it is not uniformly beneficial for aspect-level prediction. Different image regions may serve distinct roles: some provide content support for post understanding, some offer sentiment-related evidence, while others introduce irrelevant or misleading signals. To address this challenge, we propose VEGA, a MABSA framework that integrates visual evidence construction with evidence-guided region calibration. Specifically, VEGA first leverages a multimodal large language model to construct two complementary types of visual evidence from each image-text pair: content-aware visual evidence and context-aware sentiment evidence. These evidence streams are then used to calibrate region-level visual representations through a dual-support cross-attention mechanism, enabling image regions to contribute according to their roles in content understanding and sentiment inference. Finally, the calibrated visual features are integrated with the original text in a unified encoder-decoder architecture for both multimodal aspect sentiment classification and joint multimodal aspect-sentiment analysis subtasks. Experiments on public benchmarks demonstrate that VEGA consistently outperforms strong task-specific baselines. Further analyses confirm the effectiveness of visual evidence construction and evidence-guided region calibration.

papers.title: ReasonGraph: Graph-Enhanced Reasoning Distillation for Aspect Sentiment Triplet Extraction
papers.abstract: Aspect Sentiment Triplet Extraction (ASTE) aims to extract aspect–opinion–sentiment triplets from review sentences and is a fundamental task in fine-grained sentiment analysis. Recent large language model-based chain-of-thought (CoT) methods improve instruction following and semantic reasoning for ASTE, but their verbose reasoning outputs introduce substantial inference overhead and often lack explicit structural grounding. We propose ReasonGraph, which integrates gold-guided CoT distillation with dependency-graph-based syntactic grounding. The distillation pipeline first trains the model with explicit reasoning chains and final answers, and then shifts to direct answer generation, allowing reasoning ability to be internalized while keeping inference compact. Meanwhile, a GATv2 dependency-graph encoder injects parsed syntactic structures as continuous prefix embeddings, enabling the LLM to adaptively balance syntactic and semantic cues. Experiments on four standard ASTE benchmarks show that ReasonGraph achieves strong performance with significantly faster inference than CoT-based reasoning methods. Further analysis indicates that our method effectively captures complementary semantic and syntactic information and focuses on the most informative cues for triplet extraction. Our code is available at https://github.com/cscsysu/aste-cikm.

papers.title: Boundary and Discourse-Aware Modeling for Dialogue-Level Aspect-Based Sentiment Quadruple Analysis
papers.abstract: Dialogue-level Aspect-based Sentiment Quadruple Analysis (DiaASQ) aims to extract all (target, aspect, opinion, sentiment) quadruples from multi-turn multi-party dialogues, where sentiment elements may be scattered across different speakers and turns. Despite exploiting dialogue structures, existing methods face two fundamental bottlenecks: First, span representations relying on average pooling treat all tokens equally, which inherently dilutes critical boundary cues and introduces semantic ambiguity—especially when boundaries carry sentiment-bearing modifiers. Second, existing methods model dialogue structures at the coarse utterance level, neglecting fine-grained span-pair interactions across turns—crucial for linking scattered sentiment elements. To address these limitations, we propose: (1) Boundary-Aware Bilinear Attention Pooling (BAP), which replaces uniform averaging with boundary-guided attention, using bilinear projections to dynamically weight span tokens based on their relevance to start/end boundaries; (2) Role-aware Dialogue Householder Projection (RDHP), which refines span-pair representations via geometry-aware partial projections, projecting away dialogue-irrelevant directions while preserving sentiment-bearing subspaces. Extensive experiments on Chinese and English DiaASQ benchmarks demonstrate competitive performance, establishing a new state-of-the-art on the English benchmark with substantial gains in cross-turn quadruple extraction.

papers.title: Schema-Driven Structured Information Extraction from Biomedical Literature via Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Named Entity Recognition and Relation Extraction are key Information Extraction tasks that enable the transformation of unstructured text into structured, machine-interpretable knowledge. In the biomedical domain, the extraction process must be guided by semantic constraints and domain knowledge to prevent the introduction of incorrect, inconsistent, or irrelevant information. In this paper, we propose a framework for constrained multi-stage information extraction pipelines guided by biomedical ontologies. The approach relies on the specification of a schema describing the entities, relations, constraints, and semantic dependencies relevant to the target domain. The schema is used to automatically generate a list of context-aware prompts that guide a general-purpose LLM during the extraction process (avoiding specific fine-tuning). The framework further supports mapping to ontology terms, extraction guidelines, and ontology-derived examples to improve extraction consistency and semantic validation. The proposed approach has been integrated into SchemaLink, an intelligent web platform supporting schema specification, prompt generation and execution, ontology-aware mapping, and visualization of extracted entities and relations. Extensive experiments on biomedical information extraction benchmarks show that our approach outperforms existing schema-guided prompt engineering methods by more effectively modeling dependencies between entity and relation extraction tasks, while achieving performance comparable to fine-tuned domain-specific models.

papers.title: Mitigating the Morpheme Tokenization Bottleneck in Agglutinative Languages: A Korean Case Study with Interleave Attention
papers.abstract: Decoder-only language models score text through next-token likelihoods over tokenizer-induced token sequences. This scoring interface becomes unstable when tokenizer segmentation shapes candidate selection or passage relevance scores rather than contextual fit alone. Agglutinative languages expose this problem sharply because morphosyntactic information is densely packed into surface forms. Korean offers a representative agglutinative stress case through particles, endings, compounds, and spacing variation. We propose Interleave Attention, a decoder augmentation that injects morphology-aware auxiliary representations into the scoring path. Prefix-aligned interleaving integrates these representations into a fused causal sequence rather than a separate cross-attention memory. Under matched initialization, continued-pretraining corpus, objective, and scoring interface, Interleave continued pretraining (CPT) produces stable trajectory-level gains over a parameter-matched decoder-only baseline, improving the overall benchmark average by 3.34 points and the context-conditioned average by 7.12 points. Controlled relevance scoring shows improved rank-sensitive scoring under a fixed hard-negative pool, and Korean surface-form stress tests indicate additional Korean-side robustness under surface variation. These results support a bottleneck-mitigation interpretation that separates the general Interleave effect from the morphology-based auxiliary-tokenizer effect.

papers.title: Dynamic Topic Modeling for Cross-Corpus Temporal Analysis
papers.abstract: Dynamic Embedded Topic Models (D-ETM) provide an interpretable framework for modeling temporal semantic evolution, but cross-corpus comparison remains difficult because topics are often learned independently and aligned only after training, a process that does not guarantee stable topic correspondence across corpora and time. To address this problem, we propose a D-ETM framework that first learns a common dynamic topic space over a merged multi-corpus collection, which we call the shared backbone, then introduces corpus-specific residual adaptation around the frozen backbone without creating separate latent topic spaces. This design preserves a shared topic index for cross-corpus comparison while allowing each corpus to specialize lexically. We evaluate the framework on three temporally structured corpora spanning 97 years: the Corpus of Historical American English, Harvard Business Review, and International Labour Review. Residual adaptation improves corpus-specific fit relative to the shared backbone while preserving the same-index cross-corpus topic trajectories, achieving substantially stronger alignment than full fine-tuning from the same backbone, with (97.5 ± 0.7%) versus (17.9 ± 1.1%) trajectory Retrieval@1, as well as stronger alignment than independent training with post-hoc Hungarian matching. These results suggest that incorporating topic alignment into the model can support more stable over-time cross-corpus comparisons while retaining corpus-specific lexical variation.

papers.title: Seeing is Deciding: Evidence-Based Parallel Probing for LLM-based Web Agents
papers.abstract: Autonomous agents powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) can automate complex web tasks, but their reliability is limited by uncertain action outcomes: the consequence of interacting with a web element is often known only after execution. Existing sequential methods are vulnerable to error propagation after wrong decisions, while tree-search approaches rely on speculative pre-execution scoring and incur substantial exploration cost. We introduce WebTactix, an evidence-based parallel probing framework that shifts web navigation from speculative prediction to grounded decision making. Rather than scoring actions before execution, WebTactix executes multiple candidate plans in parallel, observes their successor pages, and compares the resulting evidence to select the next branch while accounting for future continuation. This design enables the agent to explore multiple alternatives without committing prematurely to uncertain decisions or incurring the overhead of extensive tree search. Experiments on WebArena and Online-Mind2Web demonstrate consistent improvements in both task success and efficiency, with WebTactix achieving 76.8% success on WebArena while reducing average completion time by 56.2% relative to the strongest tree-search baseline.

papers.title: Co-JDPRec: Collaborative Joint Dynamic Pruning for Efficient LLM-based Generative Recommendation
papers.abstract: Generative recommendation leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to model item semantics and user preference dynamics through sequence-to-token generation, but deep Transformer layers and wide Feed Forward Network (FFN) dimensions introduce substantial memory and latency overhead in online recommendation scenarios. Existing LLM pruning methods are mainly designed to preserve general language modeling ability, often overlooking the recommendation-specific states shaped by item semantics, collaborative signals, and temporal preference dynamics. To address this limitation, we propose Co-JDPRec, a collaborative joint dynamic pruning framework that shifts the pruning objective from parameter removal to recommendation-state preservation. Specifically, Co-JDPRec introduces a task-aware saliency criterion that combines collaborative alignment and sequence-order sensitivity, enabling the model to identify neurons critical for user-item relations and evolving preference dynamics. Guided by this saliency, Co-JDPRec jointly searches FFN width and layer depth to derive a compact heterogeneous architecture, followed by distillation recovery to restore recommendation performance. Theoretically, Co-JDPRec characterizes structural importance via first-order Taylor sensitivity under recommendation-aware objectives. Empirically, it achieves superior accuracy–efficiency trade-offs on both title-based and semantic-ID-based generative recommendation backbones, validating the effectiveness of recommendation-state-aware pruning.

papers.title: MISTRec: Masked Item-Slot Token Modeling for LLM-based Generative Recommendation
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently been explored for generative recommendation, where item tokenization plays a critical role. Existing studies design item identifiers such as discrete Semantic IDs, single-token identifiers, and multi-token or set identifiers. However, in many identifier-based methods, the item-level grounding of these introduced identifiers is not established during general-domain pre-training and must instead be learned during recommendation-specific adaptation. Consequently, LLMs may treat them as opaque prediction symbols rather than stable item representations. To address this issue, we propose MISTRec, a masked item-slot modeling framework for learning structured continuous item representations. MISTRec introduces three key designs. First, MISTRec decomposes each item into continuous CF-aware and latent semantic slots, reducing the entanglement between collaborative signals and metadata-derived item semantics. Second, it trains these slots with Masked Slot Autoencoding (MSA) by reconstructing corrupted historical slots and completing a fully masked future item. Third, it introduces False Negative Reweighting (FNR), which downweights semantically conflicting negatives during target alignment and improves the stability of full-catalog ranking. Experiments on three public benchmarks show that MISTRec consistently improves next-item recommendation over strong sequential and generative baselines, while yielding more stable item neighborhoods across random seeds.

papers.title: Rethinking Item Tokenization in Generative Recommenders: From Fixed Atoms to Semantic Subwords
affiliations: University of Science and Technology of China
papers.abstract: In generative recommender systems, items are typically tokenized into fixed-length semantic ID sequences for autoregressive next-item prediction. However, for user-context modeling, this fine-grained representation triggers Intra-item Attention Overload : excessive attention is spent on low-level intra-item dependencies rather than high-level inter-item behavioral transitions. To address this, we propose Semantic Subword Tokenization (SST) , which represents historical items as variable-length semantic subwords while preserving fixed-length target decoding. SST first applies Item-level Subword Tokenization (IST) to merge stable adjacent atom tokens into compact semantic subword tokens , thereby reducing intra-item reassembly in the encoder. It then introduces Behavior-induced Co-occurrence Augmentation (BCA) to inject coarse-grained semantic prefix transition signals, guiding the freed modeling capacity toward inter-item behavioral regularities. Extensive experiments on three public datasets and three generative recommender backbones show empirical improvements of SST over fixed-length and transferable variable-length SID baselines. Code is available at https://github.com/mxrcandy/Semantic-Subword-Tokenization.

papers.title: Beyond Uniform Token Training: A Multi-Target Framework for Learning Token-Weighted Objectives in Generative Recommenders
papers.abstract: Recent generative recommendation models recast next-item prediction as the generation of a semantic identifier sequence. While this formulation enables autoregressive models to produce item IDs directly, the commonly used token-level likelihood objective does not distinguish between tokens that play different roles in item identification. This limitation is especially pronounced for semantic-ID representations, where prefix tokens often determine coarse item groups and later tokens provide finer-grained disambiguation. To better align training with the structure of semantic IDs, we study token-level learning signals from two complementary perspectives. First, we introduce a prefix-aware weighting scheme, Front-Greater Weighting, which emphasizes tokens according to their contribution to reducing semantic ambiguity among candidate items. Second, frequency weighting increases the learning emphasis on infrequent tokens, addressing the long-tailed distributions and popularity bias commonly observed in recommendation data. We further introduce a multi-target optimization framework with curriculum learning, which integrates the two token-weighted objectives with the standard likelihood and enables stable optimization with adaptive emphasis across training stages. Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently improves generative recommendation performance over strong baselines and prior token-weighting methods. Additional analyses show that the method is robust across different semantic-ID constructions and backbone scales, and that it improves recommendation quality for both popular and long-tail items. Code is available at github repository.

papers.title: Learning to Reflect and Correct: Towards Better Decoding Trajectories for Large-Scale Generative Recommendation
affiliations: Wuhan University, School of Computer Science
papers.abstract: Generative Recommendation (GR) has become a promising paradigm for large-scale recommendation systems, yet existing GR models typically perform single-pass decoding without explicit refinement, causing early deviations to accumulate and degrade recommendation quality. Recent work mitigates this via two reasoning paradigms: reason-then-generate , which refines intermediate states before producing the draft, and reason-while-generating , which interleaves reasoning with token generation. Both, however, reason before a complete draft exists and cannot diagnose or revise a finalized Semantic-ID (SID) trajectory. To this end, we propose GRC, to our knowledge the first structured reflection–correction paradigm for GR that performs reasoning on a complete draft via a G eneration– R eflection– C orrection process. GRC introduces a supervised reflection-correction template with multi-granular reflection labels in the SID space, and further optimizes the GRC trajectory via GRPO-based reinforcement learning with tailored rewards that jointly evaluate correction quality and reflection accuracy. For efficient online serving, we propose an Entropy-Guided Reflection Scheduling (EGRS) strategy that prioritizes high-uncertainty trajectories for correction under a fixed beam budget. Extensive experiments show that GRC consistently outperforms eight state-of-the-art baselines by up to 13.33%, and online A/B tests demonstrate its substantial practical value in large-scale industrial recommendation, delivering a 1.39% lift in advertising revenue with only modest latency overhead.

papers.title: RQ-Reg: A Residual-Quantization-Based Framework for Continuous Value Prediction in Recommender Systems
papers.abstract: Predicting continuous values such as watch-time and gross merchandise value (GMV) is a core problem in industrial recommendation systems. Its inherent difficulty stems from the highly complex and long-tailed distributions of the target signals, which are hard to model accurately. Existing regression methods typically rely on fixed parametric assumptions on the target distribution: overly simple assumptions underfit real-world data, whereas more intricate ones tend to sacrifice scalability and generalization. To address these limitations, we propose a sequence modeling framework based on residual quantization (RQ), in which the target continuous value is decomposed into a sequence of quantization codes that represent progressively finer approximations. The model autoregressively predicts these codes from coarse to fine granularity, with each step refining the residual error left by the previous one. To further improve the quality of the learned representations, we introduce an ordinal-aware representation learning objective that aligns the RQ code embedding space with the ordinal structure of target values, thereby yielding continuous representations of quantization codes and more accurate predictions. We conduct comprehensive experiments on public benchmarks for watch-time and lifetime value (LTV) prediction, together with a large-scale online A/B test for GMV prediction on an industrial short-video recommendation platform. Across all settings, the proposed method shows competitive performance among existing state-of-the-art approaches and generalizes well across diverse continuous value prediction scenarios.

papers.title: FAF: A Feature-Aware Adaptive Pre-training Framework for Bridging Gaps in CTR Prediction
affiliations: University of Science and Technology of China
papers.abstract: Self-supervised pre-training has emerged as an effective solution to data sparsity in Click-Through Rate (CTR) prediction. However, existing paradigms still face two critical limitations: (1) task degeneration in pre-training, where heuristic or random target construction may lead to trivial shortcuts; and (2) limited adaptivity in fine-tuning, where static transfer strategies fail to accommodate optimization heterogeneity across diverse feature fields and ID frequencies. To address these issues, we propose the F eature-aware A daptive pre-training and fine-tuning F ramework (FAF). The core of FAF lies in two coupled designs. First, we improve pre-training target construction from both token and feature levels. At the token level, we introduce a position-decayed future item prediction task to incorporate additional future behavior supervision while reducing the influence of noisy distant targets. At the feature level, we formulate masked feature selection as a combinatorial optimization problem and derive an entropy-redundancy scoring criterion, which selects informative target fields with low contextual redundancy to construct non-trivial reconstruction tasks. Second, we design an adaptive fine-tuning strategy that combines field-aware and item frequency-aware update regulation. This strategy dynamically adjusts embedding update magnitudes across heterogeneous feature fields and item frequencies, improving the compatibility between pre-trained representations and downstream task adaptation. Extensive experiments on three real-world datasets show that FAF brings consistent overall performance gains over strong baselines across multiple backbone models, demonstrating its effectiveness in representation learning and compatible knowledge transfer.

papers.title: FC-GNN: Unleashing Field Priors for Graph-based CTR Prediction
affiliations: Huazhong University of Science and Technology
papers.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have been adopted for click-through rate (CTR) prediction to explicitly capture and model feature interactions. However, existing graph evolution approaches with separate structural inference and feature aggregation face two key challenges in recommendation scenarios. On the one hand, recursively updated structural representations can suffer from degraded edge discriminability during graph evolution, destabilizing high-order topology learning. On the other hand, heterogeneous feature fields make conventional message passing prone to semantic misalignment. Consequently, the learned topology may not align with the semantic requirements of subsequent message propagation. In this paper, we propose Field-aware Compositional GNN (FC-GNN), which exploits field semantics as a dual-role inductive bias to stabilize graph learning. At the structure level, we introduce a Field Prior Matrix as a field-conditioned interaction operator, reducing the dependence of edge discrimination on feature representations. At the node level, we establish Field Semantic Anchors as shared semantic coordinates and employ a field-conditioned gating mechanism to calibrate heterogeneous feature representations before message passing. Moreover, we reuse the same field prior matrix during aggregation to form a feedback bridge between structure inference and semantic propagation. Experimental results on three public datasets demonstrate that FC-GNN consistently outperforms existing methods.

papers.title: Hard but Not Too Hard: Semi-Hard Negative Sampling for Implicit Collaborative Filtering
papers.abstract: Negative sampling plays a pivotal role in implicit feedback-based collaborative filtering (CF) models optimized with pairwise ranking loss, as these models must learn to rank preferred items higher than non-preferred ones. As simply treating all unobserved interactions as negative samples may degrade model accuracy, previous studies have explored various negative sampling strategies, such as static and hard negative sampling, to select more informative negative samples. However, static negative sampling methods often fail to select informative samples because they do not account for training dynamics or the structure of user preferences, whereas hard negative sampling methods suffer from the false negative problem and may therefore introduce incorrect training signals. To address these limitations and provide a theoretical solution to the negative sampling problem, we conduct an in-depth analysis of implicit CF under the Bayesian Personalized Ranking loss. As a result, we find that sampling highly preferred items as negatives degrades recommendation performance, whereas more frequently sampling moderately preferred items improves it. Based on these findings, we propose Semi-Hard Negative Sampling (SHNS), a novel negative sampling method for implicit CF that selects moderately difficult negative samples while dynamically annealing the sampling difficulty to mitigate the risk of false negatives. Extensive experimental results show that SHNS achieves superior performance compared with 10 state-of-the-art negative sampling methods. Further empirical analysis demonstrates that SHNS effectively mitigates the false negative problem while maintaining the ability to select informative negative samples.

papers.title: Dual-Tree LLM-Enhanced Negative Sampling for Implicit Collaborative Filtering
papers.abstract: Negative sampling is a pivotal technique in implicit collaborative filtering (CF), enabling efficient and effective training by contrasting observed interactions with sampled unobserved ones. Recently, large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in recommender systems, yet their use in negative sampling remains underexplored. Existing methods often rely on textual information and task-specific fine-tuning, which may limit their applicability in settings with scarce textual metadata or constrained computational resources. To this end, we propose a text-free and fine-tuning-free D ual- T ree L LM-enhanced N egative S ampling method (DTL-NS). It consists of two modules: (i) an offline false negative identification module that leverages hierarchical index trees to transform collaborative structural and latent semantic information into structured item-ID encodings for LLM inference, enabling accurate identification of false negatives; and (ii) a multi-view hard negative sampling module that combines user–item preference scores with item–item hierarchical similarities from these encodings to mine high-quality negatives, thus improving models’ discriminative ability. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DTL-NS consistently improves recommendation performance across different implicit CF models, negative sampling methods, and LLMs.

papers.title: Do All Nodes Benefit Equally from Knowledge Graphs? Adaptive Node-Aware KG Fusion for Recommendation
papers.abstract: KG-aware recommendation has been widely studied to alleviate data sparsity by using knowledge graphs (KGs), which represent items, entities, and their relations as graphs and provide item-side knowledge. However, existing methods incorporate item knowledge without considering how much each user or item node should rely on it. As a result, they apply KG signals indiscriminately across nodes, even to nodes whose collaborative filtering (CF) signals from the interaction graph (IG) are already reliable. In this paper, we propose AdaKG (Adaptive Node-Aware KG Fusion), a novel KG-aware recommendation method that adaptively adjusts the contribution of auxiliary knowledge for each node. Since user-item interactions and item knowledge provide different types of signals, directly mixing them can distort the CF signals. To avoid this, AdaKG separately encodes the IG and KG with view-specific encoders, allowing each view to capture its own information. It then estimates how strongly each node should rely on item knowledge by measuring the stability of its CF signals under small adversarial perturbations, assigning a larger KG contribution to less stable nodes. Finally, AdaKG adaptively aligns the IG and KG embeddings in a shared space and fuses them according to the estimated node-wise reliance. Through experiments, we show that AdaKG achieves strong performance compared with its baselines and the effectiveness of our adaptive fusion strategy.

papers.title: SocialKAN: Learning User Preferences on Signed Social Graphs with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
papers.abstract: User-user social networks are widely utilized as side information in recommendation and have been shown to improve performance. We argue that current social recommenders still have room for improvement. First, for social data utilization, most methods focus mainly on positive trust relations, while failing to effectively use negative distrust relations, which can also provide useful signals for recommendation. Second, in terms of modeling architecture, most methods rely on linear or nonlinear transformation structures (e.g., multi-layer perceptrons) as their foundational building blocks. Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs), recently introduced for their strong data-fitting ability, offer a promising alternative. To this end, in this paper, we propose SocialKAN, a novel KAN-based trust-distrust-aware social recommender method. Specifically, SocialKAN introduces three KAN-based graph learning channels to model the user-item interaction graph, user trust graph, and user distrust graph, respectively. To better enable effective cross-view adaptation among the three channels, we design a semantic routing module for knowledge sharing at the embedding level and an adaptive consensus knowledge distillation strategy for output alignment at the optimization level. Experimental results on the three datasets show that our proposed SocialKAN method achieves strong performance. Ablation studies further validate the rationality and effectiveness of the components designed in our SocialKAN.

papers.title: KG-ARMM: Residual Structural Fusion for Graph-Augmented Personalized Retrieval
papers.abstract: Dense multimodal retrieval scales well, but it can miss relational evidence from user histories, item neighborhoods, and domain entities. We present KG-ARMM, a retrieval-compatible Residual Structural Fusion (RSF) framework. A text-and-poster backbone supports approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) candidate generation; an offline item graph and filtered knowledge graph (KG) supply evidence to a lightweight pairwise re-ranker. The primary configuration gives the learned score limited authority, combining it with normalized structural support, a popularity penalty, and a long-tail bonus. On a temporal MovieLens–The Movie Database (TMDB) benchmark evaluated against the full catalog, the balanced variant improves normalized discounted cumulative gain at 20 (NDCG@20) by 8.3% (0.04273 to 0.04628) and Recall@20 by 7.0% (0.09968 to 0.10666) over the multimodal backbone. A matched full-scale control without graph/KG features or the direct structural term reaches 0.04405 NDCG@20 and 0.10336 Recall@20; complete-model paired gains remain positive with 95% intervals [0.00205, 0.00241] and [0.00285, 0.00375], respectively. KGSupport@20 rises from 0.2704 in that control to 0.3128, with stable catalog behavior. Sparse-history users gain most, and validation-holdout ablations favor the filtered relation bundle. Unrestricted learned-score authority yields higher accuracy but collapses long-tail exposure. These results support structural evidence as a sparse, auditable correction layer over dense multimodal retrieval rather than as an unconstrained replacement for the base ranking signal.

papers.title: BRIDGE: Behavior-Guided Residual Integration with Dual-Frequency Graph Evidence
affiliations: University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract: Multimodal recommendation improves item representations by combining visual, textual, and collaborative signals, but stronger cross-view alignment does not always improve ranking. Our diagnostics on Amazon Baby show that direct consistency has an effective range: moderate alignment helps, while stronger alignment suppresses recommendation-specific variation. We also observe a clear spectral split: low-frequency components capture shared structure, whereas higher-frequency components retain more private ranking signal. Based on these findings, we propose BRIDGE, a behavior-guided residual integration framework built on dual-frequency graph evidence. BRIDGE separates the model into three parts: DFGE decomposes graph-smoothed ID, visual, and textual channels into spectral bands; BEN converts training-only co-user overlap into signed candidate evidence; and CRI applies that evidence only inside the base top-K candidate set during training and inference. This design keeps the multimodal backbone and localizes behavior evidence to candidate calibration. Experiments on Amazon Baby, Sports, and Electronics show that BRIDGE reaches 0.1128/0.1262/0.0778 Recall@20 and 0.0525/0.0594/0.0385 NDCG@20, outperforming baselines by up to 7.3% in Recall@20 and 14.9% in NDCG@20. Project materials are available at https://lizesheng13.github.io/bridge/.

papers.title: Information-Guided Selective Modality Alignment for Multimodal Recommendation
papers.abstract: Multimodal recommendation (MMRec) aims to enhance recommendation performance by leveraging rich item content from multiple modalities. However, directly incorporating all modality information does not necessarily lead to better preference modeling, since user interests are often more related to a subset of modality signals, while other signals may be weakly aligned with user preferences or even introduce noise. Although recent MMRec methods improve modality utilization through invariant learning, attention mechanisms, graph refinement, or contrastive learning, their alignment processes are often implicit or heuristic and lack a clear objective for selecting modality signals that better match user interests. In this paper, we propose AMUR, an information-guided selective modality-interest alignment framework for multimodal recommendation. Inspired by an information-theoretic view, AMUR aims to enhance modality information that is more related to user interests while reducing the influence of less aligned signals. Specifically, AMUR first refines modality graph structures towards user behavior, and then selectively aligns shared interest-related semantics across modalities. This enables AMUR to improve modality-interest alignment while preserving useful modality-specific complementary information. Extensive experiments on three real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of AMUR over competitive baselines. The codes are available here. (https://github.com/Wenze1/AMUR)

papers.title: ViSalRec: Visual and Saliency-Informed Reward Augmentation for Sequential Recommender Systems
papers.abstract: In Reinforcement Learning (RL)-based sequential recommendation, offline training often reduces user feedback to sparse binary rewards, weakening credit assignment and limiting policy optimisation. In visual recommendation settings, user choices are also shaped by product appearance, visual attention, and semantic impressions, which provide preference cues that binary outcomes cannot capture. However, how to transform such visual cues into reward supervision and how they impact recommendation performance remains underexplored. Therefore, we introduce ViSalRec, a unified visual-feedback reward augmentation framework for offline RL-based recommendation. ViSalRec treats visual preference cues as an additional reward layer that transforms item image, predicted saliency maps, and multimodal Large Language Model (LLM) judgements into dense reward signals, instantiated as saliency-based rewards, visually-conditioned LLM likeability rewards, and history-conditioned LLM purchase rewards. Within SA2C-style actor–critic recommenders, we study how these reward formulations interact with data characteristics, sequence encoders, and advantage-estimation strategies. Experiments on Amazon Review variants show that visual reward augmentation can improve recommendation performance, but its effectiveness depends on the proxy signal, data density, and reward-integration strategy. Overall, LLM-mediated and history-aware rewards are more reliable than raw saliency rewards, especially under denser data and value-based training. These findings provide an account of when visual preference feedback improves offline RL-based recommendation and how such rewards can be designed and integrated.

papers.title: Next Token Prediction for Generalizable Human Activity Recognition
affiliations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)
Singapore-MIT Alliance for Research and Technology
papers.abstract: One major challenge of sensor-based Human Activity Recognition (HAR) is data heterogeneity, where domain shifts between training and testing data could significantly degrade recognition performance. Recently, large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong cross-domain generalization capabilities by modeling language with next-token prediction, offering a promising paradigm for mitigating domain shifts in HAR. In this paper, we propose NextHAR, a novel self-supervised sensor pretraining framework for generalizable HAR. NextHAR first tokenizes sensor data in the frequency space, converting them into motion-semantic tokens. Then, to learn human motion dynamics, NextHAR jointly models inter-channel correlations and temporal dependencies by predicting the next sensor token groups. Furthermore, we introduce a comprehensive cross-domain HAR benchmark to enable systematic evaluation. Extensive experiments on this benchmark show that NextHAR outperforms state-of-the-art methods by 13.83% in accuracy and 15.00% in F1-score. Moreover, NextHAR achieves an average inference latency of 0.033 seconds on wearable devices, highlighting its efficiency for real-world applications. Our code and organized benchmark are publicly available at https://github.com/saiketa/NextHAR.

papers.title: Exploring Semantics-Frequency Alignment in Diffusion Transformers for Financial Time Series Generation
affiliations: China Electronics Cloud Tech Co., Ltd
industryAffiliations: China Electronics Cloud Tech Co., Ltd
papers.abstract: Existing financial time series generation (FTSG) approaches predominantly model unconditional distributions, lacking the semantic controllability required to simulate deliberate market dynamics, such as macroeconomic shifts and geopolitical shocks. To bridge this gap, this paper studies text-conditioned FTSG that synthesizes realistic multivariate price sequences guided by natural language market descriptions. We propose Fin-CoDiT , a novel diffusion transformer framework engineered around a profound architectural inductive bias: the structural isomorphism between the hierarchical semantic depth of large language models (LLMs) and the spectral frequencies of time-series signals. To exploit this, Fin-CoDiT introduces a Semantics-Frequency Alignment mechanism via Grouped Routing Attention , which dynamically routes explicit LLM layers to their targeted frequency bands during the denoising process. To encode cross-variable dependencies of time series without violating the temporal arrow, we propose Time-Frequency Causal Variational Autoencoder , which strictly operates as a channel-wise bottleneck equipped with orthogonal causal convolutions to fundamentally eliminate future information leakage. Furthermore, it incorporates a branched decoder with in-network differentiable morphological projections, guaranteeing absolute physical market constraints (e.g., Price high ≥ Price low ). For the training and evaluation of this novel paradigm, we construct an automated multi-agent workflow that creates high-quality text-time series pairs from real-world market states spanning January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2025. Extensive experiments on treasury futures and ETFs demonstrate that Fin-CoDiT establishes a new state-of-the-art, significantly outperforming existing baselines in both generation fidelity and controllability.

papers.title: UPLOTS: A Unified Pretrained Language Model for Constrained Time-series Generation
affiliations: The University of New South Wales
The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology Guangzhou (HKUST-GZ)
The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
papers.abstract: Many time-series generation studies train a separate generator for each dataset. We study a complementary setting in which one shared, channel-independent generator is trained on several timestamp-derived scenario pools and a compact textual prompt selects the desired pool at inference. We propose UPLOTS, a U nified, P rompt-guided L anguage model framework f O r constrained T ime- S eries generation. UPLOTS combines a Diffusion-TS generator with a truncated pretrained language-model backbone, a Time-series Prompt Embedding Module, and two multi-dataset balancing mechanisms: Curriculum-Aware Loss Modulation and Rolling-Loss Dynamic Sampling. We evaluate four real-world datasets under morning- and evening-peak scenarios and extend the analysis to 14 prompt configurations on ETTh and Energy, covering temporal, calendar, load-level, and volatility subsets. The results support unified, in-distribution generation for the predefined datasets and scenario prompts. Downstream forecasting experiments further assess the utility of the generated samples for data augmentation. Our code is available at https://github.com/cruiseresearchgroup/UPLOTS.

papers.title: Beyond Node-Level Relations: Hybrid Hierarchical Graphs for Multivariate Time Series Imputation under Node Blackout
papers.abstract: Missing data imputation in multivariate time series (MTS) becomes particularly challenging when an entire target node is unobserved throughout an input window, a setting we refer to as node blackout . This setting arises in both spatiotemporal sensing datasets and more general MTS benchmarks, where a node denotes the basic relational unit and may correspond to either a physical sensor stream or a feature/variable channel. Existing methods increasingly exploit inter-variable dependencies through graph structures or attention-based interactions, but most still depend primarily on flat node-level support. Such support becomes fragile when blackout targets have weak local relations or when multiple blackout nodes occur within the same local region, making immediate neighborhoods insufficient or ambiguous for reconstruction. To address this issue, we propose HHGI, a H ybrid H ierarchical G raph learning framework for MTS I mputation under node blackout. HHGI preserves a sparse local graph as a stable structural prior while introducing a higher-level support graph over subgraphs. The higher-level support graph is constructed from two complementary views: inherited topology, which preserves topology-consistent support from the local graph, and subgraph similarity, which retrieves support from structurally compatible local subsystems beyond immediate node-level neighborhoods. To make this higher-level support adaptive to each input window, we construct it from temporal representations and stabilize subgraph formation with shared node priors. We further introduce a missingness-aware adaptive fusion mechanism that balances local and hierarchical supports according to node missing ratio and local-support reliability. Experiments on five real-world MTS datasets demonstrate strong and consistent performance of HHGI across both explicit spatial settings and general multivariate benchmarks under node blackout. Our code is available at https://github.com/jhBae00/H2GI.

papers.title: ViCO: Vision-Augmented Time Series Anomaly Detection with Prototype-Guided Coordination
affiliations: Hong Kong Institute of Science & Innovation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract: Time series anomaly detection aims to identify time points or intervals that deviate from normal temporal behavior. In reconstruction-based detection, this requires errors that distinguish anomalies rather than merely accurate reconstruction. However, most existing methods rely solely on temporal modeling, while vision-augmented approaches focus primarily on forecasting, leaving the potential of structural visual cues for reconstruction-based detection underexplored. Moreover, bridging temporal and visual representations further remains challenging. To address these challenges, we propose a Vision-Augmented Coordination framework for time series anomaly detection, called ViCO. A decoupled visual teacher and temporal student characterize normal behavior from complementary views: tri-view visual representations capture structural regularities, whereas raw sequences model value-sensitive dynamics. Prototype-Guided Coordination retrieves normal structural prototypes and conditions the temporal decoder, translating visual structure into reconstruction guidance for anomaly scoring. Extensive experiments on five real-world datasets demonstrate that ViCO consistently outperforms strong baselines by up to 9.0%, while enabling teacher-free inference for lightweight deployment. Code is available at https://github.com/Cedarrr1/ViCO.

papers.title: OpenTAD: Detecting Open Set Anomalous Trajectory with Memory-Enhanced Distribution Drift Learning
affiliations: Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences
Institute of Computing Technology,Chinese Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract: Detecting emerging anomalous trajectories of unseen types is a critical yet challenging problem for applications such as urban planning, traffic management, and public safety. Existing methods often rely on closed-set assumptions, i.e., they either assume all anomaly types are known or detect anomalous trajectories without using anomaly labels, limiting their ability to detect novel, unseen anomalies. In this paper, we propose OpenTAD, an open-set trajectory anomaly detection framework for identifying anomalous trajectories of both seen and unseen anomaly types. A pseudo-anomaly generation strategy is introduced to address label scarcity by enriching the anomaly manifold, enabling OpenTAD to learn compact normal boundaries even with limited anomaly samples. To tackle spatio-temporal complexity, a memory-augmented trajectory encoding module is designed to capture high-order spatio-temporal dependencies under complex dynamics. Moreover, OpenTAD leverages distribution shift learning to handle anomaly uncertainty by maximizing the separation between normal and anomalous distributions in the latent space, ensuring reliable detection of unseen anomalies. Extensive experiments on multiple real-world trajectory datasets with both synthetic and real anomalies demonstrate that OpenTAD outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving an 8.88% improvement in detecting novel anomalies.

papers.title: OSTAR: Online Anomalous Sub-trajectory Detection via Topology-Aware Autoregressive Reasoning
affiliations: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China
papers.abstract: Online anomalous sub-trajectory detection is a core technology for applications such as real-time traffic monitoring and fraud prevention. Existing methods primarily suffer from three key limitations: 1) weak capability in fine-grained anomaly localization, 2) insufficient constraints regarding road network topology, and 3) difficulties in interpreting the spatiotemporal physical logic of anomalous behaviors. To address these issues, we propose OSTAR, an online generative framework for anomalous sub-trajectory detection driven by topology-aware autoregressive reasoning. Specifically, OSTAR first utilizes a macro-micro-aware perception module to capture local movement dynamics.
