papers.abstract: Multivariate time-series models achieve strong predictive performance in healthcare, industry, energy, and finance, but how they combine cross-variable interactions with temporal dynamics remains unclear. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) has been widely used for interpretation. However, existing time-series variants typically treat the feature and time axes independently, fragmenting structural signals formed jointly by multiple variables over specific intervals. We propose GroupSegment-SHAP (GS-SHAP), which constructs explanatory units as group-segment players based on cross-variable dependence and distribution shifts over time, and then quantifies each unit's contribution via Shapley attribution. We evaluated GS-SHAP across four real-world domains: human activity recognition, power-system forecasting, medical signal analysis, and financial time series, and compared it with KernelSHAP, TimeSHAP, SequenceSHAP, WindowSHAP, and TSHAP. GS-SHAP consistently achieves the highest deletion-based faithfulness (ΔAUC) across all four benchmark datasets. In synthetic evaluations with controlled ground-truth structures, GS-SHAP achieves 24.4% higher IoU-based recovery of multivariate-temporal patterns than the strongest baseline. In addition, GS-SHAP runs on average 3.38x faster than TimeSHAP across approximation budgets in power-system forecasting, showing that it can simultaneously achieve high explanatory faithfulness and computational efficiency. In a financial case study, GS-SHAP identifies interpretable multivariate-temporal interactions among key market variables across market regimes, highlighting its potential utility for risk-aware investment analysis. Code is available at https://github.com/jirungx/GroupSegment-SHAP.

papers.title: Curvature-Regularized Graph Autoencoders with Rewiring for Node-Level Graph Anomaly Detection
affiliations: Huazhong University of Science and Technology
papers.abstract: Graph anomaly detection aims to identify nodes whose structural or relational patterns deviate from the norm. While autoencoder-based methods are widely used, reconstruction error on adjacency and node features may become unreliable if the graph exhibits large geometric curvature. In this work, we propose a curvature-regularized, plug-and-play enhancement to graph autoencoders for node-level anomaly detection. Our key idea is to encourage a near-flat latent geometry for normal regions by incorporating a curvature reconstruction penalty into the training objective. Furthermore, we present a novel curvature-based positional encoding mechanism for Graph Transformers, which encodes local topological information directly into the attention layers as node-wise geometric priors. We also introduce a curvature-guided rewiring step as preprocessing, which improves geometric consistency and enables reliable curvature regularization. Anomalous nodes are then identified through their curvature deviations, together with standard reconstruction signals. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent performance improvements over strong baselines. In particular, applying our geometry-aware preprocessing and curvature penalty directly to the classical DOMINANT model already yields state-of-the-art results. Our code is available at https://github.com/TechnologyAiGroup/crgad.

papers.title: Towards Decoupled Contrastive Learning with Neighborhood Enhancement for Graph Anomaly Detection
affiliations: Shenzhen Academy of Inspection and Quarantine
papers.abstract: Unsupervised graph anomaly detection (UGAD) is crucial to identify anomalous behavior in graph-structured data. Most existing methods rely on contrastive learning, typically adopting node-subgraph and node-node contrastive paradigms. However, anomalous nodes can interfere with local neighborhood modeling, compromising node-subgraph contrast. Moreover, the training of these two paradigms is often coupled, which limits their ability to fully capture node-level anomaly cues. To address these limitations, we propose DeSEN, a novel two-stage UGAD learning framework that decouples the two contrastive learning paradigms. In Stage 1, we introduce a structural-semantic neighborhood enhancement strategy based on biased views to suppress anomalous interference during neighborhood modeling. In Stage 2, we leverage the confident node sets constructed by affinity ranking in Stage 1 to guide node-node contrast, thereby providing effective global node-level anomaly signals. Extensive experiments on eight real-world benchmark datasets, including a large-scale Open Graph Benchmark (OGB) dataset, against ten state-of-the-art baselines show that DeSEN significantly improves both AUROC and AUPRC, while the training and inference pipeline completes within a few minutes. These results validate the effectiveness and efficiency of DeSEN.

papers.title: RoleMine: Mining Behavioral Patterns in Heterogeneous Call Graphs
papers.abstract: Large event graphs often contain rich edge attributes that describe how interactions occur. In call graphs, such attributes include response codes, durations, delays, and inter-arrival times, which are crucial for detecting suspicious entities. However, node-level anomaly detection remains challenging because anomaly labels are rarely available, normal behavior is highly heterogeneous, and operators require interpretable evidence. In this paper, we propose RoleMine, an unsupervised probabilistic framework for node-level anomaly detection in heterogeneous attributed call graphs. RoleMine has three key properties. (a) Accurate: it models role-dependent predictive distributions over heterogeneous edge attributes without anomaly labels. (b) Scalable: it uses observed-edge inference with linear training cost in the number of observed edges. (c) Explainable: it represents nodes by behavioral roles and explains anomalies through communication contexts and attribute-level deviations. Experiments on large real-world daily call graphs show that RoleMine achieves pAUC above 0.995, improves average precision by up to 2.8× over the strongest baseline, and scales linearly, easily handling 34.3M edges in our experiments.

papers.title: TASD: Temporal Adaptive Semantic Decomposition for Task-only Blockchain Graph Fraud Detection
papers.abstract: Blockchain fraud detection plays a critical role in online risk-control services. Constructing temporal blockchain graphs captures evolving interactions, entity behaviors, and risk propagation under causal deployment constraints. However, task-only snapshots make history-dependent temporal graph methods difficult to apply, especially when sparse fraud labels require stable fraud-discriminative semantics across evolving patterns. To fill this gap, we propose TASD, a Temporal Adaptive Semantic Decomposition framework for task-only temporal graph learning in blockchain fraud detection. In particular, TASD introduces four designs: 1) normal and abnormal semantic decomposition with alpha-guided routing for risk-aware aggregation; 2) subspace-stratified Fisher constraints to stabilize semantic parameters across time-ordered snapshots; 3) compact Gaussian prototypes to preserve historical normal and abnormal semantic distributions without historical graph replay; and 4) confidence-guided semantic distillation from the previous snapshot model to transfer reliable temporal semantic knowledge. Experimental results on Elliptic and Elliptic++ Actor demonstrate that TASD improves AUC-ROC by 3.30% and MacroF1 by 1.20% on actor/address-level risk recognition, and improves MacroF1 by 2.56% on transaction-level risk recognition when compared to state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating its effectiveness for task-only temporal blockchain fraud detection.

papers.title: Condensed Multi-Level Bisimulation Summaries
papers.abstract: Summary graphs have shown to be a valuable tool in graph analysis and processing, with applications in query optimization, retrieval, and visualization, among others. Many summarization approaches are based on the concept of stratified bisimulation, which determines vertex equivalence based on outgoing paths of length k. Summaries based on bisimulation typically also store information about all paths of length less than k, and thus explicitly encode the 1, 2, …, k bisimulations. To this end, we introduce condensed summaries : a formal model for representing stratified bisimulations in a compact manner. By leveraging repeating structures between consecutive bisimulation levels, condensed summaries represent all levels of bisimulation up to some k, while containing O(|V|) vertices, independent of k. We also prove that condensed summaries are equivalent to an established, uncondensed representation. Furthermore, we provide an algorithm for computing condensed summaries, along with an optimization that can yield a 20-fold speed-up. To demonstrate the efficacy of our model and algorithm, we provide experimental results on various edge-labelled graphs with up to 28 billion edges and a bisimulation depth of up to 4,757. All experiments successfully reached full bisimulation in less than 10 hours, while those with up to 1 billion edges only took minutes or even seconds, with no more than 64 GiB of memory. The resulting summaries were all substantially smaller than the original graphs, sometimes with a 95% reduction in vertices and edges. Code is available at: https://github.com/R-van-Bakel/Multi-Summaries.

papers.title: VisAdj: Learning Adjacency Matrices from Node-Link Images
papers.abstract: Learning adjacency matrices from node-link images is a fundamental problem for recovering structured graph information from visual observations.Existing methods typically rely on fixed KNN-based heuristics for candidate edge selection and fail to capture dependencies among edges.To overcome these limitations, we propose VisAdj, a new framework for topology-aware adjacency prediction. VisAdj introduces an attention-sparse neighbor sampler to adaptively select a high-recall set of candidate node pairs and performs joint edge inference using a line-graph transformer that treats candidate edges as tokens and explicitly models dependencies among incident edges.Extensive experiments on synthetic graphs, road networks, and vessel images demonstrate that VisAdj consistently outperforms existing baselines by clear margins.

papers.title: Continuous-Time Quantum Walks based Graph Neural Network
affiliations: School of Engineering Science, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are widely used on graph-structured data. However, most GNNs suffer from two key weaknesses. First, message passing acts as a low-pass filter based on the homophily assumption, so it performs poorly on heterophilic graphs, where connected nodes differ. Second, stacking layers makes node features converge exponentially to constants, a problem known as over-smoothing. Existing work usually addresses the two weaknesses separately. The few methods that target both rely on empirical heuristics, and many over-smoothing solutions further sacrifice the expressive power of the model. To address both weaknesses with theoretical justification, we propose CTQW-GNN , a GNN built on Continuous-Time Quantum Walks (CTQW). The design is motivated by two properties of the CTQW propagator e -iHt . (i) It is unitary and its eigenvalues lie on the unit circle, so no frequency component is damped. This directly counters the low-pass bias. (ii) Unitarity preserves the feature norm, so the Dirichlet energy does not decay exponentially with depth. This directly counters over-smoothing. Guided by these properties, CTQW-GNN combines three aggregation modules, each motivated by a specific gap in prior work. CTQW-based Aggregation evolves node features through the unitary propagator. It captures the mid- and high-frequency signals needed for heterophilic graphs and provably keeps the Dirichlet energy from collapsing, so it addresses both weaknesses in a single branch. CTQW-Attention Aggregation builds a multi-hop neighbor graph from the CTQW amplitudes and applies attention over it, so distant homophilic nodes that single-hop aggregation misses can still be reached. LF Aggregation is a standard low-pass branch (GAT) that preserves accuracy on strongly homophilic graphs, where a pure CTQW branch is suboptimal. We further provide a spectral-gap analysis that explains the energy preservation, and a Lieb–Robinson-type bound that gives a principled rule for choosing the walk-time t. Experiments on 14 benchmarks (9 heterophilic, 5 homophilic) show that CTQW-GNN reaches state-of-the-art accuracy on every dataset. Krylov propagation and Chebyshev-based sparsification keep the CTQW-related computation linear in the number of edges under the stated sparsification rule.

papers.title: Dual Prompt Adaptation for Zero-Shot Classification on Text-attributed Graphs
affiliations: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
papers.abstract: Graph learning plays a crucial role in capturing valuable information from both graph structures and node attributes. Despite their success, existing methods struggle to generalize to unseen datasets or classes. To achieve robust generalization, we identify two essential capabilities a graph model should possess: (1) Zero-shot inference on unseen classes, and (2) Cross-dataset adaptation under distribution shifts. Recently, Text-attributed Graphs (TAGs) have shed light on the possibility of achieving zero-shot classification due to their rich semantic information in node textual attributes. However, current studies on TAGs rely on handcrafted prompts for adaptation, which is engineering-intensive and overlooks structure shifts across different datasets. To bridge this gap, we propose ZeroPA, a dual-prompt adaptation framework for TAG methods that perform zero-shot prediction by matching node representations with label-text representations. Specifically, the textual prompt is prepended to label descriptions to enhance zero-shot classification. The graph prompt, on the other hand, is constructed as a subgraph and inserted into the original graph to calibrate node representations, thereby addressing distribution shifts. The dual prompts are optimized in an alternating and iterative manner, where each reinforces the other during adaptation. We conduct extensive experiments to verify the effectiveness of ZeroPA. The results demonstrate that ZeroPA consistently boosts the generalizability of TAG methods across diverse datasets. Our code is available at https://github.com/liuyang-tian/ZeroPA.git. (https://github.com/liuyang-tian/ZeroPA.git)

papers.title: ID 2 GL: Incremental Node Representation Learning on Large-Scale Dynamic Directed Graphs
papers.abstract: Node representation learning on dynamic graphs is a fundamental task for numerous real-world applications. However, existing dynamic Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) face two critical challenges: (1) the inability to effectively model crucial directional information inherent in many real-world interactions, and (2) suffer from poor scalability due to the neighbor explosion problem. To address these limitations, we propose ID 2 GL, a novel and scalable framework for incremental node representation learning on dynamic directed graphs. ID 2 GL features a decoupled architecture and introduces a novel propagation mechanism based on complex-valued personalized PageRank. This mechanism not only captures directionality via complex phases but also incorporates multi-hop neighbor information, which effectively alleviates the neighbor explosion issue. To handle continuous updates efficiently, we propose an incremental update mechanism that requires only local computations on affected nodes, supported by theoretical guarantees on the post-update representation error. Finally, a transformer-based prediction module is utilized to capture the temporal evolution of node representations for various downstream tasks. Extensive experiments on multiple real-world datasets, including the massive Papers100M dataset, demonstrate that ID 2 GL significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both node classification and link prediction tasks, and achieves competitive efficiency and scalability.

papers.title: Counterfactual Explanations for Hypergraph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Hypergraph Neural Networks (HGNNs) effectively model higher-order interactions in many real-world systems but remain difficult to interpret, limiting their deployment in high-stakes settings. We introduce CF-HyperGNNExplainer, a counterfactual explanation method for HGNNs that identifies the minimal structural changes required to alter a model's prediction. The method generates counterfactual hypergraphs using actionable edits limited to removing node-hyperedge incidences or deleting hyperedges, producing concise and structurally meaningful explanations. Extensive experiments on hypergraph benchmark datasets show that CF-HyperGNNExplainer generates valid and concise counterfactuals, highlighting the higher-order relations most critical to HGNN decisions.

papers.title: NetSight: Joint Spatio-Temporal Dependency Modeling for Network Traffic Prediction
papers.abstract: The traffic in today's networks is increasingly influenced by the interactions among network nodes as well as by the temporal fluctuations in the demands of the nodes. Traditional statistical methods to predict network traffic metrics have become obsolete due to their inability to address the non-linear and dynamic spatio-temporal dependencies present in today's network traffic. The most promising direction of research today is graph neural networks (GNNs) based prediction approaches that are naturally suited to handle graph-structured data. Unfortunately, the state-of-the-art GNN approaches separate the modeling of spatial and temporal information, resulting in the loss of important information about joint dependencies. These GNN based approaches further do not model information at both local and global scales simultaneously, leaving significant room for improvement. To address these challenges, we propose NetSight, which jointly learns spatio-temporal dependencies simultaneously at both global and local scales from the time-series of measurements of any given network metric collected at various nodes in a network. NetSight achieves this through three key innovations: a spatio-temporal adjacency matrix that fuses spatial topology with temporal similarity, a node normalization technique that enables joint spatio-temporal learning, and an architecture that applies temporal modeling directly on spatial embeddings rather than treating the two modalities independently. Through extensive evaluations and comparison with prior approaches using data from three large real-world networks, we show that NetSight significantly outperforms prior state-of-the-art approaches. All code and data used in this paper is available at [1].

papers.title: Decomposed Attention Frequency Debiased Transformer Model: Large Time-series Model for Satellite Orbit Prediction
papers.abstract: Accurate satellite orbit prediction is critical for collision avoidance and sustainable space operations. However, conventional prediction methods are constrained by coarse update intervals and orbit discontinuities. Additionally, building separate prediction models for each satellite is computationally expensive, making large-scale accurate forecasting increasingly impractical. To address the aforementioned challenges, we propose the D ecomposed A ttention F requency debiased transformer ( DAF ) model, a large time-series prediction model that utilizes efficient Real Fast Fourier Transform (RFFT) and Inverse RFFT alongside positional embeddings. Our DAF also integrates Tensorized Multi-Head Attention based on Tensor Train Decomposition for parameter-efficient compression and improved performance. We pre-trained on a large-scale Starlink dataset comprising 6,955 satellites and evaluated zero-shot performance on seven cross-domain satellite orbit datasets and three real-world datasets. DAF achieves up to a 34.85% reduction in mean squared error and a 16.01% reduction in mean absolute error over the second-best model, using only 0.045% of its parameters while maintaining inference speed comparable to conventional neural network baselines. These results demonstrate that DAF enables zero-shot, high-precision orbit prediction not only for Starlink satellites but also for other satellite types.

papers.title: Compositional Spectral Prompts for LLM-based Online Time Series Forecasting
papers.abstract: To address the sequential and evolving nature of time series, the Online Time Series Forecasting (OTSF) task has been extensively studied in multiple domains. Existing research focuses on adapting to non-stationary environments by employing memory buffer-based retrieval strategies. However, we observe that such frameworks struggle with long-term adaptation and fail to generalize to unseen patterns. To this end, we introduce CoSPOT, an LLM-based online time series forecasting framework that leverages a pre-trained LLM as the backbone online forecaster, motivated by its strong few-shot capabilities. For efficient online adaptation, CoSPOT keeps the LLM frozen and employs compositional spectral prompts grounded in frequency-domain bases to guide the model with the overall distribution of the input, thereby substantially reducing the number of parameters updated during the online phase. Specifically, CoSPOT decomposes time series into frequency bases and composes the corresponding spectral basis prompts according to their amplitudes, allowing unseen patterns to be represented as new combinations of learned basis prompts. Our extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate the superiority and practicality of CoSPOT across challenging online scenarios, including extended online phases and cross-dataset settings with substantial distribution shifts. Our code is available at https://github.com/seungyoon-Choi/CoSPOT.

papers.title: LSPP: Injecting Local Structural Patterns into Time Series Forecasting via Adaptive Prototype Pool
affiliations: Nanjing University of Science and Technology
papers.abstract: Deep learning has demonstrated remarkable advancements in time series forecasting. Most existing methods formulate forecasting as a purely continuous regression task optimized by mean squared error. However, this point-wise strategy neglects underlying structural patterns, often yielding over-smoothed and unreliable predictions. To address this challenge, we propose Local Structural Prototype Pool (LSPP), a two-stage pattern-aware method that injects local structural patterns into forecasting via an adaptive prototype pool, reformulating prediction as a discrete-continuous representation learning process. Specifically, LSPP first builds a shared prototype pool through self-supervised reconstruction to compactly capture recurring structural patterns. During forecasting, LSPP encodes historical patches into global continuous representations, matches them against the prototype pool to extract local structural patterns, and fuses both global and local representations for the final prediction. A central contribution of LSPP is that the prototype pool remains learnable throughout the forecasting stage, continuously adapting to evolving temporal dynamics via a semantic alignment loss. Extensive experiments on diverse real-world benchmarks demonstrate that LSPP achieves competitive performance while maintaining favorable computational efficiency. Our code is available at https://github.com/l00907l/LSPP.

papers.title: KoopSDE: Time-Series Forecasting Under Noise with Koopman Operators and Latent Stochastic Differential Equations
papers.abstract: Long-horizon forecasting of multivariate time series is a fundamental problem in machine learning, with applications in resource planning, environmental monitoring, economic analysis, and biomedical surveillance. As the prediction horizon grows, small errors accumulate; at the same time, real measurements are rarely noise-free, and many systems show both structured dynamics and random variation. Methods based on Koopman operator theory have shown that nonlinear dynamics can be represented as linear evolution in a learned observable space, yielding models that are both accurate and mathematically interpretable. A persistent limitation of deterministic formulations is that they do not explicitly separate observation noise from the linear dynamics being learned; without such separation, noise may be absorbed into the operator and the embedding, making the true dynamics harder to recover and degrading long-range prediction. We introduce KoopSDE, a method that extends Koopman-based linear latent forecasting with a latent stochastic differential equation whose drift is tied to the Koopman generator through a matrix logarithm identity, and whose diffusion is learned from data. The model combines objectives for linear evolution and stochastic trajectories with a denoising mechanism that biases the Koopman component toward smooth dynamical structure while the SDE branch is trained against the raw observations. KoopSDE is evaluated on six standard long-horizon benchmarks and on an epidemiological series. It achieves the best or second-best mean squared error on every reported dataset and horizon, reduces the average MSE by 5.4% compared to a strong deterministic Koopman baseline across all settings, and shows growing improvement at longer horizons. Synthetic validation on a chaotic attractor with controlled noise further shows that the complete KoopSDE framework remains advantageous as controlled observation noise is introduced.

papers.title: LIPTS: LLM-enhanced Time Series Interpolation and Prediction with Incomplete Data
papers.abstract: Multivariate time series forecasting supports state estimation and trend analysis of complex dynamic systems by modeling temporal dependencies among multiple variables. However, real-world time series are often sparse and incomplete due to irregular or constrained data collection, which degrades forecasting performance. Existing methods typically adopt either imputation-then-forecasting or direct forecasting from incomplete observations. The former separates imputation from forecasting, causing interpolation errors to propagate into prediction, while the latter may overlook latent evolution patterns in missing segments. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) suggest their potential to capture high-level sequential semantics and infer contextual patterns beyond observed numerical values, making them promising for reasoning over incomplete temporal dynamics. To address these challenges, we propose LIPTS (Large language model-based interpolation and prediction for Time Series), an end-to-end framework for time series imputation and forecasting based on LLMs. LIPTS jointly optimizes missing value interpolation and downstream forecasting within a unified framework, thereby alleviating the propagation of interpolation errors in two-stage pipelines. Moreover, it introduces an LLM-enhanced cross-modal semantic branch to infer global temporal semantics behind incomplete observations and provide complementary information for latent evolution in missing segments. The numerical branch captures historical and seasonal dependencies from observed values, while latent alignment bridges semantic representations and the numerical forecasting space, encouraging interpolated values to follow the temporal distribution required for downstream forecasting. Extensive experiments on real-world benchmarks demonstrate that LIPTS outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in prediction accuracy and robustness across different missing rates and prediction horizons.

papers.title: Cross-Variable Forecasters Commit to an Arbitrary Mixing Scaffold
papers.abstract: Modern multivariate time-series forecasters increasingly rely on cross-variable mechanisms, with their gains commonly attributed to learning meaningful inter-variable dependency structure. This attribution is widely assumed but rarely tested at the mechanism level, since benchmark improvements may arise either from learning meaningful variable relationships or simply from the capacity to mix information across variables. To address this, we introduce a shuffle control, a per-instance random permutation applied to a model’s cross-variable operator that destroys variable identity while exactly preserving sparsity, weight distribution, row sums, and overall mixing capacity. Applying this control to representative cross-variable forecasters, we find that the learned wiring is largely interchangeable with a random one of the same shape. The dissociation is sharp: trained models strongly depend on their learned wiring, yet training from scratch on a random one recovers nearly identical accuracy. To verify that the shuffle control can detect genuine structure, we construct synthetic datasets with installed dependency patterns, where the same analysis produces strong shuffle sensitivity and the expected ordering. Overall, our study suggests that many current cross-variable forecasting gains arise primarily from mixing capacity rather than recovery of meaningful dependency structure, and we release the shuffle control as a simple mechanism-level diagnostic for evaluating future cross-variable claims. Code is available at https://github.com/SeongJinAhn/Cross-Variable-Forecasters-Commit-to-an-Arbitrary-Mixing-Scaffold.

papers.title: CausalDiff: Causality-Preserving Diffusion for Interpretable Multivariate Time-Series Generation
papers.abstract: Multivariate time-series generation is important for data augmentation, simulation, and downstream analysis. Beyond the temporal dynamics of individual variables, multivariate time series also encode evolving cross-variable relationships, among which directional dependencies with temporal lags characterize how information propagates across variables over time. However, existing generative methods primarily focus on matching the distributional and temporal characteristics of real data, while the direction, strength, and temporal delay of these lagged dependencies may still be distorted in generated sequences. To address this gap, we propose CausalDiff, an interpretable nonlinear diffusion framework that explicitly models dynamic lagged causal relevance during time-series generation. Specifically, each window is represented by a historical prefix, a lagged causal-relevance tensor, and a residual sequence, corresponding to the initial temporal context, estimated lagged propagation structure, and unexplained variation, respectively. A KAN-based edge mechanism further parameterizes each estimated lagged relation with an explicit nonlinear function, making the learned edge-wise propagation patterns interpretable. For anomalous time-series generation, CausalDiff models normal-referenced shifts in causal relevance and residual variation to synthesize deviations from normal dynamics. Experiments show that CausalDiff achieves better agreement with ground-truth causal structures on causal benchmarks and stronger consistency with estimated lagged causal structures on real-world datasets while maintaining competitive distributional quality. These findings indicate that explicitly modeling lagged causal relevance helps align generated multivariate time series with the structural dynamics observed in real data while retaining edge-level interpretability. The source code is available at: https://github.com/znmiao/CausalDiff.

papers.title: DCFAD: Dual-Path Cross-Attention with Learnable Fractional Fourier Transform for Time Series Anomaly Detection
affiliations: Shanxi University of Finance and Economics
papers.abstract: Multivariate time series anomaly detection is crucial for failure diagnosis, network security, and intelligent operations. Reconstruction-based approaches are well suited for unsupervised scenarios, as they detect anomalies without labeled data and model complex temporal patterns through reconstruction. However, despite recent progress in point-wise anomaly detection and frequency-enhanced representations, existing methods largely rely on fixed representation domains, which may limit their ability to separate diverse pattern-wise anomalies from normal patterns and produce robust anomaly scores. We propose DCFAD, a unified framework that integrates a learnable fractional Fourier transform (FrFT) and a dual-path cross-domain attention mechanism. DCFAD learns anomaly-sensitive intermediate representations between time and frequency domains by adaptively adjusting the fractional order of FrFT during training. Meanwhile, the dual-path cross-domain attention establishes cross-domain correspondences from temporal and variable dimensions, enabling selective fusion of time-domain and fractional-domain features for reliable anomaly reconstruction. Extensive experiments on 10 real-world datasets with multiple evaluation metrics demonstrate the state-of-the-art overall performance of DCFAD in multivariate time series anomaly detection. Notably, DCFAD achieves a 9.5 percentage-point improvement in average AUC-ROC over the strongest AUC-ROC baseline while maintaining efficient inference. The complete code has been released at https://github.com/Jia-xw1/DCFAD.

papers.title: Tanca: Topology-Anchored Neural Causal Architecture for Event Prediction in Critical Infrastructure Networks
papers.abstract: In critical infrastructure networks such as microwave communication systems, accurate prediction of asynchronous event streams is crucial for proactive operations and maintenance as well as root-cause localization. Although deep temporal point process (TPP) models, exemplified by the Transformer Hawkes Process (THP), have made progress in temporal dependency modeling, their application to industrial-scale physical networks faces a fundamental topology--causality paradox: data-driven self-attention mechanisms tend to infer spurious causal associations from co-occurrence noise, whereas static physical topology priors struggle to capture latent cross-layer dependencies. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Topology-Anchored Neural Causal Architecture (Tanca). Built upon standard temporal contextual attention, Tanca introduces a physical-distance prior bias and a learnable latent causal bias, thereby jointly modeling temporal dependencies, physical constraints, and data-driven causal evidence at the attention-logit level. Furthermore, it introduces a Topology-Enhanced Causal Gating (TECG) module, which uses distance-aware exponential decay gating and learnable smooth conflict gating to enable the model to respect physical boundaries while suppressing spurious local-neighbor propagation and retaining long-range latent causal paths. To evaluate the effectiveness of Tanca, we conduct extensive experiments on real-world alarm datasets and synthetic datasets. The results demonstrate that Tanca consistently outperforms multiple representative baseline models in terms of event-type prediction accuracy and test log-likelihood.

papers.title: GadMIL: Granularity-Aware Association Discovery for Multi-Instance Time Series Classification
affiliations: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)
Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications
The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
papers.abstract: Time series classification (TSC) aims to identify discriminative temporal evidence that determines sequence-level labels. Multi-instance learning (MIL) models each sequence as a bag of temporal instances and enables instance-level evidence aggregation. However, existing MIL-based methods rely on a fixed instance granularity, implicitly assuming that discriminative patterns emerge at a single temporal resolution. In practice, temporal evidence is inherently multi-granularity, spanning long-term trends and short transient motifs. While multi-granularity architectures construct representations at different resolutions, they do not explicitly model how cross-granularity interactions contribute to bag-level decisions under the MIL formulation. Consequently, multi-granularity representation, structured cross-granularity interaction, and instance-level evidence aggregation remain disconnected. We propose GadMIL , the first granularity-aware multi-instance learning framework that unifies these components through structured association discovery. GadMIL constructs hierarchical instance bags across temporal granularities and introduces a structure-constrained input-adaptive masking mechanism to selectively activate informative cross-scale interactions. A positive instance clustering objective reinforces reliable hierarchical associations, and a granularity-wise expert fusion strategy adaptively integrates scale-specific predictions at the decision level. Extensive experiments on 46 UEA and UCR datasets demonstrate consistent state-of-the-art performance over strong Transformer-, multi-granularity-, and MIL-based baselines, validating the effectiveness of sparse cross-granularity association discovery for better time series classification.

papers.title: Pitfalls with Downsampled Data in AutoML for Clustering
papers.abstract: Finding the best-suited hyperparameters for applied algorithms is challenging in practice and in scientific evaluation. AutoML provides a reliable way to search for these. Still, a major issue in AutoML is scalability, as repeated evaluations are time-consuming, especially for large datasets. For classification tasks, downsampling has been shown to be effective for handling large datasets. In AutoML for unsupervised ML tasks such as clustering, recent research has also begun to integrate downsampling. However, finding suitable hyperparameters for clustering is quite underexplored and an even bigger challenge. We describe and demonstrate three key issues to address when applying downsampling to this task. Particularly, sampling may alter the instantiation of the underlying distribution, an aspect to which clustering methods are typically sensitive. Furthermore, we provide guidance for practitioners on mitigating some of these problems. Finally, we establish directions for future research to better support AutoML users for clustering.

papers.title: ACMDG: An Effective and Scalable Active Clustering via Multi-granularity Diffusion Graph
affiliations: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China
papers.abstract: Active clustering injects minimal human feedback into clustering via pairwise constraints, which is highly useful in data mining pipelines but difficult to scale in practice. Existing methods are expensive in two stages: initialization often requires building costly global structures, and each interaction round may trigger heavy recomputation. Meanwhile, substantial accuracy gains still demand many constraints. We present ACMDG, an effective and scalable active clustering framework built on a multi-granularity diffusion graph. ACMDG constructs a sparse yet connected multi-granularity diffusion graph structure by progressively modeling data relationships from fine-grained nearest-neighbor links to coarse-grained representations. Within an iterative refinement framework, it selects informative nodes in batch mode, categorizes them efficiently via a neighborhood-set-based interaction strategy, and refines clustering by diffusion-based label propagation. The overall framework runs in O(n log n) time. Extensive experiments on real-world and synthetic datasets show that ACMDG outperforms its counterparts in most cases in terms of clustering quality and scalability, while requiring significantly fewer constraints. Code is available at: https://github.com/BZhXuang/ACMDG_CIKM2026

papers.title: Offline Competence-Gap Mining for Motion Forecasting via Mode-Consistent Predictive Instability
papers.abstract: Large motion-forecasting logs contain substantially more scenes than practitioners can inspect, motivating budgeted, model-aware data triage. We formulate competence-gap discovery as an offline retrieval problem for a frozen stochastic multimodal forecaster. A dropout-free reference pass supplies its highest-confidence mode as a per-scene reference future, and each stochastic pass is aligned to that future by nearest-mode selection. The resulting model-specific predictive-instability score combines trajectory displacement and confidence volatility for the tracked reference mode. On nuScenes and Argoverse, the method yields the strongest high-error retrieval and sparsification performance among the tested confidence and representation-distance selectors; on Argoverse, it also outperforms the tested diversity and representativeness selectors. Fine-tuning LAformer on 500 mined Argoverse samples under mixed-batch replay reduces held-out tail minADE by 3.9%, compared with 2.0% for low-confidence selection, while producing the smallest full-set minADE degradation among the tested deployable selectors. The same LAformer-mined subset reduces HiVT tail minADE by 3.4%, demonstrating that the selected samples remain useful for a second forecasting backbone. These results support the use of mode-consistent predictive instability for offline audit prioritization.

papers.title: Evidence-Consistent Generative Detection under Scenario-Level Distribution Shift
papers.abstract: Conventional in-distribution evaluation can overestimate robustness when training and test data share recurring task-specific patterns or surface cues. This risk is especially relevant in social-engineering fraud detection, where attackers can preserve malicious intent while changing the scenario, impersonated entity, or wording. We study this problem as scenario-level out-of-distribution (SL-OOD) detection for SMS and voice phishing, where entire attack scenarios are held out from training while the label space remains fixed. This setting tests whether models can generalize to unseen attack scenarios using decision-relevant evidence rather than familiar scenario-specific cues. Using this SL-OOD evaluation, we find that high in-distribution performance does not reliably predict held-out robustness across feature-, encoder-, and decoder-based baselines. We interpret this gap as scenario memorization: reliance on recurring scenario-specific lexical or entity cues rather than decision-relevant evidence. We propose ECoG, an evidence-consistent generative framework that combines evidence-span supervision with a rationale-label consistency objective during training. On the 0.5B decoder, relative to the same backbone trained without consistency regularization, ECoG raises Macro-F1 on OOD challenging instances by 3.22 points, reduces the share of predictions whose generated rationale supports the opposite label by 4.22 points, and increases token-level overlap with reference evidence spans by 8.38 points; the reduction in prediction-rationale inconsistency is consistent across four decoder backbones. These results suggest that compact generative detectors can benefit from evidence supervision and rationale-label consistency under social-engineering shift.

papers.title: UGDACal: Nodewise Calibrator for Unsupervised Graph Domain Adaptation
papers.abstract: Unsupervised graph domain adaptation (UGDA) aims to enable node classification on an unlabeled target graph by transferring knowledge from a labeled source graph. Calibrating classifiers is essential to produce reliable probability estimates that support trustworthy decision-making. However, the prior art on UGDA primarily focuses on improving classification accuracy, largely ignoring the calibration of probability estimates. This paper proposes a novel nodewise calibrator (i.e., UGDACal) specifically designed for UGDA models. UGDACal computes the nodewise calibration parameter using an attention-based network that incorporates the structural information around a node. In addition, UGDACal is designed to generate an ensemble comprising nodewise-temperature-calibrated, uncalibrated, and uniform predictions to enhance calibration performance. A pseudo-labeled set is constructed from the unlabeled target graph and employed to train UGDACal, mitigating the impact of domain divergence. Extensive experiments on benchmark UGDA tasks demonstrate that UGDACal outperforms state-of-the-art calibration methods in calibrating UGDA models. The code is available at https://github.com/JiarenX/UGDACal.

papers.title: Knowledge-Informed Local Causal Discovery of Optimal Adjustment Sets
affiliations: Université Paris-Saclay, CNRS, CentraleSupélec, LISN UMR 9015
INSA Rouen Normandy, University of Rouen Normandy, LITIS UR 4108
papers.abstract: Local causal discovery is a scalable alternative to global structure learning. However, it can struggle to identify valid adjustment sets in data-scarce settings because of finite-sample uncertainty, incomplete local neighborhoods, and unresolved Markov equivalence. Although many application domains provide structured background knowledge, its integration into local causal discovery remains limited. We propose b-LOAD, a knowledge-informed extension of the LOAD algorithm for local discovery of optimal adjustment sets. b-LOAD incorporates prior edge constraints directly into the local structure-learning procedure and uses Meek's rules to expand the discovery frontier dynamically, yielding a knowledge-constrained MPDAG over the relevant local subgraph. This strategy helps prevent structurally relevant nodes introduced by prior knowledge from being excluded by local search. We prove that, under sound background knowledge, the procedure monotonically refines the admissible equivalence class and can enlarge the set of identifiable causal queries, enabling recovery of optimal adjustment sets that are not identifiable from observational conditional-independence information alone. Empirically, b-LOAD improves downstream causal effect estimation relative to purely data-driven and standard knowledge-augmented baselines, particularly in data-scarce and structurally complex regimes. Results on real-world biological networks show that locally targeted prior knowledge provides the largest gains and remains beneficial under moderate structural noise. These findings position b-LOAD as a scalable approach for converting fragmented domain knowledge into more reliable causal-effect estimation.

papers.title: Anytime-Budget Embedding Allocation for DLRMs via Continuous-Capacity Multiple-Choice Knapsack
papers.abstract: Embedding tables dominate the memory footprint of deep learning recommendation models (DLRMs), yet existing compression methods usually assume that the deployment memory budget is fixed before training. This is inconvenient in production, where the same recommender may be served across hardware tiers, multi-tenant resource conditions, or changing A/B-test operating points. We study anytime-budget embedding allocation : train one DLRM once, then export a hard budget-feasible embedding layout for any memory target in a specified range. We propose Continuous-Capacity Entropy-Smoothed MCKP (CC-MCKP), a differentiable allocation layer that integrates the real-valued budget directly into the multiple-choice knapsack partition function through a smooth feasibility gate. Differentiating this continuous-capacity partition function yields per-table action marginals for training and an analytic budget shadow price for sensitivity analysis, while final deployment still uses a hard MCKP solve with conservative discretization to guarantee feasibility. We provide smoothness, marginal, shadow-price, hard-limit, finite-gate, and grid-consistency results for the layer. Across Criteo Kaggle and Criteo Terabyte, one CC-MCKP-trained model approaches independently trained per-budget specialists (within about 10 -3 AUC on average) and provides the strongest average single-run accuracy, with its clearest gains at intermediate and unseen budgets and small reversals at the minimum-budget corner, where the feasible layout is unique. Hard export preserves zero budget violations, while one training run costs about 2× a plain model instead of the 13× of a per-budget specialist suite.

papers.title: A Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning Framework for Formulaic Alpha Factor Generation and Adaptive Composition
papers.abstract: Alpha factor mining aims to automatically construct predictive signals from raw market features and is fundamental to stock return forecasting. Recent reinforcement learning (RL) approaches formulate formulaic alpha discovery as a sequential decision problem yet face three key challenges. First, factor generation suffers from delayed and sparse rewards: informative feedback is typically available only after a complete expression is generated, making credit assignment for intermediate decisions difficult and limiting exploration efficiency. Second, overly rapid policy convergence limits the diversity and novelty of discovered expressions, further exacerbating factor crowding. Third, static factor composition fails to adapt to non-stationary market conditions. To address these challenges, we propose AlphaHRL, a new hierarchical RL framework for joint factor generation and adaptive composition. At the low level, we introduce process-level reward shaping to provide dense supervision during expression generation, including validity and stability signals. Then, we perform a tree-structured decomposition and a memory-based comparison to reshape terminal rewards using novelty, redundancy, and marginal utility signals relative to a maintained factor pool. At the high level, we learn a dynamic allocation policy that reweighs factors based on recent information coefficient (IC) trajectories, enabling regime-aware composition of a mega-alpha. Extensive experiments demonstrate that AlphaHRL consistently improves both factor quality and portfolio performance relative to state-of-the-art baselines. Our code is published anonymously at https://github.com/ECNU-CILAB/AlphaHRL.

papers.title: Knowledge World Model: Latent Rollouts for Learning Path Recommendation
affiliations: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology
papers.abstract: We replace the recursive observation-feedback rollout used in offline Learning Path Recommendation (LPR) with a latent transition predictor, thereby reducing pseudo-response error accumulation and per-step rollout computation. RL-based LPR commonly trains policies inside learner-model simulators. Existing rollouts ask the simulator to score the recommended problem, threshold the score into a pseudo-response, append that response to the history, and re-encode the history before the next decision. We refer to this detour as the Interaction Bottleneck, which induces pseudo-response error accumulation and repeated history re-encoding. The proposed Knowledge World Model (KWM) uses a latent transition predictor to map the current latent state and recommended problem to the next latent state. The same mastery readout then computes mastery estimates and rewards. Across five datasets and four RL-based LPR agents, KWM improves target mastery gain with an average relative gain of 14.47%. In efficiency measurements, KWM increases training episode throughput by 35.53% on average and achieves an average per-step latency speedup of 1.93x on ASSIST09. KWM also improves scores for sparse histories and target concepts absent from observed histories, while reducing long-horizon state drift. These results indicate that offline LPR can plan more reliably by rolling out latent states instead of recursively generating response histories.

papers.title: EVOL: Simulator-Guided Evolutionary Expert Synthesis for Deployment-Free Learning Path Recommendation
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) for learning path recommendation (LPR) faces two coupled obstacles. First, the policy must commit to a sequence of L concepts without intermediate feedback, producing a combinatorial search space that grows super-exponentially with L and provides reward only at the final step. Second, expert learning paths would be the natural cure for sparse-reward RL, but they do not exist in educational data, because student logs record what learners did, not what they should have done. We address both obstacles by importing a recipe from simulator-based demonstration learning in robotics: the knowledge tracing simulator is used both to synthesize per-learner expert demonstrations through evolutionary search and to train a deployment-free policy that distills these demonstrations into a feed-forward learner. Our framework EVOL instantiates this pipeline with an asymmetric actor-critic where the actor commits to deployment-realistic blind planning while the critic exploits the privileged simulator state during training. Across three datasets (ASSIST15, Junyi, EdNet; 39–189 concepts) and path lengths L∈5,10,20, EVOL surpasses 8 baselines spanning heuristic, sequential, RL, graph-enhanced RL, and LLM-enhanced methods. We further compare three imitation strategies (BC, AWR, DAPG) and show that final performance is governed by the quality of evolutionary experts rather than by the particular imitation objective.

papers.title: FreKT: Model-Agnostic Frequency-Domain Enhancement and Fusion for Knowledge Tracing
affiliations: Guangzhou College of Applied Science and Technology
papers.abstract: Knowledge tracing (KT) aims to estimate learners' latent knowledge states from historical interactions and predict their future performance. However, by treating learning histories mainly as temporal dependencies over discrete interactions, existing KT methods lack an explicit mechanism to distinguish stable knowledge progression from stage-wise learning rhythms and short-term response perturbations. Frequency-domain modeling offers a promising complementary view for KT, but existing attempts to introduce frequency modeling into KT remain insufficiently adapted to KT. They often rely on post-hoc spectral analysis over temporally compressed representations, lack semantic alignment between frequency patterns and knowledge-state transitions, and are tightly coupled with specific KT architectures, limiting their generality. To address these limitations, we propose FreKT, a model-agnostic frequency-domain KT framework. FreKT introduces a strictly causal parallel frequency branch to directly capture local spectral fluctuations from learning interactions. It further performs exercise-aware band reconstruction and aggregation to identify prediction-relevant frequency components and aligns the selected spectral patterns with temporal knowledge states through a task-aligned fusion module. With its model-agnostic design, FreKT can be flexibly integrated into different temporal KT backbones without changing their original prediction paradigms. Experimental results on multiple real-world datasets show that FreKT consistently improves the performance of various temporal KT models. Further analyses also verify the effectiveness of frequency-domain modeling in capturing learning behavior variations.

papers.title: Beyond Structured Vitals: Semantic-Temporal Alignment for Full-Record ICU Risk Forecasting
affiliations: Shanghai East Hospital, School of Medicine, Tongji University
papers.abstract: Traditional Electronic Health Record (EHR) datasets heavily favor structured data, often missing the nuanced progression of patients in intensive care. To address this gap, we introduce FRICU, a newly constructed dataset integrating structured vitals with full-record clinical narratives across complete admission trajectories using expert-verified, event-level annotations. Recognizing that the pathological impact of historical events depends on their semantic content rather than mere chronological proximity, we propose Semantic-Temporal Alignment (SeTA), a semantic-guided temporal attention mechanism that dynamically calibrates temporal receptive fields for query-specific evidence retrieval. For supervision, expert-verified risk labels are transformed into continuous trajectories via bidirectional Gaussian decay, providing smooth event-level supervision for gradual risk evolution. On FRICU, SeTA achieves a Sample AUPRC of 0.428, improving over TALE-EHR by 21.2%. On MIMIC-IV, SeTA achieves the best AUPRC on IMV and mortality prediction and remains competitive on sepsis prediction, demonstrating generalization beyond text-intensive full-record trajectories. To facilitate reproducibility, our code is available at https://github.com/violetesk/SeTA-FRICU.

papers.title: Mitigating Negative Feedback in Sequential Recommendations with Barlow Twins
papers.abstract: Sequential recommender systems are commonly optimized for next-item prediction, but they often underutilize negative feedback such as dislikes, skips, or low ratings. As a result, items that a user is likely to reject may still be ranked highly, which can reduce user satisfaction. Effectively incorporating negative feedback is challenging because such signals are often sparse, noisy, and must be modeled without degrading positive-preference prediction. We propose NegBT, a non-contrastive framework for negative-feedback-aware sequential recommendation based on the Barlow Twins objective. The key idea is to construct two deterministic views of the same user's history: a positive-only sequence that captures core preferences and a full mixed-feedback sequence that preserves the original behavioral context. By encouraging consistency between these representations while reducing feature redundancy, NegBT incorporates mixed-feedback histories as an auxiliary regularizer without relying on hard negative sampling. Experiments on three datasets show that NegBT provides a strong balance between positive-item accuracy and negative-feedback avoidance. In particular, it improves over positive-only SASRec on positive-target ranking metrics while reducing the relative promotion of negative items, with especially clear gains on explicit-feedback datasets and long user histories.

papers.title: Enriching Sequential Recommendation with Graph Laplacian Positional Embeddings
papers.abstract: Sequential recommenders typically rely on learnable positional embeddings to encode the order of user interactions. In this work, we ask whether this ordinal signal can be replaced by a structural one derived from the item space. We propose to use Laplacian positional embeddings in SASRec: we build an item co-occurrence graph from training interactions, compute eigenvectors of its symmetric normalized Laplacian, and use them as frozen graph-derived positional embeddings. The backbone architecture and training objective remain unchanged. Experiments on four public sequential-recommendation benchmarks show that this simple replacement improves SASRec performance on most ranking metrics and remains competitive with strong positional and temporal encoding baselines. These findings indicate that item-item graph structure can be an effective substitute for standard ordinal positional embeddings in sequential recommendation.

papers.title: Debate4Rec: Multi-Agent Debate for List-Level Feedback and Selection in Generative Recommendation
papers.abstract: Generative recommendation has become a promising paradigm for producing complete recommendation lists, yet providing proper feedback to multiple candidates remains challenging. A key difficulty is the conflict between matching users' historical preferences and maintaining content diversity. Existing reward modeling and re-ranking methods usually rely on fixed objective aggregation or single-model judgment, which limits their flexibility and explainability in resolving such conflicts. To address this issue, we propose Debate4Rec, a multi-agent debate framework for feedback and candidate-list selection in generative recommendation. Debate4Rec acts as an external list-level feedback signal producer that provides interpretable feedback and selects the best candidate list. It decomposes list evaluation into two specialized agents: a Preference Agent for assessing alignment with user interests, and a Diversity Agent for evaluating category coverage, redundancy, and list richness. The agents first make independent judgments and then conduct a structured two-round debate to exchange evidence, revise decisions, and reach a final selection. Experiments on ML-1M and a Kuaishou short-video dataset show that Debate4Rec achieves competitive and often better performance than the LLM-based and traditional re-ranking baselines under the candidate-list selection setting. Ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of role-specialized agents, structured debate, and the feedback-selector mechanism.

papers.title: Distilling Post-Conversion Content for User Retention Modeling
papers.abstract: User retention is a key metric to measure long-term engagement in modern platforms. In real-time bidding (RTB) advertising system for user re-engagement, the retention model is required to predict future revisit probability at bidding time, before the user converts and consumes any content. Although post-conversion content, termed Onboarding Content , provides highly informative signals for retention prediction, directly using it in training causes severe feature leakage and creates a gap between training and serving. To address this issue, we propose OCARM , a two-stage distillation-aligned framework for O nboarding C ontent A ugmented R etention M odeling, enabling the model to implicitly capture future content using only observable features during inference. In the first stage, we deliberately expose onboarding content to train a hierarchical encoder that produces teacher representations. In the second stage, a user encoder is aligned with the frozen teacher through distillation, allowing the model to approximate the inaccessible onboarding signals without leakage. Extensive offline experiments and online A/B tests demonstrate that our framework achieves consistent improvements in a real-world growth scenario.

papers.title: Gryphon: A Unified Architecture for Semantic-ID Generation and Item-Level Scoring in Industrial Recommendations
papers.abstract: Generative retrieval (GR) has become a scalable approach to candidate generation: each item is assigned a short hierarchical token sequence called a Semantic ID (SID), and the next item's SID is decoded autoregressively. A practical limitation is that the decoder's beam search optimizes the likelihood of token sequences, not the relevance of the underlying items. These objectives diverge when sequence likelihood is poorly calibrated due to beam search error accumulation, and when several items collapse onto a single SID and receive identical scores. We introduce Gryphon, an encoder-decoder generative recommendation architecture that adds a jointly trained item-level scoring component alongside SID generation, reusing the encoder's user representation computed in a single forward pass. Instead of ranking SIDs by accumulated token likelihood, Gryphon resolves each generated SID to its concrete items and re-scores those items directly, which sidesteps miscalibrated sequence scores and separates items that collide on the same identifier. On an industrial music service, with item-level scoring trained under a next-item-prediction objective, Gryphon attains the highest item-level Recall@1000, above the strongest baselines (+3.7% over vanilla GR and +2.5% over collision-resolved GR) at comparable parameter count and latency. Gryphon's item-level ranking also surpasses its beam-likelihood ranking of the same candidates (+4.2% gain), demonstrating the benefit of item-level scoring in GR. Deployed as the sole candidate source in a 7-day A/B test, Gryphon produced no statistically significant change in total listening time (+0.25%) while replacing a pipeline of more than 15 candidate generators and a separate preranking stage, substantially simplifying the candidate-generation system.

papers.title: S²DGR: Stable-State Diffusion for Generative Recommendation
papers.abstract: Generative recommendation represents each item as a semantic ID (SID) sequence and predicts the next item by generating its tokens from user-item interaction history. Recent diffusion-based methods replace autoregressive decoding with masked denoising, enabling bidirectional SID modeling and generation without a fixed left-to-right order. However, masked-diffusion GenRec still depends on two main selection stages: which SID tokens are masked during training and which partial SID candidates are retained during inference. Existing noising strategies estimate token uncertainty from a single probe context, which can make masked views sensitive to context-specific uncertainty, while path-level decoding can retain redundant trajectories that lead to the same partial SID state. We propose S 2 DGR, a stable-state diffusion framework for generative recommendation. S 2 DGR introduces Stability-Aware Noising (SAN), which aggregates SID-token uncertainty across multiple probe contexts to construct stable masked training views, and State-Unique Denoising (SUD), which selects inference candidates according to partial SID states rather than only denoising paths. Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets show that S 2 DGR consistently improves over strong discriminative, generative, and diffusion-based recommendation baselines.

papers.title: GRID: Generative Recommendation via Inpainting Diffusion
papers.abstract: Generative Recommendation (GR) utilizing discrete Semantic IDs (SIDs) has emerged as a promising paradigm for sequential recommendation. However, existing GR paradigms exhibit significant generation flaws: traditional autoregressive (AR) models suffer from strict left-to-right causal constraints leading to error accumulation, while current discrete diffusion adaptations rely on isolated next-item beam search, which causes "homogeneous stacking" and lacks explicit list-level coordination. Furthermore, these methods often compromise the interpretable, hierarchical structure of SIDs. To address these limitations, we propose GRID, a novel framework that reformulates generative top-K recommendation as a 2D discrete diffusion inpainting problem. By modeling the recommended item list and their multi-digit hierarchical SIDs along two orthogonal axes, GRID recovers the complete matrix of future items simultaneously via parallel decoding. To ensure structural validity and semantic diversity, we introduce a hierarchical SID construction method alongside a dual-regularized inpainting objective that enforces hierarchy consistency and intra-list uniqueness. Supported by a progressive curriculum training strategy, extensive experiments on three Amazon datasets demonstrate that GRID effectively overcomes homogeneous stacking, fundamentally resolving the limitations of traditional decoding, and achieves state-of-the-art performance across all benchmarks.

papers.title: SPRIG: Semantic-ID-enhanced Paths for Knowledge Graph-based Generative Recommendation
papers.abstract: Recommender systems leveraging generative models often generate item identifiers directly, rather than ranking catalog items by a recommendation score. Recent work extends beyond pure sequential interaction signals by incorporating item content and structured relationships among items, with two distinct directions emerging. Semantic IDs (SIDs) enrich item representations by replacing opaque, randomly initialized embeddings with hierarchically quantized discrete codes derived from item content. Knowledge-graph (KG) path reasoning instead generates entity-relation paths that ground recommendations in structured relationships between items, attributes, and external entities, thereby enriching the relational context. These two lines have complementary limitations: SID-based models lack relational grounding, while KG-based generative recommenders still represent items as arbitrary, opaque tokens tied to large embedding tables, limiting parameter sharing and generalization. We propose SPRIG , a generative recommender that integrates content-derived SIDs into KG path reasoning. SPRIG is trained on information-rich KG paths that terminate in items represented as discrete, content-derived tokens, combining the advantages of both approaches. We evaluate SPRIG on movie and music recommendation datasets against baselines spanning sequential language models, KG-augmented methods, and SID-based approaches. Our results show that SPRIG achieves competitive performance over prior generative models while using fewer parameters and a lower compute cost. Code: https://github.com/justinhangoebl/semantic-id-knowledge-graph-recommender

papers.title: Split Decisions: How Evaluation Protocols Change Recommender Model Selection
papers.abstract: Offline recommender evaluation often treats the train/test split as a technical detail, even though different split protocols answer different deployment questions. We study how the split protocol changes not only absolute ranking metrics, but also the model that would be selected from a candidate set. We evaluate widely used recommender models on widely used public recommender benchmarks under global-temporal, leave-one-out, random-interaction, and per-user temporal splits. Our evidence uses full-catalog ranking and defines split-induced model-selection regret : the loss on a global-temporal target caused by selecting a model under another split. Across public datasets and bounded industrial stress tests, non-global protocols often select different models and transfer poorly to the chronological target. The pattern persists across metrics, cutoffs, split seeds, and model sanity checks, suggesting that split choice is a model-selection decision rather than a harmless preprocessing detail. The results suggest that chronological deployment claims should either select models under a global-temporal protocol or report the regret induced by alternative splits.

papers.title: Do LLM Recommenders Know When They're Hallucinating? Auditing Confidence Calibration in Catalog Faithfulness
papers.abstract: LLM recommenders for top-K item suggestion regularly emit titles outside the target catalog. Prior audits report a binary out-of-domain rate; none ask whether the model knew. We jointly audit hallucination rate (OOD@10) and verbalized-confidence calibration (ECE, Brier, reliability) for four zero-shot LLM recommenders from four independent vendors (Mistral Large, Llama-3.3-70B, GPT-OSS-120B, Claude Sonnet 4.6), not grounded or fine-tuned systems, across three catalogs (MovieLens-25M, Amazon Reviews 2023 Toys, Yelp Open Dataset), stratified by item popularity. Measuring catalog membership is itself the hard part: on identical outputs the reported rate moves by an order of magnitude with the string matcher used, and F1 cannot separate the candidates. We validate the instrument against 201 human judgments and select on net bias, where the adopted one is off by -0.040 against +0.144 for the common fuzzy rule. Hallucination is then strongly catalog-dependent (0.6-2.7% on MovieLens, 11.6-38.7% on Yelp, 49.3-61.0% on Amazon Toys). Each model holds a near-constant confidence level barely responsive to the catalog, while the catalog-hit rate swings 60 points, so the sign of the error is set by where a model's constant lands against a catalog's accuracy: 7 of the twelve cells are under-confident and 5 over-confident, all four under-confident on MovieLens, all four over-confident on Amazon Toys. We read this as an elicitation mismatch: "Just Ask" elicits a generic quality rating, not a catalog-membership probability. A conformal abstention threshold over verbalized confidence changes hallucination by at most 1.65 pp across four alpha levels, because the channel cannot separate correct items from hallucinations. We recommend that audits report calibration alongside OOD, validate the matcher producing the OOD number, and use catalog-anchored elicitation.

papers.title: Give Me MoE: Dynamic Expert Routing for Inductive Graph-based Recommendation
affiliations: Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology
National Research University Higher School of Economics
papers.abstract: Graph-based recommender systems capture high-order user–item dependencies but often underperform in cold-start settings, especially for new items with limited interactions. Inductive graph models generalize to unseen users and items via node features and neighborhood aggregation. However, most rely on shared parameters that may be suboptimal for heterogeneous neighborhoods, which can limit cold-start performance. We propose MoE-IGR, a Mixture-of-Experts module for inductive graph-based recommendation that replaces the shared post-aggregation update with dynamic, layer-wise expert routing, enabling context-dependent message passing. We instantiate MoE-IGR on PinSage and evaluate it on three real-world datasets under temporal, cold-user, cold-item, and joint cold-start protocols. MoE-IGR yields substantial gains (up to 16% Recall@20), largest in cold-item recommendation (up to 34.4% NDCG@20). Routing analysis reveals expert specialization: cold items focus on a subset of experts, warm items prefer others, and semantically related item groups exhibit similar routing patterns, suggesting that experts capture both collaborative and semantic signals.

papers.title: Evaluating Provider-Fairness Mitigation in Price-Aware Recommendation
papers.abstract: Price-aware recommender systems incorporate economic signals into ranking, offering practical benefits but their implications for provider-side fairness remain largely unexplored. In this work, we present the first systematic evaluation of fairness mitigation in price-aware recommendation. We quantify provider-side exposure disparities across groups defined by continent , country , and price segment using three representative price-aware models on two datasets. Our analysis reveals systematic provider-side disparities, indicating that price-aware ranking can exhibit substantial provider imbalance. We then evaluate three post-processing re-ranking strategies (PFair, PFAR, and Calibration) applied to top-k recommendations to mitigate these disparities. Results show that mitigation effectiveness varies substantially across methods and settings. PFair achieves the strongest reductions for interaction-based exposure disparities, whereas PFAR is generally more effective under catalog-based reference distributions but exhibits substantial instability. Calibration remains comparatively conservative, producing only limited changes in disparity. These findings highlight the fairness risks of price-aware recommendation and show that the effectiveness of existing mitigation strategies is conditional on both the fairness reference distribution and the underlying ranking model.

papers.title: Orthogonal Popularity Decomposition for Sequential Recommendation
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
papers.abstract: Popularity bias is common in sequential recommenders, disproportionately favoring frequent items over long-tail ones. We identify representation anisotropy as a geometric manifestation of this bias: item embeddings collapse toward a cone whose dominant direction correlates with item frequency. To address this, we propose Orthogonal Popularity Decomposition (OPD), which introduces a learnable popularity direction and projects item embeddings onto it, isolating a popularity component from an orthogonal collaborative subspace. OPD produces a near-isotropic embedding subspace and provides an interpretable, controllable popularity prior that can be tuned at inference without retraining. Experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that OPD enables controllable accuracy–fairness trade-offs and consistent performance gains across all datasets. The source code is available online.

papers.title: T-MSDF: T-shaped Convolutional Multi-stream Discovery Framework with LLM-Driven Compatibility Priors
papers.abstract: In modern recommender systems, the “filter bubble” effect remains a formidable challenge as models tend to over-exploit historical interactions at the expense of potential interest discovery. Although various exploration strategies have been proposed, effectively balancing prediction precision with serendipity within the ranking layer remains an open problem. To address this challenge, this paper introduces T-MSDF , a novel T-shaped convolutional Multi-stream Sequential Discovery Framework. T-MSDF leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to construct a category affinity table that quantifies semantic complementarity between product categories, enabling the generation of augmented behavior sequences along exploration paths grounded in real-world common-sense logic. The framework consists of four synergistic components: (1) an LLM-constrained Sequence Expansion module that generates knowledge-augmented behavior streams; (2) a T-shaped Convolutional Fusion Network that harmonizes temporal evolution with spatial complementarity across behavior streams; (3) an Interest Decoupling and Alignment scheme, which disentangles convergent preferences from divergent exploration signals via residual extraction and discovery-aware contrastive learning; and (4) an Adaptive Gated Fusion Network , which dynamically weights the decoupled interest representations to prioritize serendipitous recommendations without compromising ranking precision. Extensive offline evaluations and online A/B tests on a large-scale industrial platform demonstrate that T-MSDF significantly improves key discovery metrics, achieving a +5.92% increase in Discovery Rate (DR) and a +6.15% lift in Discovery-CTR , alongside notable growth in CTR (+1.18%) and GMV (+2.30%) .

papers.title: Can Large Language Models Identify Meaningful Touchpoints in Conversion Attribution?
papers.abstract: Touchpoint selection in conversion attribution, namely identifying meaningful touchpoints contributing to conversions, is essential for e-commerce recommendation and online advertising. Current selection methods rely heavily on collaborative-filtering-based heuristics, which fail to align with user-perceived semantic intent. Through human annotation, we reveal a significant semantic gap: many implicitly-related, semantically relevant touchpoints remain undetected by existing rules. Therefore, we systematically evaluate the capability of Large Language Models (LLMs) in identifying these hidden associations. Our evaluation shows that while LLMs effectively uncover a substantial portion of implicitly-related touchpoints, significant room for improvement remains in their selection performance. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of different prompting strategies and foundation model choices on identification performance, providing valuable insights into their reasoning patterns and effectiveness. These insights offer a new roadmap for transitioning conversion attribution from mechanical rule-matching to human-aligned semantic reasoning. Moreover, we leverage the LLM-attributed conversion labels for enhancing industrial CVR model training and achieve significant offline performance gains, showing the potential of LLMs in conversion attribution.

papers.title: Context-Aware User Intent Modeling for Relevant Recommendation in E-commerce
papers.abstract: Relevant recommendation is essential for e-commerce conversion and is typically initiated by a user-clicked trigger item. However, user intent is inherently dynamic and multifaceted.
