We evaluate C2P on a public benchmark and a large-scale industrial dataset. Offline results show that C2P outperforms strong baselines, with notable gains on ambiguous attributes. Online A/B tests on AliExpress further show consistent improvements in seller adoption, attribute completeness, and user engagement, validating C2P’s effectiveness and efficiency in real-world deployment.

papers.title: Self-Evolving Ontology via Cumulative Definition Enrichment for Entity Canonicalization
papers.abstract: Ontology grounding pipelines rely on expert-curated vocabularies, but citizens describe the same facilities in their own words. The Korean Safety e-Report platform, which routes over one million citizen complaints annually to responsible agencies, suffers from exactly this problem: its keyword-matching pipeline fails to recognize many citizen expressions, causing misrouted reports and delayed field response. We present Cumulative Definition Enrichment (CDE), which continually discovers synonym expressions from incoming complaints and incorporates them into entity definitions, producing embeddings that improve as the ontology absorbs real usage. Experts design the ontology structure, while CDE learns the vocabulary from the complaint stream. We define two evaluation metrics: Direct Link Rate (DLR), the fraction of complaints resolved through automatic ontology grounding, and Qualified DLR (Q-DLR), which combines DLR with synonym mapping accuracy. DLR alone can be misleading because adding incorrect synonyms still increases coverage; Q-DLR captures whether the added synonyms are actually correct. On 100K real complaints across two ontology versions and two initialization settings, CDE achieves the highest Q-DLR in every condition. Scalability experiments on 600K complaints confirm consistent performance. All processing runs on-premise with limited GPU resources under strict data sensitivity constraints, and the system is planned for government integration starting in 2027.

papers.title: Micro vs. Macro Averaging for Link Prediction Evaluation in Knowledge Graphs
papers.abstract: Link prediction aims to infer missing (subject, predicate, object) triples in a knowledge graph. To evaluate link prediction, each test triple is transformed into two queries: (subject, predicate, ?) and (?, predicate, object), and the rank of the corresponding correct, singleton answer is recorded. However, current empirical studies largely ignore the fact that multiple test triples may share the same (subject, predicate) or (predicate, object) pairs, resulting in queries with multiple correct answers. These settings naturally correspond to micro and macro averaging in traditional machine learning and information retrieval. Despite its importance, the macro setting has received very little attention. Prior work is limited to a single study over two benchmarking datasets, FB15K-237 and WN18RR, using a limited set of ranking metrics. Other metrics specifically designed to capture multi-answer retrieval behavior, such as Bpref and RBP, have not yet been analyzed in the macro setting. In this paper, we present an empirical study of micro and macro averaging for link prediction evaluation in knowledge graphs. We analyze nine benchmarking datasets to characterize query imbalance and the distribution of correct answers per query. We further evaluate ten pre-trained link prediction models for each dataset under both micro and macro averaging using several metrics, including Bpref and RBP. Our results show that macro averaging tends to yield higher effectiveness scores than micro averaging, consistent with previous observations on FB15K-237. Non-singleton queries, those with multiple answers, exhibit distinct ranking behavior, revealing differences in how models find correct answers beyond the first one. We conclude that macro averaging and non-singleton queries deserve more attention in link prediction evaluation.

papers.title: Pre-retrieval Query Clustering for Adaptive Top-k Document Retrieval in RAG Systems
papers.abstract: RAG systems commonly retrieve a fixed number of documents (top-k) to ground generation, but this static approach is brittle: simple queries suffer over-retrieval (adding noise and cost) while complex queries are under-retrieved, causing recall failures that cascade into incorrect answers. Motivated by the question of how many documents must be retrieved to answer an arbitrary query reliably, we propose a practical, general framework for query-adaptive retrieval depth. Offline, we estimate per-query retrieval difficulty by measuring NDCG under the default retriever and deriving a query-specific “saturation” point k* from the NDCG–k curve. Because computing these signals online is expensive, we cluster a large set of queries in embedding space and summarize each cluster with a recommended retrieval depth that targets high coverage (e.g., ~95%) using a mean-plus-variance rule. At runtime, the system assigns an incoming query to a cluster and selects the corresponding top-k in constant time. Compared with post-retrieval confidence methods that rely on clustering retrieved documents, our approach is pre-retrieval and query-centric, making it robust in heterogeneous, case-like corpora and applicable across domains such as legal, healthcare, finance, and enterprise search. Finally, this framework has been tested in full-traffic queries that improved F 1 by over 36% while reducing token usage by 14% on low-complexity clusters without accuracy loss.

papers.title: GraphMind: From Operational Traces to Self-Evolving Workflow Automation
papers.abstract: Complex operational workflows are central to system operations, yet remain difficult to automate due to heavy human input and limited adaptability. We present GraphMind, a system that constructs, executes, and evolves action-centric workflow graphs with minimal human effort. The system operates in three phases. First, a *scalable offline pipeline* extracts structured workflow graphs from human resolution traces, capturing problems, actions, and their causal relationships. Second, an *online multi-agent traversal* engine navigates the graph to dynamically construct and execute workflows, combining graph-guided retrieval with LLM-driven reasoning. Third, *Adaptive Traversal Reinforcement* (ATR) reinforces successful traversal paths, enabling execution-informed graph adaptation. GraphMind has been deployed across four cloud database services for incident investigation. Evaluated on 93 held-out incidents and validated via blind expert review, the system outperforms an Agentic Summary-RAG baseline in mitigation reach, hallucination rate, and diagnostic throughput while requiring 8x less retrieval context. The ATR layer reduces hallucination rate by 26%, demonstrating that workflow graphs can learn from execution feedback. A 12-week field study confirms practical value: 97% of scored conversations yield actionable results within interactive latency.

papers.title: HiSAC: Hierarchical Sparse Activation Compression for Ultra-long Sequence Modeling in Recommendation Systems
papers.abstract: We introduce HiSAC (Hierarchical Sparse Activation Compression), a framework that compresses ultra-long user behavior sequences into compact, personalized interest representations for industrial recommendation. Modeling histories with thousands of interactions is essential for capturing dynamic user preferences, yet existing compression methods suffer from two fundamental limitations: they impose a fixed number of global interest centers that ignore per-user granularity, and they rely on hard assignment that introduces quantization error and discards long-tail behaviors. HiSAC addresses both via three tightly integrated components: (1)multimodal tokenization with Residual Quantized VAE that maps items to a hierarchical discrete codebook, (2)a hierarchical voting mechanism that sparsely activates user-specific interest-agents as adaptive preference centers, and (3)a Soft-Routing Attention that aggregates all historical signals in a debiased semantic space, weighting contributions by similarity to minimize quantization error and preserve sparse long-tail preferences. We validate HiSAC on a large-scale industrial dataset (200M users, 30B interactions) and the public Taobao-MM benchmark, where it consistently outperforms both generic compression baselines and state-of-the-art sequence models. Deployed on Taobao's “Guess What You Like” homepage serving hundreds of millions of daily active users, HiSAC delivers a 1.65% CTR uplift, 2.24% CTCVR improvement, and 2.56% increase in orders while reducing end-to-end inference latency by over 40% relative to the deployed compression baseline.

papers.title: Controllable Autoregressive Retrieval with Long-term Action Perception for Recommendations
papers.abstract: Autoregressive retrieval (AR) has emerged as a leading paradigm for the first stage of industrial recommender systems. However, existing AR methods (i) overlook long-term action perception, training their generation only against the immediate next interaction, and (ii) lack the controllability needed to align candidate generation with diverse business goals without retraining. We propose Controllable Autoregressive Retrieval with long-term action perception (CAR), a simple yet deployable framework that addresses both issues. A long-term supervision module attaches multiple action-sliding prediction heads at different future horizons and transfers their knowledge to the main model via parameter sharing (P-CAR) or cascading (C-CAR), injecting a long-horizon perspective. An action-induced input module reorders the input as an action--item sequence and exposes a target action token at inference time, enabling goal-aware control over the recall set. Experiments on three public benchmarks and two industrial datasets, along with online A/B tests on QQ Music and WeSing, which now serve hundreds of millions of daily users in production, show consistent, statistically significant gains over strong AR baselines.

papers.title: TagLLM: A Fine-Grained Tag Generation Approach for Note Recommendation
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown promising potential in E-commerce community recommendation. While LLMs and Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) are widely used to encode notes into implicit embeddings, leveraging their generative capabilities to represent notes with interpretable tags remains unexplored. In the field of tag generation, traditional close-ended methods heavily rely on the design of tag pools, while existing open-ended methods applied directly to note recommendations face two limitations: (1) MLLMs lack guidance during generation, resulting in redundant tags that fail to capture user interests; (2) The generated tags are often coarse and lack fine-grained representation of notes, interfering with downstream recommendations. To address these limitations, we propose TagLLM, a fine-grained tag generation method for note recommendation. TagLLM captures user interests across note categories through a User Interest Handbook and constructs fine-grained tag data using multimodal CoT Extraction. A Tag Knowledge Distillation method is developed to equip small models with competitive generation capabilities, enhancing inference efficiency and reducing costs. In online A/B test, TagLLM increases average view duration per user by 0.31%, average interactions per user by 0.96%, and page view click-through rate in cold-start scenario by 32.37%, demonstrating its effectiveness. TagLLM has been deployed in Dewu's community services, generating tag features for over 600,000 new notes daily.

papers.title: ConnectionMind: Leveraging Social Networks and Large Language Models for Personalized Recommendation at Meta
papers.abstract: Modern recommendation systems on social media platforms such as Meta must model complex social relationships alongside massive and heterogeneous content such as text and video. Traditional recommendation models, however, often omit these signals or treat them independently, limiting their ability to integrate multi-relational context for fine-grained personalization. We present ConnectionMind, a production-ready recommendation framework that tightly integrates social network structure with large language models (LLMs) to enable scalable and reasoning-aware personalization at Meta. ConnectionMind constructs a heterogeneous graph connecting users, items, friends, groups, and creator pages, and formulates recommendation as a graph reasoning problem that discovers personalized paths from users to candidate items. An LLM-based policy reasons over these graph structures to guide recommendation decisions. To train the system at scale, ConnectionMind adopts a two-stage strategy: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on large-scale user–item interaction trajectories to initialize the reasoning policy, followed by end-to-end reinforcement learning (RL) to further optimize personalized graph reasoning. Extensive experiments on multiple real-world datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over representative baselines. More importantly, ConnectionMind has been deployed in Meta's large-scale recommendation pipeline and evaluated through online A/B tests, achieving a 0.43% improvement in video watch time . These results demonstrate the effectiveness and measurable real-world impact of graph-based LLM reasoning for production recommendation.

papers.title: LLM Meets Traffic: Traffic-Aware Large Language Models for Next POI Recommendation in Vehicle Navigation Interfaces
papers.abstract: Next Point-of-Interest (POI) recommendation is a production-relevant task for modern in-car navigation interfaces. Given a user’s current and historical context, the system can suggest the next destination while accounting for both user preference and travel feasibility. However, existing Large Language Models (LLMs) for next POI recommendation (1) overlook real-time traffic conditions and thus fail to account for user-specific trade-offs between POI preferences and travel time, and (2) rely on text embedding-based POI candidate retrieval, which may surface semantically similar yet geographically implausible POIs. To address these limitations, we propose TraPOI, a Traffic-aware LLM for Next POI Recommendation. TraPOI consists of (i) a multimodal embedding alignment module to project POI, GPS, and traffic data into the LLM’s latent space, and (ii) a multi-view candidate retrieval module that retrieves distance-based and embedding-based candidates to facilitate spatially feasible and semantically relevant next POI recommendation. We also introduce (iii) multimodal prompting to explicitly incorporate traffic and spatial context into the LLM’s reasoning process. We constructed two novel datasets aligning check-in records with real-time traffic data from Seoul and California (CA) to validate our approach. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TraPOI significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving accuracy gains up to 11.61%. Our code and dataset are available at: https://github.com/kmw409722-svg/TraPOI.

papers.title: Resolving Price-Segment Blindspot in Search Ranking for Value-Driven Marketplaces
papers.abstract: On value-driven marketplaces, user-product interactions concentrate heavily around affordable products. Search ranking systems trained on such engagement data therefore learn relevance patterns that primarily reflect the preferences of the dominant value conscious user cohort, limiting their ability to accurately personalize results for users whose intent aligns with relatively higher-priced products. We refer to this failure mode as the Price-Segment Blindspot . This challenge cannot be addressed through static promotion of higher-priced products, because price preference is highly contextual. A value-conscious user may occasionally search for an expensive “silk saree” before a wedding, while users with affinity toward high-priced products may still prefer inexpensive products for routine purchases. Effective ranking therefore requires modeling latent user affinity and real-time query intent to infer when different price segments are relevant. We address this challenge by incorporating user-level affinity and query-level intent signals into a production ranking system. However, on-platform interactions alone provide weak evidence of user's price-segment affinity due to sparse interactions in higher price segment. To address this sparsity, we augment the user affinity model with off-platform behavioral signals that better capture user spending patterns. In a three-week A/B experiment on the Meesho platform with ∼300 million monthly active users, our approach improved the GMV c (Gross Merchandise Value Contribution) of the High Price-Segment products by 5.92% and orders by 6.32% , while keeping the overall O/V i (Orders-per-Viewer) nearly flat +0.06% .

papers.title: Scalable Organization-Specific Language Model Adaptation for Multi-Tenant Enterprise Search
papers.abstract: In multi-tenant (An architecture where a single, shared instance of software and infrastructure serves multiple independent customers (“tenants”). It maximizes resource efficiency and lowers costs, while relying on strict data isolation and access controls to keep each tenant's data secure and invisible to others. In this work, multi-tenancy refers only to shared infrastructure. It does not involve cross-organization training, gradient sharing, parameter mixing, or any form of data pooling across tenants. Every per-organization model is trained exclusively on its own organization’s data.) enterprise search, every organization brings proprietary jargon, domain-specific acronyms, entity relationships, and behavioral patterns that general-purpose language models systematically fail to capture. Bridging this organizational knowledge gap with full-parameter models is intractable at scale and further complicated by challenges unique to the multi-tenant enterprise setting: (i) strict tenant isolation at both training and serving time, (ii) eye-off development workflows that prohibit human inspection of data and customer content, (iii) cross-region data residency constraints, and (iv) scaling per-organization training to hundreds of tenants without linearly increasing inference overhead. We present a scalable system that addresses these challenges through a four-stage pipeline: (1) initialization from a pre-trained cross-encoder, (2) full-parameter masked language modeling (MLM) continual pre-training on an internal first-party corpus, (3) per-organization MLM adaptation via Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) on individual organization document corpora, and (4) joint per-organization LoRA ranking fine-tuning with a feature interaction layer trained on approximately 200 million behavioral query–document pairs. The underlying production infrastructure enforces security and governance (tenant isolation, eye-off development workflows, and data residency). A shared backbone serves hundreds of organizations on one GPU by routing requests to statically compiled organization-specific bundles. Online experiments show a 4.2% improvement in Query Success Rate (QSR) across 200 organizations, with MLM adaptation yielding a further 4.8% QSR improvement over ranking-only within a selected cohort of 20 organizations.

papers.title: TRACE: Accountable Agentic Retrieval for Source Discovery in Digital Archives
papers.abstract: Historical archives pose a difficult retrieval problem for retrieval-augmented generation systems: documents are OCR-degraded, heterogeneous across genres and sources, and require strong source traceability for scholarly and institutional use. We introduce TRACE, a training-free agentic retrieval framework designed for accountable source discovery over historical corpora. The system was developed in the context of DECIDON, an interdisciplinary project on the circulation of political discourse between parliamentary debates and the press during the French Third Republic, involving digitised historical collections and institutional use cases. The prototype is currently deployed internally within the project and accessible to 24 researchers across six partner institutions. We evaluate TRACE on HistoriQA-ThirdRepublic, a benchmark of 1752 French historical questions over parliamentary debates and newspapers from 1887, with documents derived from Bibliothèque nationale de France digitised collections. TRACE achieves R@10 = 0.856 and MRR = 0.653, outperforming sparse, dense, graph-based, and agentic RAG baselines, with the largest gains on multi-hop and cross-corpus questions. At approximately $0.02 per question under the default hosted inference configuration, TRACE also remains economically feasible for heritage institutions, laboratories or companies that cannot rely on costly local GPU infrastructure. These results suggest that, for large digital libraries and archives, retrieval accountability and corpus-aware agent design can provide a practical alternative to heavier training-based or graph-construction approaches.

papers.title: HIRA: A Human-in-the-Loop Retrieval-Augmented Cascade for Document Classification in Regulated Industries
papers.abstract: Document classification in regulated industries is constrained by data residency, limited cold-start labels, scarce review capacity, and costly model-governance procedures. In this setting, the practical goal is not only to obtain high accuracy, but also to reduce LLM calls, avoid frequent model retraining, and send only the most ambiguous cases to human review. We present HIRA, a training-free, on-premises retrieval-augmented cascade for document classification in regulated deployments. HIRA first combines BM25 over OCR text, dense text embeddings, and image-level representations through validation-calibrated weighted reciprocal-rank fusion. Confident documents are classified directly by retrieval. Uncertain or visually confusable documents are passed to a locally hosted LLM verifier, which receives the OCR text, retrieved exemplars, label descriptions, and confusion-specific terms. When the verifier remains uncertain, the document is sent to human review. Each correction is then stored as a margin-weighted retrieval exemplar and also updates a Dirichlet-smoothed confusion graph, allowing the system to improve without updating model weights. On a private 80-class trade-finance corpus, HIRA processes the full 30,233-document production stream while requesting human correction for only 1,945 documents (6.4%), improving Macro-F1 from 0.6218 to 0.8548 . On the corrected Tobacco-3482 benchmark, HIRA reaches 0.9423 Macro-F1 with a locally hosted DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B verifier, 17.4 percentage points above the zero-shot LLM baseline, while invoking the verifier for only about 40% of documents and therefore reducing LLM calls by approximately 60% . With 518 human corrections, corresponding to 24.8% of the pool, HIRA matches the fully labelled pool oracle in which all 2,086 pool documents are indexed with their ground-truth labels. These results show that selective human feedback and retrieval-memory adaptation can provide a practical alternative to repeated model retraining for long-tail document classification in regulated deployments.

papers.title: Delivery Scope Generation for Last-mile Delivery: Fine-grained Urban Area Segmentation, Modeling, and Optimization
papers.abstract: Generating non-overlapping delivery scopes is a fundamental task in last-mile delivery, requiring spatially meaningful and contiguous scopes with scalable optimization. This paper proposes a systematic framework for delivery scope generation. We first develop a fine-grained urban segmentation method that integrates road networks and Areas of Interest boundaries to generate atomic regions and construct a region connectivity graph for modeling spatial adjacency. Based on this representation, the problem is formulated as a graph-based region assignment problem. To enable large-scale planning, we design a tailored heuristic algorithm enhanced by exact local refinement. The framework supports both order-weighted delivery distance minimization and amortized delivery distance optimization via a learning-based estimator. Experiments on real-world data show that the proposed approach achieves near-optimal solutions with low computational cost and scales to mega-city instances with hundreds of stations. The system has been deployed in an online grocery platform with over 1,000 stations, demonstrating its practical effectiveness and industrial value.

papers.title: BasketFormer: Contrastive Masked Language Modeling with Temporal Encoding and Repeat-Explore Gating for Next-Basket Recommendation
papers.abstract: Next-basket recommendation (NBR) in online grocery is a challenging task due to the dual nature of shopping behavior: customers repeat staple items while also exploring novel products. Existing approaches either treat baskets as flat item sets, losing inter-basket temporal structure, or employ sequential models that lack explicit repeat-explore decomposition. We propose BasketFormer, a Transformer-encoder architecture that unifies three complementary innovations: (1) an InfoNCE-based contrastive loss that replaces the full-vocabulary softmax with in-batch contrastive scoring, yielding stronger item representations; (2) a bucketed inter-basket gap encoding that captures purchase cadence through compact learnable embeddings without increasing sequence length; and (3) a repeat-explore gate supervised by the soft repeat ratio that learns to decompose the next-basket representation into repeat and general components. We evaluate BasketFormer on two public benchmarks (Ta-Feng, Instacart) and a large-scale proprietary grocery dataset (71K customers, 3.8M transactions). BasketFormer achieves +9.5% and +7.1% relative Recall@10 improvement over the strongest baseline on Ta-Feng and Instacart, respectively, and +28.0% over TIFU-KNN on the proprietary dataset, while boosting explore-item recall by 17×.

papers.title: Lossless Compression of Proximity Graph Indexes for Efficient Approximate Nearest Neighbors Search
papers.abstract: Graph-based Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) indexes, such as HNSW, are the backbone of modern vector search. However, their massive memory footprint creates a severe infrastructure bottleneck. While vector quantization is widely adopted to reduce the memory required to store data vectors, the graph's edge structure increasingly dominates total memory usage. Compressing these adjacency lists for online search presents a critical system challenge: because decompression occurs during query processing, i.e., while navigating the graph, memory savings cannot come at the expense of query latency. In this paper, we present a compression technique explicitly tailored for live HNSW routing. By applying offline graph permutations to artificially induce structural locality, we enable the use of SIMD-accelerated integer compressors, such as Stream VByte, for rapid on-the-fly decompression. Evaluated across diverse real-world workloads, we significantly outperform the current state of the art in both compression ratio and query latency. Our experimental results show that we achieve compression ratios up to 52.7% with negligible penalties in latency compared to the uncompressed baseline. Furthermore, our technique has been effectively deployed in production at eBay, achieving up to 44.3% reduction in edge storage with no degradation in query latency.

papers.title: MUSE: A Simple Yet Effective Multimodal Search-Based Framework for Lifelong User Interest Modeling
papers.abstract: Lifelong user interest modeling is crucial for industrial recommender systems, yet existing approaches rely predominantly on ID-based features, suffering from poor generalization on long-tail items and limited semantic expressiveness. While recent work explores multimodal representations for behavior retrieval in the General Search Unit (GSU), they often neglect multimodal integration in the fine-grained modeling stage—the Exact Search Unit (ESU). In this work, we present a systematic analysis of how to effectively leverage multimodal signals across both stages of the two-stage lifelong modeling framework. Our key insight is that simplicity suffices in the GSU: lightweight cosine similarity with high-quality multimodal embeddings outperforms complex retrieval mechanisms. In contrast, the ESU demands richer multimodal sequence modeling and effective ID-multimodal fusion to unlock its full potential. Guided by these principles, we propose MUSE, a simple yet effective multimodal search-based framework. MUSE has been deployed in Taobao display advertising system, enabling 100K-length user behavior sequence modeling and delivering significant gains in top-line metrics with negligible online latency overhead. To foster community research, we share industrial deployment practices and open-source the first large-scale dataset featuring ultra-long behavior sequences paired with high-quality multimodal embeddings. Our code and dataset are available at https://taobao-mm.github.io.

papers.title: Sequential Multimodal Evidence Optimization for Product Media Ranking in E-Commerce
papers.abstract: On modern e-commerce stores, customers consume ordered slates of heterogeneous product media—such as images, videos, and 3D renders—before making purchase decisions. Existing media-ranking systems often optimize myopic engagement proxies such as clicks or dwell time, even though product media assets are cooperative informational components of the same item that together help customers find the information they need through sequential interaction. We present Sequential Multimodal Evidence Optimization (SMEO), a two-stage utility-guided framework for customer-oriented media sequencing. SMEO first learns a trajectory utility model from consumed media prefixes to estimate how ordered evidence helps customers reach a purchase decision, while mitigating position-bias and variable-depth imbalance in logged data. Recognizing that customer attention is a limited resource, it then trains an autoregressive ranking policy with survival-weighted reward-to-go that prioritizes the most decision-relevant information early, so customers can find what they need with less effort. By decoupling utility learning from policy optimization, SMEO enables stable offline learning from biased logs and post-hoc media attribution without explicit media-level labels. Evaluated offline on large-scale e-commerce sessions using doubly robust off-policy estimation, SMEO improves estimated conversion by 5.5% and helps customers reach a purchase decision with 15% fewer swipes than existing baselines.

papers.title: Personalized Quality-Aware Reranking for Long-Term User Retention in E-commerce
papers.abstract: Modern recommendation systems are predominantly optimized for short-term engagement signals such as Click-Through Rate (CTR) and Conversion Rate (CVR), often overlooking post-purchase user satisfaction. As a result, ranking systems can repeatedly promote products that drive immediate interactions but lead to poor user experiences and long-term dissatisfaction. We address this gap through a personalized quality-aware reranking framework that explicitly incorporates product quality into the ranking objective. We adopt the Net Quality Detractor (NQD) ratio, the fraction of 1–2 star post-purchase ratings, as a direct measure of severe dissatisfaction that average rating alone cannot capture. Building on this signal, we propose a dual-model architecture: Personalized NQD (PNQD), which estimates user-specific dissatisfaction risk for a user–product pair, and Retention-Driven Alpha (RDA), which adaptively controls the strength of the quality penalty based on a user's historical experience and predicted retention. Offline experiments show that PNQD captures user-level quality preferences beyond product-level signals, while large-scale online A/B experiments demonstrate a 0.48% reduction in realized post-purchase NQD and 0.47% Net Merchandise Value (NMV) uplift over a non-personalized quality baseline, with neutral impact on engagement. The system is fully deployed, serving approximately 200 million monthly active users.

papers.title: LLM-Powered Pipeline for Web Page Classification
papers.abstract: We present a fully automated, end-to-end pipeline for the large-scale multi-label classification of web documents. Our approach addresses the challenge of creating production-ready classifiers without manual annotation while maintaining high classification accuracy. The pipeline combines generative and discriminative ML techniques to construct training datasets and train classifiers without human labeling. A two-stage annotation process generates the training data: semantic dense retrieval pre-selects candidate documents for each category, followed by an LLM-as-a-judge filtering step that achieves near-human annotation quality. A classification model is then trained using the task-specific fine-tuning of a semantic sentence transformer with an MLP head. We evaluate the approach by benchmarking it against the previous production baseline. Each classified pageview contributes to the aggregation of user interests aligned with the IAB Content Taxonomy. These aggregated interests enable the construction of audience segments for advertising applications and serve as features for a downstream ad ranking model. An online A/B test evaluating these system upgrades demonstrates statistically significant improvements in key business metrics (+2.73% CTR).

papers.title: Efficient Frame Selection for E-Commerce Video Analysis
papers.abstract: E-commerce video analysis systems---spanning fulfillment-center (FC) packaging and return-center (RC) unpackaging---face two challenges at scale: transferring and indexing full-resolution video is prohibitively expensive (evidence collection), and downstream Vision Language Model (VLM) inference requires query-specific evidence frames (evidence analysis). We propose a two-stage frame selection approach: Stage 1 is a query-agnostic on-device video summarizer that compresses each video to k keyframes via Determinantal Point Process diversity and Laplacian-variance quality scoring (8× reduction, ?1% of frames transmitted); Stage 2 is a set of domain-adapted per-category relevance rankers fine-tuned with a pairwise RankNet loss on human-verified labels. On product matching at a major e-commerce store, our approach improves over uniform sampling by +13.0pp accuracy and +11.8pp macro F1 at 3 frames, and by +21.6pp accuracy at a single frame---outperforming the best of six recent frame-selection baselines by +18.9pp.

papers.title: CarbonMix: Exploiting Multi-Scale Dynamics in Carbon Flux Forecasting via Lightweight Slow-Fast Decoupling
affiliations: Jiangsu Hengwang Digital Technology Co., Ltd.
industryAffiliations: Jiangsu Hengwang Digital Technology Co., Ltd.
papers.abstract: Carbon flux forecasting is a critical task in large-scale environmental information management, yet extracting actionable predictive knowledge from these datasets remains challenging. The environmental drivers of net ecosystem exchange (NEE) operate on fundamentally different timescales—radiation and turbulent fluxes cycle diurnally, while soil and thermal variables evolve over seasons to years. We present CarbonMix, a lightweight knowledge-driven framework inspired by slow-fast decomposition in dynamical systems theory. CarbonMix separates temporal modeling from cross-variable interaction: a per-variable temporal mixer captures fast periodic patterns (e.g., diurnal cycles), while a low-rank variable mixer captures slow cooperative modes among drivers, conditioned on the current regime via temporal context gating. Spectral analysis across 10 eddy covariance sites confirms that 4 principal components explain approximately 79–84% of cross-variable covariance and that driver timescales span three orders of magnitude—validating the slow-fast prior underlying our design. In our efficiency evaluation on the Weather benchmark, CarbonMix uses 434.4K parameters and 0.07G MACs, remaining substantially smaller than strong multivariate baselines while achieving the best average performance across 10 sites spanning four ecosystem types and competitive performance on public Weather data. We also release a standardized multi-site carbon flux benchmark.

papers.title: Beyond Correlation: Deploying Causal AI to Attribute E-Commerce Sales Loss at Scale
papers.abstract: E-commerce stores struggle to understand the root causes of declining seller revenue, often relying on correlation-based analytics that leads to ineffective or even harmful interventions. This paper introduces the Revenue Loss Monitor (RLM), a system that uses Double Machine Learning (DML) to move from simple correlation to causal attribution of revenue loss. RLM successfully isolates the causal impact of seller-controllable factors, such as pricing, advertising, and inventory - from confounding market trends. Validated across thousands of seller accounts, RLM has demonstrably improved the accuracy of attributions. We discuss the end-to-end methodology, from our hybrid product and seller level modelling approach to the significant real-world challenges of data quality and model validation in a production environment. Online validation with domain experts shows that DML-based attributions are 19.8% more accurate than traditional correlation-based methods, with the system showing 24.9% month-over-month growth in active users. Furthermore, A/B experiments demonstrate that sellers acting on RLM-identified causal factors achieve up to 29% greater revenue recovery compared to a control group, highlighting RLM’s effectiveness as a scalable and trustworthy causal business intelligence solution.

papers.title: eForecaster-MultiRegion: A Deployed Day-Ahead Load Forecasting System for Provincial Grid Operations
papers.abstract: Accurate day-ahead electric load forecasting is critical for secure and economic dispatch of modern power grids. In this paper, we present eForecaster-MultiRegion, a deployed multi-region load forecasting system integrated into the eForecaster platform and serving a major province in Eastern China, covering 17 cities and a population of over 110 million. This setting poses practical challenges including strong regional heterogeneity (e.g., coastal vs. inland consumption patterns) and highly volatile air-conditioning-driven demand under rapidly changing weather conditions. To address these challenges, eForecaster-MultiRegion adopts a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture within a Multi-Task Learning (MTL) framework, enabling the model to share cross-city patterns while specializing to local city-level dynamics. Post-launch results show consistent improvements over the previous production system. After deployment in 2025, eForecaster-MultiRegion achieved 98.29% accuracy in summer and 98.77% accuracy in winter operations, corresponding to +1.41 and +0.68 percentage-point year-on-year improvements, respectively. In this application setting, each 1% absolute accuracy gain corresponds to an estimated RMB 500–800 million in annual economic value. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of eForecaster-MultiRegion for provincial-scale grid operations.

papers.title: Image-Based Feature Engineering for Rapid, Explainable Nanoparticle Megalibrary Screening
papers.abstract: Advanced laboratory techniques have made it possible to synthesize up to tens of millions of nanoparticles on a single chip. Manual analysis at this scale is infeasible, necessitating the development of automated characterization procedures. This work describes the design of a rapid decision framework to perform quality assessment of grayscale nanoparticle images. Key information is extracted from experimental images and used to train decision trees for screening; model inference time is expected to be < 0.3 ms and the median feature engineering time ranges between 12.0 ms and 33.6 ms on the test set. Additionally, model precision is > 91% on all tests, with a maximum precision of 99.3%. Relative to previous studies, this work provides more explainable, interpretable models for automated nanoparticle characterization and returns decisions in a fraction of the time.

papers.title: Hard Rules, Soft Preferences: Bridging Reasoning, Learning, and Optimization for Personalized Packing Checklist Generation
papers.abstract: Packing for air travel is recurring and error-prone: the checklist must be personal and context-aware, yet feasible under safety rules, item dependencies, and luggage limits. Existing packing assistants are template-driven or recommendation-driven but unconstrained, leaving users to deal with regulatory and capacity violations. We propose a reasoning-guided learning framework with three stages: (1) a symbolic engine that generates a regulation-compliant seed checklist with explicit dependency structure, (2) a two-stage preference learner that estimates inclusion and priority utilities from user add and remove actions, mitigating survivorship bias, and (3) a CP-SAT optimizer that selects a compact, feasible subset. On 604 labeled trip scenarios (29K inclusion labels, 343K pairwise comparisons), the symbolic engine attains 99.7% recall and 0.96 rubric validity versus 0.78 to 0.81 for frontier LLMs; gradient boosted trees and LambdaMART reach AUC-ROC 0.943 and NDCG@5 0.923; and CP-SAT attains 100% constraint satisfaction versus 28% for greedy and 10% for random. Deployment of the first two stages in FlyEnJoy, a production iOS travel app, doubled checklist completions and reduced completion time. The proposed architecture provides a general framework for constrained personalization, applicable wherever hard feasibility coexists with subjective preferences.

papers.title: OneMall: One Architecture, More Scenarios — End-to-End Generative Recommender Family for E-commerce at Kuaishou
papers.abstract: In the wave of generative recommendation, we present OneMall , an end-to-end generative recommendation framework tailored for e-commerce services at Kuaishou. Our OneMall systematically unifies the e-commerce's multiple item distribution scenarios, such as Product-card, short-video and live-streaming. Specifically, it comprises three key components, aligning the entire model training pipeline to the LLM's pre-training/post-training: (1) E-commerce Semantic Tokenizer : we provide a tokenizer solution that captures both real-world semantics and business-specific item relations across different scenarios; (2) Transformer-based Architecture : we largely utilize Transformer as our model backbone, e.g., employing Query-Former for long sequence compression, Cross-Attention for multi-behavior sequence fusion, and Sparse MoE for scalable auto-regressive generation; (3) Reinforcement Learning Pipeline : we further connect retrieval and ranking models via RL, enabling the ranking model to serve as a reward signal for end-to-end policy retrieval model optimization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that OneMall achieves consistent improvements across all e-commerce scenarios: +14.7% GMV in Product-Card, +10.3% GMV in Short-Video, and +4.9% GMV in Live-Streaming. OneMall has been deployed, serving over 400 million daily active users at Kuaishou.

papers.title: BAGEL: Behavior and Preference Alignment for Generative Live-Streaming Recommendation
papers.abstract: Generative recommendation represents a paradigm shift through reformulating the recommendation task as an auto-regressive token generation over discrete Semantic IDs (SIDs). However, existing SID-based approaches inadequately capture the temporal dynamics and behavioral discrimination in live-streaming recommendation, primarily due to two critical challenges: (1) dynamic content-behavior misalignment , where static SIDs fail to encode time-varying segment semantics and hierarchical behavioral intensity; (2) reward-agnostic preference alignment , where SID embedding alignment lacks fine-grained reward guidance, resulting in a significant gap between embedding and diverse online business metrics. To address these challenges, we propose a Behavior and Preference Alignment for Generative Live-Streaming Recommendation ( BAGEL ). First, to tackle dynamic content-behavior misalignment, we introduce real-time segment-level alignment that captures product transitions at 30-second granularity during live-streaming. Additionally, we leverage an end-to-end behavior-guided quantization that infuses hierarchical behavioral signals into residual quantization layers, enabling SIDs to integrate dynamic content and encode user preference intensity hierarchically. Second, a retrieval-based preference alignment is developed to tackle reward-agnostic preference alignment, providing multi-dimensional reward signals for end-to-end alignment optimization and advancing preference alignment from the conventional post-training stage into the representation alignment phase. Extensive experiments on industrial-scale datasets and online A/B tests on Kuaishou's local-life service demonstrate the effectiveness of BAGEL.

papers.title: MERGE: Next-Generation Item Indexing Paradigm for Large-Scale Streaming Recommendation
papers.abstract: Item indexing, which maps a large corpus of items into compact discrete representations, is critical for both discriminative and generative recommender systems, yet existing Vector Quantization (VQ)-based approaches struggle with the highly skewed and non-stationary item distributions common in industrial streaming recommenders, leading to poor assignment accuracy, imbalanced cluster occupancy, and insufficient cluster separation. To address these challenges, we propose MERGE, a next-generation item indexing paradigm that adaptively constructs clusters from scratch, dynamically monitors cluster occupancy, and forms hierarchical index structures via fine-to-coarse merging. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MERGE significantly improves assignment accuracy, cluster uniformity, and cluster separation compared with existing indexing methods, while online A/B tests show substantial gains in key business metrics, highlighting its potential as a foundational indexing approach for large-scale recommendation. Codes are available at https://github.com/baiyimeng/MERGE.

papers.title: LLM-based User-Product Relevance Evaluation for Dynamic Product Advertising
papers.abstract: Dynamic Product Advertising (DPA) retrieval systems are a core component of modern e-commerce advertising; however, their evaluation remains challenging. Conventional offline engagement metrics are limited by sparse, biased feedback, while online evaluation is costly and time-consuming. In this work, we propose a user--product relevance metric for offline evaluation of DPA retrieval systems. The metric first compresses the engagement history into a compact set of intent representatives via Semantic-ID-grouped, event-stratified segmentation, then assesses the relevance of a recommended product to each individual intent and aggregates them as a user-level relevance score, yielding a stable and interpretable measure of retrieval quality. To compute this metric at scale, we leverage large language models (LLMs) as semantic relevance judges, capturing nuanced functional and semantic relationships that heuristic methods often miss. We propose an agentic, human-aligned prompting framework that generates multi-category relevance guidelines and distills teacher-model judgments into an efficient student model for scalable evaluation. The resulting metric strongly correlates with offline and online business metrics, enabling faster and more reliable DPA retrieval iteration before A/B testing.

papers.title: SA-RSQ:A Versatile Sparse Representation Framework for Multi-modal Recommender Systems
affiliations: Institute of Software Chinese Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract: Deploying high-dimensional multimodal features in industrial recommender systems incurs substantial storage and latency overhead. Hard quantization is compact but introduces boundary distortion, whereas dense soft quantization couples representation quality to the limited storage budget. We propose Sparse Activation-based Residual Soft Quantization (SA-RSQ), which uses Top-K sparse routing and softmax weights to store compact (Index, Probability) tuples. The stored tuples decouple per-item storage from codebook dimensionality; for a fixed selected support, gradients propagate through the routing weights and weighted reconstruction without relying on a straight-through estimator. Experiments on a proprietary food-delivery advertising dataset show favorable reconstruction-performance and CTR trade-offs across storage budgets of 8-48 bytes per item. A preliminary Next-Distribution Prediction study and a one-week online A/B test further demonstrate the practical potential of SA-RSQ, with relative lifts of +2.51% in CTR and +3.66% in CPM.

papers.title: Generative Pseudo-Labeling for Pre-Ranking with Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Pre-ranking models in industrial recommendation systems face a train--serving discrepancy: they are trained exclusively on exposed interactions yet must score all recalled candidates at serving time, including unexposed items without feedback. This induces sample selection bias that degrades generalization and suppresses long-tail content. Existing remedies introduce new biases of their own, from false negatives in negative sampling to inherited exposure bias in teacher--student distillation and training instability in adversarial domain adaptation. We propose Generative Pseudo-Labeling (GPL), which leverages large language models to assign semantically grounded pseudo-labels to unexposed items. Items are first tokenized into semantic identifiers via a frozen multimodal encoder and a Residual Quantized VAE, after which a fine-tuned language model generates user-specific interest anchors from behavioral histories. Relevance scores are computed by matching these anchors with candidates in a shared multimodal space and calibrated through uncertainty-aware weighting that accounts for semantic dispersion, historical consistency, and generation confidence. The pre-ranker is trained jointly on observed interactions and confidence-weighted pseudo-labels. All language model inference runs offline and is cached per user, imposing zero online latency. Deployed on a large-scale industrial platform, GPL achieves a 3.07% CTR lift in online A/B testing while improving recommendation diversity and long-tail coverage.

papers.title: TelecomAudit: Origin-Aware Benchmark Auditing and Calibration for 5G Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Modern wireless networks support reliability-critical applications, from industrial automation and autonomous mobility to UAV connectivity, making anomaly detection critical for 5G and self-optimizing 6G operations. Yet labeled telecom faults are rare, costly to annotate, and difficult to release, so telecom anomaly detectors are trained and evaluated using injected, generated, or simulated anomalies. This raises a deployment question: can strong synthetic-benchmark performance be trusted for detector selection? Rather than assuming synthetic anomalies are valid proxies for deployment-relevant faults, we ask whether benchmark anomalies cover KPI regimes occupied by controlled-real faults, and we operationalize this question as origin-aware benchmark auditing: a deployment-oriented evaluation workflow that conditions evaluation on anomaly origin. Across two public 5G/Open RAN testbed corpora, the audit exposes a failure hidden by aggregate metrics: synthetic-only training can retain strong performance on synthetic anomalies while missing controlled-real fault regimes under deployment-relevant operating conditions. We provide evidence that this failure reflects an operating-regime coverage gap rather than a model-specific limitation or feature leakage, and that modest controlled-real calibration improves controlled-real detection where additional synthetic or normal data, and synthetic reweighting do not. We release a reproducible audit toolkit and artifacts, and an operator checklist for deployment-oriented benchmark validation, together with industrial validation as a pre-production shadow-mode CI gate within Nokia's anomaly-detection pipeline.

papers.title: ThreatLens: Evidence-Guided Ranking of High-Priority CVEs
papers.abstract: Security teams must prioritize vulnerabilities before exploitation evidence is complete. Existing signals, such as CVSS, EPSS, advisories, and public exploits, are useful but fragmented and time-sensitive; retrospective rankings can therefore overstate performance by using evidence unavailable at decision time. We present ThreatLens, a simple yet effective and deployment-realistic framework for CVE prioritization. ThreatLens ranks vulnerabilities at each review point using only cutoff-valid evidence and learns from future CISA KEV entries as weak supervision for exploitation relevance. Under forward-in-time, CVE-disjoint evaluation, ThreatLens significantly outperforms CVSS, EPSS, and rule-based evidence-fusion baselines. On the held-out test split, ThreatLens surfaces 80.0% of future KEV CVEs in the top 20, over three times EPSS at the same budget, and reaches 95.9% in the top 50. Early-warning analysis further shows that ThreatLens identifies a substantial fraction of subsequent KEV entries before formal catalog inclusion, supporting timely, evidence-grounded triage.

papers.title: Routing Patient Messages in Primary Care Using Explainable Ontology-Guided Large Language Models
affiliations: Shenkar College of Engineering, Design and Art
papers.abstract: Accurately routing patient-generated messages is a major challenge in primary care, where clinicians must manage large volumes of unstructured text. In this work, we propose a novel method for message routing in family medicine that integrates large language models (LLMs) with a domain-specific clinical ontology. Developed in close collaboration with pharmacists and physicians, the ontology encodes textual indicators relevant to message routing decisions. We incorporate this ontology by leveraging two LLMs, aiming to improve routing accuracy while generating natural language explanations that clarify the rationale behind each decision, thus enhancing primary care experts' trust in the system. We evaluate our method using a large-scale dataset from a healthcare provider, comprising a substantial volume of patient messages. This setting introduces an additional challenge, as the messages are written in Hebrew, a morphologically rich language. Despite this complexity, our results show high classification accuracy alongside high-quality, interpretable explanations. We further evaluated the proposed method in a real-world online setting, demonstrating its practical value for supporting message triage in clinical practice.

papers.title: MTUKG: A Multi-scale Temporal Urban Knowledge Graph Dataset for Knowledge-Enhanced Spatiotemporal Prediction
affiliations: Changchun University of Science and Technology
papers.abstract: Integrating multi-source knowledge into urban knowledge graphs (UrbanKGs) has shown strong potential for improving urban spatiotemporal prediction (USTP). However, existing public UrbanKGs are often misaligned with the temporal and multi-scale nature of USTP. First, they usually represent urban facts as static triples, ignoring when facts become valid, expire, or change over time. Second, their functional-zone layers are typically derived from static POI clustering, which overlooks spatial boundaries, activity interactions, and event-driven temporal semantics. As a result, current datasets provide limited support for modeling temporally valid knowledge and its cross-scale effects on prediction. To address these limitations, we propose MTUKG, a multi-scale temporal urban knowledge graph dataset. MTUKG represents urban events as time-interval facts, enabling knowledge to be aligned with specific prediction windows. It further introduces a spatial unit-driven method that integrates spatial morphology, semantic distributions, spatial decay effects, and dynamic events to construct temporal functional zones and establish multi-scale temporal associations across micro, meso, and macro urban scales. Experiments on USTP and knowledge reasoning tasks demonstrate that MTUKG significantly enhances predictive performance and provides a structured knowledge resource for modeling the temporal dynamics, functional evolution, and multi-scale dependencies in urban systems. The dataset and source code are available at https://github.com/Jiahaohuhu/MTUKG.

papers.title: StreamFuels: A Dynamic Resource for Time Series Benchmarking in Fuel Analytics
papers.abstract: Fuels and petroleum derivatives (e.g., gasoline, diesel, and kerosene), remain essential energy sources for transportation systems, industrial operations, and residential use. Historical data on fuel sales, production, and pricing, typically represented as time series, enable tasks such as demand forecasting, pattern discovery, and anomaly detection, supporting data-driven decision-making in transportation logistics, production planning, and price regulation. However, these efforts are often hindered by the lack of accessible, well-structured datasets. To address this gap, we present StreamFuels, an open-source Python library that serves as a dynamic benchmarking resource for time series mining in the fuel sector. StreamFuels programmatically retrieves the most recent data from official government sources at access time, delivering five curated datasets with over 40,000 time series. The data are cleaned, standardized, and provided in the TSF format, ensuring compatibility with popular time series toolkits. We validate the resource by benchmarking state-of-the-art algorithms across three tasks: forecasting, classification, and pattern analysis (i.e., motif and discord discovery). Our results establish reproducible performance baselines and demonstrate the utility of StreamFuels for advancing research on time series mining and data-driven applications in the fuel sector.

papers.title: Daily52: An Air-exposed Smell Dataset for Real-world Odor Classification
papers.abstract: Previous gas-sensing datasets were designed and collected in sealed environments primarily for laboratory research or domain-specific applications. The lack of air-exposed settings limits the study and modeling of the gas properties under natural volatilization. This work bridges this gap by building an unsealed gas-sensing dataset for real-world gas classification, dubbed Daily52 , collected from 52 everyday items measured using a self-developed electronic nose (e-nose). We thoroughly benchmark various odor classification models as baselines, among which InceptionTime is found to achieve an impressive 88.24% accuracy in recognizing items. Comprehensive analysis further demonstrates that our dataset is high-resolution and effective for studying the olfactory modality. Potential olfactory research is also discussed beyond our dataset. To our knowledge, this is the first dataset that enables benchmarking methods for classifying real-world gas-sensing data of natural volatiles.

papers.title: LEMMA-RCA: A Large Multi-modal Multi-domain Dataset for Root Cause Analysis
papers.abstract: Root cause analysis (RCA) is crucial for enhancing the reliability and performance of complex systems. However, progress in this field has been hindered by the lack of large-scale, open-source datasets tailored for RCA. To bridge this gap, we introduce LEMMA-RCA, a large dataset designed for diverse RCA tasks across multiple domains and modalities. LEMMA-RCA features various real-world fault scenarios from Information Technology (IT) and Operational Technology (OT) systems, including microservices, water distribution, and water treatment systems, with hundreds of system entities involved. We evaluate the performance of six baseline methods on LEMMA-RCA across various settings, including offline and online models, as well as single and multi-modal settings. Our study demonstrates the utility of LEMMA-RCA in facilitating fair evaluation and promoting the development of more robust RCA techniques. The dataset is publicly available at https://www.lemmarca.info.

papers.title: MemeChain: A Multimodal Cross-Chain Dataset for Meme Coin Forensics and Risk Analysis
papers.abstract: The meme coin ecosystem has grown into one of the most active yet least observable segments of the cryptocurrency market, characterized by extreme churn and widespread fraudulent behavior. While countless meme coins are deployed across multiple blockchains, they rely heavily on off-chain web and social infrastructure to signal legitimacy. These very signals are largely absent from existing datasets, which are often limited to single-chain data or lack the multimodal artifacts required for comprehensive risk modeling. To address this gap, we introduce MemeChain, a large-scale, open-source, cross-chain dataset comprising 34,988 meme coins across Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Solana, and Base. MemeChain integrates on-chain data with off-chain artifacts, including website HTML source code, token logos, and linked social media accounts, enabling multimodal and forensic study of meme coin projects. By providing cross-chain coverage and rich off-chain context, MemeChain serves as a foundational resource for research in financial forensics, multimodal anomaly detection, and automated scam prevention in the meme coin ecosystem.

papers.title: NRCD: An Open Database of Collegiate Running with Unified Performance Standardization
affiliations: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
papers.abstract: Collegiate running in the United States generates thousands of race results annually in cross country and track and field, yet no large-scale dataset has been publicly available for research. Existing websites such as Athletic.net, MileSplit, and TFRRS host results but do not support bulk download, restricting prior analyses to ~500 performances, often skewing studies toward male athletes. We introduce the National Running Club Database (NRCD) , the first openly available collegiate running dataset at scale: 143,868 approved performances from 31,351 athletes across 1,423 meets in four sports (cross country (XC), indoor and outdoor track, and road races), 36.2% women, spanning 2003-2026. Meets from August 2023 onward carry comprehensive course distance, elevation gain and loss, weather at race time, and track venue metadata (99.9% of XC rows with weather fields). NRCD is community-governed through open submission and expert approval and is maintained as a live database whose meet volume has grown yearly. We release a unified performance standardization framework that operationalizes established distance, elevation, and heat adjustments in one pipeline; XC-only validation ; heat is a Hadley-band heuristic. We recommend gender-stratified modeling . On XC, full standardization lowers median within-athlete cross-meet variability by 51.1% (women) and 35.4% (men) versus raw times. We release the dataset and pipeline with a Python package `nrcd' under FAIR principles, supporting longitudinal athlete modeling, environmental-confounder studies, and gender-equity research in collegiate sport.

papers.title: CT-bias: A Dataset for Auditing the Impact of Patients' Sensitive Information on Clinical Trial Matching
papers.abstract: Medical advances are rooted in insights gathered from clinical trials. Technology plays a key role in clinical trial recruitment: patients use specialised platforms to search for clinical trials, and clinical trial recruiters search through patient records to find eligible patients. Existing research shows that personal characteristics of patients influence the outputs of models tasked with medical question answering. While similar classes of neural models are increasingly present in medical information-seeking pipelines, the scientific community lacks resources to investigate how well these models cope with bias in medical retrieval tasks. Here, we present CT-bias, a novel resource for auditing of bias for specific patients and groups of patients where private or sensitive information was recoded as a part of a medical note. To create the dataset, we perturb patient notes from an established patient-trial matching benchmark by inserting specific patient information (sexual orientation, occupation, education level) irrelevant to their medical condition. In an example experiment, we study the impact of this information on the retrieval results of 12 leading open source zero-shot dense retrieval models. We also propose a methodology to inspect models for biases, and observe that, while most models are generally robust to medically irrelevant information, some patient characteristics impact the retrieval results more than others. CT-bias will a useful resource to evaluate future ranking models and CT matching pipelines while the dataset creation protocol itself can be extended to several retrieval and prediction biomedical AI tasks.

papers.title: APEX-VW: A Document-Level English-Spanish Post-Editing Dataset in the Healthcare Domain
papers.abstract: Post-Editing (PE) of Machine Translation (MT) output often involves repeating the same lexical and terminological corrections across many segments, especially in specialised and highly repetitive documents. Despite substantial work on Automatic Post-Editing (APE), most available corpora operate at the sentence level, others are synthetic, and overall not designed to study how corrections propagate in realistic Computer-Assisted Translation (CAT) workflows. This paper presents the APEX-VW (Automatic Post-Editing eXperiments on Virtual Wards) Corpus, a new open English-Spanish (EN-ES) dataset built from recent NHS virtual-ward documents and professional PE in Trados Studio, with controlled MT, terminology, and quality assurance settings. The corpus contains seven document-coherent source texts totalling 42k words, translated with four MT systems representing different paradigms and then post-edited by professional translators. Unlike prior resources such as WMT APE corpora, eSCAPE, MLQE-PE, or LangMark, the dataset preserves document order and CAT-tool context, making it suitable for research on terminology normalisation, correction propagation, and human-in-the-loop translation support. The paper describes the corpus design, data preparation, PE setup, and initial corpus statistics, and positions the resource as a benchmark for document-level APE and propagation-aware assistive tools.

papers.title: RecDistillery: A Framework for Teacher-Student Knowledge Distillation in Recommender Systems
papers.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) improves the efficiency of recommender systems by transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student architectures. Despite its growing popularity, KD research for recommendation remains fragmented, making reproducibility and fair comparison across distillation strategies difficult. We present RecDistillery , the first open-source, model-agnostic framework for standardizing teacher–student KD workflows in recommender systems. The framework provides a modular architecture unifying data preparation, teacher integration, student training, distillation, and evaluation. It supports both native PyTorch-based recommenders and externally trained models, enabling heterogeneous teacher–student distillation within a unified pipeline. RecDistillery facilitates both the reproduction of existing KD methods and the rapid prototyping of new approaches through reusable losses, data loaders, metrics, and configuration modules. We demonstrate its capabilities through representative case studies involving multiple recommendation frameworks and externally imported teachers. The framework code, documentation, and demo examples are publicly available at https://github.com/sisinflab/RecDistillery.

papers.title: FranKGraphBench: Reproducible Benchmarking for Knowledge Graph-based Recommendation
affiliations: Computer Science and Mathematics Institute, University of São Paulo
papers.abstract: Knowledge Graphs (KGs) enable the integration of data across multiple domains and data types, supporting human interpretability, machine processing, and distributed data access. KGs have become especially valuable for enhancing recommender systems (RSs), which provide personalized user experiences and are now ubiquitous across platforms such as social media, streaming services, e-commerce, news, and search engines. However, reproducibility remains a persistent challenge in developing and evaluating machine learning methods for KG-based RSs, due to heterogeneous data sources and model complexity. Therefore, we introduce FranKGraphBench, a modular benchmarking framework that consolidates baseline models, datasets, and evaluation metrics into a standardized structure. Users can define experiments via configuration files, enabling reproducible sharing of model specifications, datasets, and evaluation settings. FranKGraphBench contains 6 KG-form RS datasets: 3 DBpedia-enriched, 1 Wikidata-enriched, and 2 unenriched. Finally, we validate its effectiveness through a small benchmark and an ablation study to showcase its capabilities and the importance of open settings for reproducible experimentation.

papers.title: OffTrail: A Benchmark for Natural-Language Context in Recommendation beyond Interaction Histories
papers.abstract: Recommender systems are increasingly expected to combine interaction histories with language. In many cases, a user's next choice may depend on a temporary situation—such as their current mood, plans, or constraints—that is not visible in past behavior. Existing benchmarks, however, mostly evaluate average next-item accuracy, broad instruction following, or content understanding; they do not isolate recommendation episodes in which external situation context is plausibly needed. We introduce OffTrail, a benchmark built on MovieLens for situation-aware recommendation beyond interaction histories. It contains two complementary families of episodes: observed off-trail choices that are real user transitions but hard to infer from prior behavior, and neighbor-supported alternative continuations that represent plausible futures for similar recent histories. Each episode packages a user history, target item, item metadata, and generated life-situation context. The contexts are treated as plausible external circumstances rather than ground-truth user intentions. OffTrail supports controlled evaluation across sequential models, LLM-based recommenders, and hybrid systems by keeping the recommendation episode fixed while exposing or withholding the situation context. By releasing the artifacts, construction pipeline, and evaluation protocol, OffTrail provides a reproducible testbed for studying whether natural-language context improves ranking when interaction history is weak or ambiguous. Benchmark: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20560655.

papers.title: Eval4Sim: An Evaluation Framework for Persona Simulation
papers.abstract: Large Language Model personas, explicit profiles specifying a user's attributes, preferences, and behavioural tendencies, are increasingly used to simulate human conversations for user modelling, social reasoning, and behavioural analysis. Evaluating whether such simulations faithfully reflect human conversational behaviour is critical, yet current practice often relies on LLM-as-a-judge approaches that provide limited grounding in observable behaviour and produce opaque scalar scores. We present Eval4Sim, an evaluation framework that measures alignment between simulated and human conversations across three dimensions: adherence, whether persona traits are recoverable from dialogue via dense retrieval; consistency, whether a persona maintains a distinguishable stylistic identity via authorship verification; and naturalness, whether conversations exhibit human-like turn-to-turn flow via dialogue NLI. Unlike optimization-oriented metrics, each dimension takes a human corpus as a reference baseline and penalizes deviations in both directions, distinguishing insufficient persona encoding from over-optimized, unnatural behaviour. The framework is corpus-agnostic: any persona-annotated conversational dataset can serve as the reference. Evaluated over ten simulation corpora, Eval4Sim surfaces systematic trade-offs invisible to single-score methods.

papers.title: Ishigaki-IDS-Bench: A Benchmark for Generating Information Delivery Specification from BIM Information Requirements
papers.abstract: Building Information Modeling (BIM) projects increasingly use Information Delivery Specification (IDS) to formalize information requirements in a machine-checkable XML format. Because IDS conditions are grounded in the Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) vocabulary, authoring them requires expertise in IFC concepts, validation tools, and property set conventions. Existing benchmarks for structured generation do not adequately capture the additional burden of vocabulary conformance and external-validator agreement that IDS imposes. We present Ishigaki-IDS-Bench, the first publicly released benchmark for IDS generation from BIM information requirements. The benchmark contains 166 examples spanning 83 practical scenarios authored in Japanese and English by six BIM/IDS experts, each paired with a gold IDS file and metadata covering input format, turn setting, target IFC versions, and construction domain. Evaluation proceeds in two stages: (i) formal validity scored by the buildingSMART IDSAuditTool along Processability, Structure, and Content, and (ii) content fidelity scored by facet-level macro-F1 against the gold IDS. Across 10 LLMs in zero-shot, the highest Facet F1 is 65.6%, achieved by GPT-5.5, while the highest Content pass rate is only 33.1%, achieved by Claude Opus 4.5. Ishigaki-IDS-Bench is released on Hugging Face (DOI 10.57967/hf/8873) under CC BY 4.0, and the evaluation code is released on Zenodo (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20550510) under Apache-2.0.

papers.title: BWOR: A Bilingual Benchmark for Modeling and Solving Operations Research Problems from Natural Language
papers.abstract: We introduce BWOR, a benchmark of 82 textbook-style operations research (OR) problems with bilingual Chinese–English statements, verified numeric answers, and execution-based evaluation. It tests whether a large language model (LLM) can turn natural-language OR descriptions into executable solver code and correct solutions. Baselines distinguish non-reasoning, reasoning, and decomposed-agent systems. The release includes data, evaluation scripts, prompts, and baseline summaries for reproducible comparison.

papers.title: Geese Belong in (Data) Lakes: An Index Lake for Anserini
papers.abstract: We present an index lake for Anserini: a remote index representation of all inverted indexes from Anserini's reproducibility suite. Each index is represented as a set of Parquet files on remote object storage, and retrieval is performed through SQL with DuckDB. Through an extensive benchmark of 239 experiments across 50 collections, we empirically confirm our results are consistent with Anserini's. We analyze query latencies over the index lake and conclude that (1) most experiments can be run relatively efficiently, requiring only a couple of seconds per query; and (2) for large collections and learned sparse indexes, queries suffer from increased latency due to high overhead. We are also able to reduce total network transfer, since (1) index lakes are smaller than the corresponding prebuilt Lucene indexes; and (2) up to 90% of the index can be skipped by pushing filters on the postings table to the data lake. The index lake increases reproducibility and makes it easier to run new experiments on standard test collections and prebuilt indexes.

papers.title: RISE: A Rust Library for Inverted Index Search Engines
papers.abstract: Inverted indexes are a crucial data structure for efficient information retrieval in large text corpora. They enable fast full-text search by mapping each term to the documents in which it appears, on top of which efficient algorithms quickly retrieve the documents relevant to a user query. We present RISE, a novel inverted index library implemented in Rust, designed to deliver high performance and efficiency for information retrieval tasks. RISE leverages Rust's safety and performance to provide a robust solution for building and querying inverted indexes, while offering accessible extensibility through its expressive trait system. While developing RISE, we revisited the inverted-index literature, thereby reproducing numerous prior works using this new test bench. We evaluated RISE against existing libraries, demonstrating competitive query performance across various datasets and workloads, with some algorithms achieving speedups of up to 2× over the current state of the art. Our results indicate that RISE is a promising tool for researchers and practitioners in the field of information retrieval.

papers.title: PosIR: A Multilingual Benchmark for Diagnosing Position Bias in Information Retrieval
affiliations: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
papers.abstract: Position bias—the systematic effect of where key information is located on retrieval effectiveness—is a critical concern in information retrieval. Although recent studies have identified such bias in dense retrievers, existing analyses focus predominantly on monolingual English, fail to disentangle document length from information position, and lack a standardized framework for controlled evaluation. To address these limitations, we introduce PosIR, a benchmark to systematically diagnose position bias across diverse retrieval scenarios, comprising 310 language–domain dataset combinations spanning 10 languages and 31 domains. Each query is paired with a positive document, a localized reference span, and positional metadata, enabling controlled analysis of retrieval quality across evidence locations and length bins. PosIR provides a complete data generation pipeline with quality-control filtering, along with baseline evaluation scripts. Experiments with 10 widely-used dense retrievers reveal that position bias is pervasive in both multilingual and cross-lingual retrieval, and that it intensifies as documents grow longer. PosIR serves as a foundational resource to advance the development of position-robust retrieval systems.

papers.title: QFR-RAG: A Multi-Level Evaluation Resource for Grounded RAG over Technical-Medical Documentation
papers.abstract: Technical-medical documentation poses a challenging setting for grounded retrieval-augmented generation (RAG): valid answers often depend on exact thresholds, workflow constraints and combinations of documented conditions. However, existing RAG benchmarks rarely provide the fine-grained evidence, completeness, citation, abstention and safety annotations needed to evaluate such behaviour. We introduce QFR-RAG, a multi-level evaluation resource for grounded RAG over Quantitative Flow Ratio (QFR) documentation for cardiology software used in angiography-based assessment of coronary disease.
