QFR-RAG comprises a 400-question benchmark: 50 technical extraction questions with reference answers and gold evidence, 50 multi-evidence questions annotated with 103 required evidence slots and 278 atomic answer nuggets and 300 paired adversarial questions targeting nonsensical requests, false premises and unsafe relaxation of documented constraints. Its layered evaluation protocol separates retrieval sufficiency, exact correctness, nugget-level completeness, citation grounding, abstention and safety-preserving refusal or correction, revealing empirically distinct failure modes across retrieval and generation. As a baseline validation, we benchmark retrieval pipelines and general-purpose and medically specialised language models of different sizes, showing that strong performance on exact technical extraction does not imply complete multi-evidence answering. QFR-RAG provides a deeply annotated framework for evaluating grounded, complete and safety-aware RAG in controlled technical-medical software documentation and illustrates an annotation design that can be adapted to similar parameter-dense domains.

papers.title: ReCaRe: A Bilingual Benchmark for Revision Candidate Retrieval in Evolving Legal Corpora
papers.abstract: Document corpora in organizational and public settings evolve as statutes, policies, specifications, and knowledge bases are revised. Maintaining such corpora requires identifying documents that should be inspected after a change, yet this candidate-identification step has not been directly addressed by existing benchmarks. We formalize this problem as Revision Candidate Retrieval (RCR) : retrieving documents for expert inspection and possible revision. RCR consists of two complementary tasks: Rat2Rev , which retrieves articles given an amendment rationale, and Rev2Rev , which retrieves co-revised articles given an observed revision. To study RCR, we introduce ReCaRe , a bilingual benchmark built from EU and Japanese legislative amendments, containing 91,361 EU articles and 90,170 Japanese articles. Our analysis shows low lexical overlap, length asymmetry, and implicit cross-article revision relationships. Experiments show that BM25 remains a strong first-stage baseline, long-context dense retrievers improve recall, zero-shot listwise LLM reranking improves Rat2Rev rankings, and document expansion and dense-retriever domain adaptation provide complementary first-stage gains.

papers.title: Lexskill: A Systematic Chinese Legal Skill Framework with High-Quality Annotations and an Execution Harness
papers.abstract: Agents in knowledge-intensive domains require not only knowledge retrieval, but also the skills to effectively use retrieved knowledge. Since domain knowledge is often highly complex, agents must possess strong reasoning capabilities in order to perform tasks effectively. In the legal domain, different legal systems exhibit substantial differences, and the reasoning logic for applying legal knowledge varies significantly across systems. Meanwhile, existing skill collections lack a systematic skill framework grounded in domain knowledge, limiting their scalability and extensibility. To address these challenges, we present LexSkill, a reasoning-oriented legal skill library for the Chinese legal system. Within this framework, legal experts construct 36 atomic skills, further organized into 180 sub-atomic skills and 2 compound skills. Since legal problem solving also requires grounded access to legal resources and coordinated reasoning across multiple steps, we further introduce Chinese-Law-Harness, which augments the skill library with MCP modules built over a case repository and a statutory repository, and incorporates a multi-agent system for skill orchestration and execution. Evaluations on existing legal AI benchmarks show that leveraging the skill library through the proposed harness significantly outperforms direct problem solving without structured support, verifying the effectiveness of our skills and harness.

papers.title: MOSAIC: Unveiling the Moral, Social and Individual Dimensions of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in sensitive applications including psychological support, healthcare, and high-stakes decision-making. Existing evaluation benchmarks rely almost exclusively on Moral Foundation Theory (MFT), neglecting other key dimensions such as social values, personality traits, and individual characteristics that shape human ethical reasoning. We introduce MOSAIC , the first large-scale benchmark designed to jointly assess the mo ral, s ocial, a nd i ndividual c haracteristics of LLMs. MOSAIC comprises nine validated questionnaires drawn from moral philosophy, psychology, and social theory, alongside four platform-based games designed to probe morally ambiguous scenarios, totaling over 600 curated items. We validate the benchmark across six models from different families, providing empirical evidence that MFT alone is insufficient for comprehensive ethical evaluation of LLMs. All resources are publicly available.

papers.title: RV-FLS: A Resource for Retrospective Verification of Forward-Looking Statements
papers.abstract: Forward-looking statements (FLSs) influence decisions before their outcomes are known, yet they are rarely revisited systematically after relevant evidence becomes available. Retrospective verification of FLSs differs from conventional fact verification because supporting or contradicting evidence may emerge gradually, remain inaccessible, or be insufficient for a responsible judgment. We introduce RV-FLS, a resource for retrospective verification of scenario-level FLSs derived from financial analyst reports. RV-FLS contains 651 human-reviewed instances. Each instance links an original statement and publication date to post-publication evidence collected within a five-year verification window, an evidence-grounded rationale, an agent-generated judgment, a human review decision, and a final label. We construct the resource through an agent-first workflow in which a retrieval-augmented language model assembles evidence packages and proposes preliminary judgments for human adjudication. As standalone label predictors, a closed-book model and a retrieval-augmented agent achieve accuracies of 26.5% and 42.5%, respectively. Under agent-first construction, however, reviewers accept 74.5% of the generated judgments, while average verification time decreases from 12.89 to 3.34 minutes per scenario. RV-FLS supports research on evidence retrieval, evidence-conditioned classification, and end-to-end retrospective verification, while providing an auditable foundation for making future-oriented claims more transparent and accountable.

papers.title: SemiHS-Bench: A Semiconductor Benchmark for HS6 Classification from Sparse ERP-Style Text
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for product classification in trade compliance and supply-chain analytics. Their potential for Harmonized System (HS) classification is substantial, especially for automating six-digit code assignment over industrial records. One persistent challenge is input sparsity: enterprise systems often expose terse descriptions, abbreviated bill-of-material entries, or bare part numbers, forcing models to recover product identity before classification. Existing HS datasets rely on richer customs rulings, shipment descriptions, or synthetic product text, and cannot isolate this operational regime. To this end, we propose SemiHS-Bench, a benchmark for HS6 classification of semiconductor supply-chain products from real ERP-style text. Specifically, each product is represented through controlled input tiers derived from the same observation, with labels grounded in a held-out multilingual corpus of customs rulings. We evaluate LLM baselines on constrained and open classification, showing substantial degradation under sparse inputs. The benchmark, ruling corpus, and evaluation tools are available online at https://github.com/cti-iel/SemiHS-Bench.

papers.title: GESIS KG: Enhancing Discovery, Interoperability and Reusability in Social Science Research through Knowledge Graphs
affiliations: GESIS - Leibniz Institute for the Social Sciences, Cologne
papers.abstract: Effective discovery and reuse of scholarly resources require machine-readable, semantically linked metadata - yet no knowledge graph exists that integrates the full range of social science scholarly resources. We present the GESIS Knowledge Graph (GESIS KG) a large-scale domain-specific knowledge graph interlinking and transforming social science metadata into an AI-ready knowledge graph to improve interoperability and automated discovery across global research ecosystems. Built on the GESIS KG Ontology, extending established vocabularies, the graph captures not only scholarly metadata but also the provenance of semantic link between these resources. GESIS KG supports semantic search, provenance-aware citation tracking, and metadata reuse through a SPARQL endpoint, OAI-PMH API, and bulk download. The resource is publicly available under CC BY 4.0 license at https://doi.org/10.7802/2969.

papers.title: TE4 RS: Toward End-to-End Explanation Evaluation for Recommender Systems
papers.abstract: Explanations in Recommender Systems (RS) play a crucial role in enhancing transparency, trust, and user satisfaction. Benchmarking such explanations, however, is not trivial, as existing evaluation frameworks typically do not assess all explanation stages (i.e., generation, abstraction, formatting, and communication) or evaluate them in isolation. In this paper, we present TE4 RS, an end-to-end explanation evaluation framework for RS that assesses explanation methods across all four stages: generation, abstraction, format, and communication. It contains 20 explanation methods covering seven categories and 31 evaluation metrics. We also integrate large language models to format the explainers' abstract outputs and to serve as proxy evaluators for human evaluation. TE4 RS allows to set up an evaluation pipeline that mimics a specific application scenario and compares multiple explanation methods, thereby fostering a holistic, structured evaluation of RS explanations. The code can be found at: https://gitlab.ifi.uzh.ch/DDIS-Public/te4-rs.

papers.title: A Resource for Evaluating Creative Search on the Infinite Index
affiliations: University of Kassel, hessian.AI and ScaDS.AI
papers.abstract: Iterative generative systems can refine generated content, such as images or text, based on an initial prompt and user feedback. Iterative refinement helps users solve creative tasks that cannot be addressed reliably through ad-hoc prompt engineering alone. However, reproducible evaluation of such systems is challenging because user interactions induce branching during annotation. We propose a method for formulating topic descriptions for interactive scenarios, inspired by classic Cranfield-style topics. We also provide guidelines for creating reproducible topics that pose meaningful challenges to the evaluated systems and build a dataset of abstract concepts that are used to formulate topics on the domain of creative image generation. We formulate a workflow for the validation of these topics and enable the evaluation of current and future iterative generative systems.

papers.title: LLMJudge: Meta-Evaluating Automatic Relevance Judgments
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to produce the relevance labels that underpin the evaluation of information retrieval (IR) and retrieval-augmented generation systems. Yet delegating relevance assessment to an LLM raises a meta-evaluation question that is hard to answer with existing resources: when, and how much, can we trust an automatic judge? We present LLMJudge, a resource for meta-evaluating LLM-generated relevance judgments. LLMJudge collects 42 complete judgment sets over the TREC 2023 Deep Learning track, spanning fine-tuned, proprietary, and open-source models and a wide range of prompting strategies. Each judgment set is paired with official human qrels, enabling two complementary axes of analysis: label agreement with human assessors (e.g., Cohen’s κ, Krippendorff’s α) and system-ranking fidelity (e.g., Kendall’s τ, Spearman’s ρ). Beyond the data, we release a standardized format, baselines, and an evaluation harness so that new judges can be plugged in and compared reproducibly. Our analysis shows that high label agreement is neither necessary nor sufficient for faithful system ranking, that open-source judges are markedly more stable than proprietary ones, and that fine-tuning improves correlation at the cost of reliability. LLMJudge is publicly available and provides a reusable testbed for auditing the judges who increasingly judge our systems. Full resources, data, and detailed results are available at https://llm4eval.github.io/LLMJudge-benchmark/.

papers.title: LEDGER: A Long-Context Benchmark of Corporate Annual Reports for Grounded Financial Retrieval and Extraction
papers.abstract: Finance reporting is a natural proving ground for large language models, and the very-long-context capabilities of recent models across all sizes make rigorous evaluation in this domain an increasingly pressing need. Yet most public financial resources reduce the task to plain-text SEC 10-K filings paired with a handful of question–answer items. We release Ledger (Long-context Evaluation of Documents for Grounded Extraction and Retrieval), a corpus of 4,999 digitized corporate annual reports — full documents with figures, tables, and narrative, not just regulatory filings. Each report is labeled with 31 consolidated financial KPIs to be extracted and linked to the market's reaction at the earnings date. From this data we derive three evaluation benchmarks spanning the difficulty spectrum: a pure page-level KPI retrieval task with TREC-style relevance judgments over 118,048 questions in natural language, a conversational “needle-in-a-haystack” single-value lookup, and a full KPI extraction task, both from long, numerically dense reports. We additionally provide human OCR-quality annotations with inter-annotator agreement and the complete extraction, validation, and scoring toolchain. We further demonstrate the dataset's research utility with a case study linking CEO-letter rhetoric to post-publication market impact. An extension to 291 French ESEF filers (1,153 reports with 24 KPIs) augments the corpus.

papers.title: RedditPersona: A Modular Framework for Community-Conditioned LLM Adaptation from Reddit
affiliations: Future Computing Group, University of Oulu
Centre for Applied Computing, University of Oulu
papers.abstract: Community-conditioned language model adaptation needs choices about data collection, community definition, and evaluation that are currently made independently in each study, making it hard to compare assumptions or reuse artifacts. We present RedditPersona, a modular framework that standardizes these choices: it collects Reddit posts and comments, profiles active users, partitions them under five grouping strategies (subreddit-based, graph-structural, semantic, hybrid, and interaction-based), trains a parameter-efficient adapter per strategy via QLoRA, and evaluates them under a shared metric suite spanning fluency, fidelity, distributional alignment, and community identifiability. Applied to 112 subreddits in the urban well-being domain (301,429 user profiles, 16M+ comments), we find that adapters' behavioral identifiability tracks each strategy's agreement with the subreddit baseline, and that a consistent trade-off between identifiability and distributional similarity to real text holds across all five strategies. The code and configuration files are available at: https://github.com/Ahghaffari/redditpersona.

papers.title: Ground Penetrating Radar Dataset for Indoor Pipeline Detection
papers.abstract: Locating pipelines embedded in walls indoors or buried underground outdoors using ground penetrating radar (GPR) data, especially the B-scan images, is a widely adopted non-destructive testing method. However, existing open-source datasets in this field are typically limited in scale or lack ground-truth annotations for pipelines. To address these limitations, we present P-GPR, a GPR dataset specially collected for pipeline detection tasks. The dataset was collected using two GPR devices following a two-stage data acquisition scheme: pipeline ground-truth information was first collected during the construction phase when the pipelines were exposed, and GPR data were subsequently acquired from the wall surfaces after construction was completed. This dataset covers representative indoor pipeline installation conditions, including water pipes and electrical conduits embedded in reinforced concrete walls and concrete block walls. Furthermore, to validate the value of the dataset, we annotate the data and conduct pipeline experiments using commonly adopted object detection methods. The associated data (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20575661) and code (https://github.com/aiiseverything/P-GPR-Dataset) have been made publicly available.

papers.title: REMEDI: A Benchmark for Retention and Unlearning Evaluation in Multi-label Clinical Disease Inference
papers.abstract: Clinical language models are trained on patient records that hold sensitive information, and patients can ask for their data to be removed under the right to be forgotten. Retraining from scratch for each request is too costly, so machine unlearning aims to erase specific records from a trained model instead. Yet, unlearning methods are mostly evaluated on synthetic, non-medical data, leaving their behaviour on real clinical records unknown. We introduce REMEDI, a benchmark for machine unlearning in multi-label clinical disease classification, built from real MIMIC-III patient records. REMEDI defines three forget-set scenarios of increasing severity, from single-patient deletion to bulk removal, and evaluates both utility and privacy through membership inference. We benchmark four unlearning method families on two biomedical models, and we find a clear utility-privacy trade-off and show that methods succeeding on small deletions collapse under large-scale forgetting, an effect that correlated disease labels make worse. We release REMEDI publicly to support reproducible research on clinical unlearning. (Code and extended version: https://github.com/anuragiiser/REMEDI)

papers.title: A Benchmark & Dataset for Detecting AI-Manipulated Visual Evidence in the Court System
papers.abstract: Photographic evidence is becoming increasingly vulnerable to forms of alteration and fabrication that existing legal and technical workflows are not well equipped to evaluate. Surveillance frames, dashcam stills, and phone photographs may be used to establish presence, sequence, causation, damage, or identity, yet contemporary generative systems allow non-experts to alter or fabricate such images through ordinary prompt-based interfaces. Existing image-forensics benchmarks provide important resources for face manipulation, classical tampering, and general synthetic-image detection, but they are not organized around the forms of visual evidence submitted in courts, the localized edits that can change what an exhibit appears to prove, or the consumer-tool threat model now facing the justice system. We introduce the CIFAR Synthetic Evidence Corpus for Detecting AI-Manipulated Images, a benchmark for evidentiary image authentication in court and justice-system contexts. The corpus contains 1,505 photographic items, including 720 authentic controls and 785 manipulated or fabricated images, spanning surveillance, dashcam, and consumer-photo imagery. Manipulations are organized into scene-condition edits, localized element edits, and full fabrications produced with contemporary generative systems. Each item is released with structured metadata covering source provenance, manipulation tier, subtype, generator, prompt template, and scene attributes, enabling controlled evaluation beyond aggregate binary detection. We also establish state-of-the-art baselines with publicly available image-manipulation detectors, showing that current systems exhibit error profiles that remain problematic for evidentiary use. The dataset, prompts, metadata manifest, code, and baseline evaluation scripts are released to support research on visual evidence authentication, information integrity, and trustworthy AI for the justice system.

papers.title: NewsReX: An Open-Source Multi-Framework for Neural News Recommendation
papers.abstract: Reproducing and comparing results in neural news recommendation research remains difficult due to fragmented codebases, inconsistent preprocessing pipelines, and tight coupling between models and deep learning frameworks. We present NewsReX (https://github.com/igor17400/NewsReX), an open-source framework that unifies multiple neural news recommendation models across two ML backends (PyTorch and JAX/Flax). Models are defined through a structured YAML specification that captures architecture, training recipe, and data contract, decoupling model definition from framework-specific implementation. A Hydra-based configuration system enables composable experiments with single-command framework switching. We provide cross-framework parity tests to verify numerical consistency across backends, allowing researchers to reproduce results from the original implementations and then transfer experiments to their preferred framework. We report comprehensive experiments on the MIND-small benchmark with multiple seeds per model and per framework, and demonstrate multilingual generalization by training on a proprietary Japanese news dataset from Nikkei News (https://nikkei.com/). We also publish pre-trained model weights on Hugging Face (https://huggingface.co/newsrex/) so that researchers can build on existing results without redundant retraining, reducing both computational cost and energy consumption. All source code, experiment configurations, and trained model weights are publicly available.

papers.title: Coverage Under Contradiction: A Benchmark for Negation-Aware Retrieval
papers.abstract: Coverage-evaluation benchmarks quantify whether retrieved evidence covers the different pieces of information needed to satisfy an information need. Existing benchmarks mostly consider factual claims that may already be known to pretrained retrieval components, leaving open whether retrievers find corpus evidence when it contradicts those priors. We study how retrievers behave when their parametric knowledge and the information in a corpus disagrees. To do so, we develop a process to augment a nugget-based coverage benchmark with controlled contradictions. For each nugget, we create a negated counterpart and edit its supporting documents to support that negation while preserving the context. Applying this process to CoverageBench, a benchmark measuring information coverage, we create CoverageBench-Negate, spanning six datasets and roughly 63,000 original-edited evidence pairs (one per nugget-document link). We attach rich construction metadata to every pair and additionally provide out-of-family LLM judgments over all pairs and a human audit of a sample. In baseline experiments, BM25 separates original from edited near-twin evidence substantially better than dense retrievers (Qwen3 and Jina), which stay near chance. We release the benchmark on Hugging Face Datasets (nuggets, documents, pairs) together with the construction materials, including the prompts used to create it.

papers.title: WCI: The Web Context Interface for Agentic Web Automation
affiliations: TIB - Leibniz Information Centre for Science and Technology
papers.abstract: Web agents struggle to interact with complex web environments designed for humans, forcing them to reverse-engineer visual and Document Object Model (DOM) structures. This discrepancy results in high token costs, hallucinated interactions, and slow runtimes, rendering reliable, large-scale web automation computationally and economically unviable. We aim to establish a machine-readable interaction layer that allows site operators to define bounded, token-efficient action spaces for web agents explicitly. We propose the Web Context Interface (WCI), a browser-native framework for agentic web automation. WCI enables site operators to expose structured interaction contracts using lightweight semantic HTML annotations and policy files, shifting web automation from a confrontational parsing paradigm to a cooperative, operator-driven ecosystem. As a comprehensive resource, we release: (1) The core WCI library, (2) An open specification for agent-directed site policies, and (3) A dataset comprising 50 multi-step task grounding scenarios across diverse web interfaces. We evaluate WCI's infrastructural utility via a static component-level grounding study across six LLMs. The WCI representations reduce token consumption by up to 8.2x. WCI also increases the success rate of target grounding from 0% on raw HTML to at least 76% for smaller open-source models, and achieves up to 96% for larger proprietary models. WCI is fully documented and open-source as an extensible foundation, lowering the economic barrier for researchers and practitioners to develop, evaluate, and deploy reproducible agentic web interaction layers at scale.

papers.title: TempBench: A Temporal Knowledge-Graph QA Benchmark with Per-Question Gold Subgraphs and Retrieval-Quality Metrics
affiliations: aivancity School of AI & Data for Business & society
papers.abstract: Temporal knowledge-graph question answering (TKGQA) asks systems to answer questions whose correct answer depends on when the question is asked. Existing TKGQA benchmarks ship answer strings (CronQuestions, MultiTQ, MusTQ) or, in the closest prior work (TimelineKGQA), per-question positive context facts scored by ranking - but none release per-question typed negatives or score retrieval by subgraph precision/recall against time-valid gold. We present TempBench, an 8,710-question multi-hop TKGQA benchmark over a Wikidata-derived temporal KG. Every question ships a gold supporting subgraph S* and - uniquely in this setting - same-(s,r) distractor and same-(s,r,o) stale-fact negatives (functional for 71.5% and 81.3% of questions; the interval x stale cell is structurally absent at 8.1% since interval answers are years; per-question flags released), across a 4x3 temporal-operator x hop-complexity matrix, scored by two answer-independent subgraph metrics (Temporal Retrieval Precision and Chain Consistency Rate) grounded in a forward-propagating temporal composability operator we formalise. These metrics expose retrieval quality that end-task exact-match conflates: at matched 2-hop architecture, removing the temporal filter collapses Chain Consistency Rate from 0.84 to 0.13, and deepening retrieval from two to three hops lifts 3+-hop chain coverage from 0.014 to 0.476 (paired McNemar p<10^-19 on n=143) - a retrieval gain whose end-task counterpart is single-seed-large but multi-seed-marginal. We release the benchmark, pipeline, annotation protocol, and per-question functional-negative flags.

papers.title: SwahiliNLU: A Broad-Domain Intent and Slot-Filling Dataset with Pragmatic Tone Annotations for Low-Resource NLU
papers.abstract: We present SwahiliNLU , a broad-domain intent recognition and slot-filling dataset for Swahili natively constructed by native speakers. The dataset comprises 3,633 utterances spanning 10 domains, 175 intent classes and 105 slot types, annotated with BIO slot labels and enriched with a three-way pragmatic tone annotation layer ( imperative , polite , conversational ) validated on a 10% double-annotated subset with a compound Cohen's κ = 0.87 across intent, tone and slot annotations, a dimension absent from prior Swahili and African-language intent datasets to our knowledge. While prior African language intent benchmarks exist, SwahiliNLU is distinguished by its broader intent taxonomy, mobile virtual assistant focus for East African urban contexts, and unique tone annotation layer. We establish baselines across intent classification, tone classification, slot filling, and zero- and 5-shot LLM evaluation using Claude Sonnet, GPT-4o mini, and Gemini 2.5 Flash. Fine-tuned SwahBERT achieves the best intent Macro-F1 of 0.55, while AfroXLMR leads tone classification at 0.9474, with all fine-tuned models exceeding 0.93 and substantially outperforming zero-shot LLMs (best 5-shot LLM: 0.85). Tone Macro-F1 exceeds 0.87 in every domain for all fine-tuned models, confirming pragmatic register is a uniformly learnable signal. These findings highlight the value of task-specific annotation for pragmatic phenomena in low-resource languages. All data, code and baseline models are released at https://github.com/alfredkondoro/swahili-nlu-intent-evals and the dataset is archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20521261.

papers.title: GQA-Q2Q: A Large-scale Benchmark for Entity Ambiguity Resolution in Visual Question Answering
papers.abstract: Vision-language models achieve remarkable results on various visual question-answering benchmarks. However, they struggle with ambiguous questions where the target entity is unclear. To address this issue, it is essential to construct a benchmark dataset that pairs ambiguous questions with entity-grounded clarifying sub-questions. This paper presents GQA-Q2Q, a large-scale dataset for resolving entity ambiguity in visual question answering via entity-grounded clarifying sub-questions. GQA-Q2Q is constructed through a template-assisted human annotation pipeline. The pipeline generates candidate sub-questions from attribute, relation, and position templates and asks human annotators to verify, select, or revise them. As a result, GQA-Q2Q contains 46,554 human-verified clarifying sub-questions with target-instance grounding. This paper also presents a proposed ambiguity-resolving VQA model that leverages the generated sub-questions before producing final answers. The experimental results show that the proposed model outperforms zero-shot and ambiguity-resolving vision-language baselines. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/gminipark/GQA-Q2Q.git.

papers.title: FoodVitals: A Diagnostic Benchmark for LLMs on Nutritional Literacy, Nutrient–Health Relations, and Food Safety
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly fine-tuned and deployed for nutrition and food-related advisory roles, yet their foundational food knowledge is rarely audited before deployment. We introduce FoodVitals, a public benchmark of 1,158 verified items spanning three high-stakes aspects of food knowledge: nutritional literacy, nutrient–health relations, and food safety. Each aspect is grounded in an authoritative source (USDA, EFSA, USDA FSIS), and the benchmark uses multiple answer formats (multiple-choice (MCQ), Yes/No (Y/N), short answer, and ranking) to characterize model performance across these aspects and assess within-aspect format sensitivity. Evaluating six instruction-following LLMs reveals two consistent patterns: (i) models that correctly identify the highest-nutrient food in a multiple-choice setting show markedly weaker ranking and uneven threshold-checking on the same nutrients, revealing a gap between coarse-grained nutritional knowledge and precise magnitude reasoning; and (ii) food-safety performance varies substantially across answer formats even when all formats draw from the same regulatory topic set, meaning a high score in one format does not reflect uniform competence across that topic area. Together, these patterns show that single-format evaluation gives an incomplete picture of where an LLM is unreliable and motivate multi-format auditing before high-stakes food deployment.

papers.title: SIDInspector: A Mapping-First Diagnostic Resource for Semantic-ID Tokenizers
papers.abstract: Semantic-ID (SID) tokenizers define the item address space consumed by generative recommenders. Yet their exported mappings remain difficult to inspect consistently before downstream training. We introduce SIDInspector, a mapping-first diagnostic resource that exposes coverage gaps, full-code aliasing, behaviorally weak prefixes, tail compression, and prefix fan-out. Its adapter contract normalizes item mappings, metadata, interactions, and optional generator traces; validation checks the resulting artifact; and mapping-level probes characterize utilization, aliasing, neighborhood alignment, popularity allocation, and structural cost. Optional interfaces extend the resource to temporal churn and generator traces. We evaluate SIDInspector on four tokenizer lines with explicit provenance. A same-item Musical study compares controlled GRID-style RQ-KMeans exports at two capacity settings with a bounded ReSID/GAOQ export; released LETTER and LC-Rec mappings test the contract on official item-index artifacts. The larger-budget GRID-style row has D2 full-code aliasing of 0.779, versus 0.977 for the width-64 row, while ReSID/GAOQ reaches 0.000. The D3 ordering differs: a deterministic category-prefix control reaches 0.447 versus 0.055–0.154 for the learned exports. Together, these results distinguish capacity, addressability, and behavioral alignment at the artifact level. Across additional datasets, D3 varies under the same category-prefix control. A bounded fixed-reranker probe links D3 to candidate exposure; ranking quality is assessed downstream.

papers.title: Route Me If You Can: A Benchmark for Query Reformulation Selection
papers.abstract: LLM-based query reformulation can improve retrieval, but no single reformulation strategy is consistently optimal across queries, domains, retrievers, or model backbones. This creates an inference-time decision problem: “Given an original query and a pool of candidate reformulations, which one should be issued to the retriever?” . Existing studies are hard to compare because they use different reformulator pools, retrievers, relevance signals, training labels, and evaluation metrics. We introduce QueryRoute, a benchmark that freezes the expensive artifacts needed to study this decision reproducibly: original queries, generated variants, ranked lists under multiple retrievers, retrieval scores, and per-query oracle labels. The benchmark contains 3,757 queries, 11 candidate systems, five reformulator backbones, and three retrievers across TREC DL, BEIR, and BRIGHT, yielding 619,905 retrieval outcomes. We benchmark supervised classification, routing, QPP, and LLM-as-judge selectors. Results show substantial oracle headroom over fixed reformulators, but current selectors recover only part of it; selector rankings change across retrievers, and similar mean effectiveness can hide different query-level behavior. The released artifacts and evaluation harness allow future selectors to be compared without regenerating variants, rerunning retrieval, or rebuilding judge pipelines. Code and data are available at https://github.com/haisonle001/QueryRoute.

papers.title: WiCleanData: Guaranteeing the Type Consistency of Wikidata by Taxonomy Refinement and Constraint Enforcement
affiliations: Télécom Paris, Institut Polytechnique de Paris
papers.abstract: Because of its collaborative nature, Wikidata suffers from errors, inconsistencies, and excessive complexity, such as redundant classes, ambiguity between instances and classes, wrong taxonomic paths, and type constraint violations. The manual curation of these issues is infeasible at scale. To address these challenges, we introduce WiCleanData , a refined version of Wikidata with a consistent taxonomy and free from type constraint violations. Specifically, we have designed an automated pipeline that first cleans the taxonomy with language model assistance, then simplifies type constraints by hierarchical aggregation, and finally filters facts accordingly. The resulting knowledge graph, free from any type violation, is made publicly available via a Web interface, enabling easy exploration and downstream applications.

papers.title: The EMN Country Factsheets Structured Dataset
papers.abstract: Each year, the European Migration Network (EMN) country factsheets deliver an overview of key migration and international protection developments within all EMN Member States and observer countries. The factsheets include both a textual component and a visual component. In this paper, we introduce a curated dataset of the textual component of these reports over 35 countries and 13 years (2012-2024.) The dataset was created to facilitate European-level research on migration policies and developments, and promote the use of reliable sources about migration in data science and media research, particularly at a time when the spread of online misinformation about migration constitutes a serious issue. The dataset transforms the original document texts into a tabular format, with columns corresponding to country, year, section, subsection, content, and harmonized title section. We illustrate the value of the dataset with concrete analyses and propose envisioned applications and uses of the dataset. The dataset is accessible through a DOI link.

papers.title: GeoBenchLLM: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs on Geo-Related Tasks
papers.abstract: In the context of geodata, existing Large Language Models have often been studied in a homogeneous setting, which has considerably limited insights into their generalization capabilities. In this paper, we present GeoBenchLLM, a comprehensive benchmark for probing LLMs on geo-related tasks. We leverage a careful selection of twelve publicly available datasets from diverse geo-related tasks and domains, and evaluate a set of LLMs on geo-spatial and temporal understanding using our benchmark. Our results show that reasoning and size have a strong impact on overall performance. GeoBenchLLM is publicly available at https://github.com/Rfr2003/GeoBenchLLM.

papers.title: SWXAI: A Unified Multimodal Explainability Library for Space Weather Forecasting and Heliophysics
affiliations: Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory
papers.abstract: Space weather forecasting and heliophysics increasingly rely on machine learning models that process heterogeneous inputs such as multi-viewpoint multi-wavelength solar images and rasters, multivariate time series, spatial annotations, and tabular event-level data. However, explainability workflows remain fragmented across libraries, model interfaces, and output formats, limiting reuse and reproducibility. We present SWXAI, an open-source library that unifies explainable AI (XAI) workflows for image, time-series, and tabular data in space weather forecasting and heliophysics. SWXAI provides a common, extensible interface across commonly used vision, time-series, and tabular learning models, with validation, adaptation, and persistent explanation objects. It also includes domain-grounded examples, reproducible notebooks, tests, and documentation, enabling users to inspect outputs, swap models or explainers, and extend workflows to new heliophysics datasets. SWXAI reduces modality-specific engineering overhead and supports comparable, reusable explanations across heterogeneous scientific machine learning pipelines. A benchmark against direct backend implementations shows that SWXAI substantially reduces the code users write to produce an explanation, with no practical runtime cost.

papers.title: CFX-Bench: A Benchmark for Counterfactual Explanations
affiliations: University of Modena and Reggio Emilia
papers.abstract: Counterfactual explanations support model interpretability by identifying actionable recourse strategies, yet their evaluation remains fragmented across metrics, baselines, and experimental protocols. This paper introduces CFX-Bench, a unified benchmarking suite for comparing counterfactual explanations for tabular classification across datasets, models, and explainers. The framework integrates quantitative and qualitative metrics, local and global explanation methods, and LLM-based components for verbalization and human-centered assessment. By combining standardized benchmarking with semantic evaluation, CFX-Bench provides a reproducible environment for analyzing the quality, reliability, and coherence of counterfactual explanations, while supporting the development of new explanation methods.

papers.title: Real-Time Adaptive Tour Recommendation with Agentic AI
papers.abstract: Tour-recommendation systems, including the recent wave of LLM-based travel planners, typically stop at plan generation: given a user request, they produce a single itinerary and stop. Once the trip starts, however, tourists are left to handle disruptions such as rain, growing queues, transit breakdowns, or user fatigue. We present AdaptTour, an agentic system that continues replanning after departure; its contribution is the overall control architecture. Mid-trip signals (weather, queue length, transit disruption, user fatigue, and free-text feedback) are fused into a single context snapshot, typed triggers pass through a debounced registry, and a replanner locks the executed prefix and re-optimises the tail, re-enforcing every constraint at each pass: money budget, accessibility, per-member vetoes and boosts, and carbon preference. The LLM is used only to score candidates, with a deterministic fallback for omitted candidates, and to generate the rationale presented to the traveller; selection, sequencing, routing, and constraint checking remain deterministic. Weather is live, while crowd, transit, and fatigue are simulated for the demonstration and explicitly labelled as such in the interface. The system provides a curated five-city catalogue of POIs (Singapore, Melbourne, London, New York, Paris), per-city fare tables, five travel modes, and OSRM-routed map polylines cached on disk for offline-capable visualisation. Source code, tests, and JSONL scenario traces are publicly available to support reproduction.

papers.title: XAnnoRank: A Comprehensive Web-Based Framework for Evaluating Explainability in Rankings
papers.abstract: XAnnoRank is a web-based framework designed to support explainability studies in rankings via user-centered evaluation. XAnnoRank provides an easily adaptable user interface (UI) that enables systematic assessment of explainability methods by presenting ranked lists with and without explanations, while collecting both implicit and explicit user feedback. Its flexibility facilitates diverse user design, including different explanation types, datasets, ranking models, and researcher-defined configurations. The tool has been successfully demonstrated and validated in a high-stakes domain through a study on explainability in recruitment conducted as part of the EU-funded FINDHR (https://findhr.eu/) project. (https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101070212) By streamlining the UI setup, XAnnoRank reduces implementation efforts and enables reproducibility across studies. The code and documentation (https://github.com/ClaraRus/AnnoRank/tree/XAnnoRank) are publicly available, together with a demonstration video (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yHJLbgGNaxs).

papers.title: TabClaw: An Interactive and Self-Evolving Agent for Spreadsheet Manipulation and Table Reasoning
affiliations: State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, University of Science and Technology of China
papers.abstract: Spreadsheets and tables are used representations for structured data analysis, but effective analysis still requires substantial manual effort and domain expertise. Recent large language model (LLM) agents can automate parts of this process, but they provide limited transparency into intermediate decisions, rely on implicit assumptions, struggle with multi-table comparison, and repeat workflows without adapting to a user's preferences. This paper presents TabClaw, an open-source interactive AI agent for spreadsheet manipulation and table reasoning. Users upload CSV or Excel files and issue natural-language requests; TabClaw clarifies ambiguous intent, exposes an editable execution plan, streams a ReAct-style tool-using analysis loop, dispatches specialist agents for parallel multi-table reasoning, and synthesizes findings with explicit consensus and uncertainty markers. Beyond one-off analysis, TabClaw records completed workflows, extracts persistent user memory, distills reusable skills from repeated tool-use patterns, supports package-style skill import, and versions external skills after repeated failures. Experiments on spreadsheet manipulation and table reasoning benchmarks show that TabClaw improves executable task completion and reasoning performance while preserving an inspectable user workflow. This paper shows how TabClaw turns spreadsheets and tables into inspectable analytical workflows while personalizing itself to recurring data-analysis tasks across diverse real-world data-analysis settings. Our code is available. (https://github.com/ustc-table-mining/TabClaw)

papers.title: MADClean: Statistical Profiling and Multi-Agent Large Language Model Reasoning for Automatic Data Cleaning
papers.abstract: High-quality data is essential for effective decision-making, data analytics, and training machine learning models. Numerous data cleaning tools and systems have been proposed in both academia and industry. Several recent tools utilize Large Language Models (LLMs), but most rely entirely on their unverified reasoning capabilities, struggling to effectively handle dirty datasets with heterogeneous error types. In this demo, we describe MADClean, a tabular data cleaning system that uses statistical profiling and a multi-agent architecture to achieve strong performance in several data cleaning tasks. MADClean uses dedicated LLM agents to recommend cleaning operations, generate executable source code, and iteratively verify and improve its outputs. We show that MADClean reliably handles dirty data across three real-world data cleaning scenarios, and scales to datasets with hundreds of thousands of rows in our evaluation.

papers.title: SMBench: No-code Benchmarking of Deep Entity Resolution
affiliations: L3S Research Center at Leibniz University Hannover
National and Kapodistrian University of Athens
papers.abstract: Entity Resolution (ER) is typically addressed through the Filtering-Verification framework. Despite numerous existing techniques, there is currently no interactive system that allows users to experimentally explore, compare, and understand the combined impact of Filtering and Verification under realistic conditions. We present SMBench, the first open-source, no-code web application for end-to-end ER that unifies Filtering and learning-based Verification in a single workflow. Unlike existing ER tools that focus on one step in isolation, SMBench allows for studying how candidate generation affects downstream matching under realistic conditions, while also exposing runtime, memory, and effectiveness trade-offs through an interactive interface. The demo will enable users to configure complete ER pipelines with a few selections, compare alternative methods on the same dataset, and inspect the resulting candidate pairs and predictions to understand why certain pipelines succeed or fail. Given that our system is modular and containerized, the same workflow can be reused for new datasets and methods with minimal effort, making SMBench useful both as a research benchmark and as a practical exploratory tool.

papers.title: PROBE-Web: An Interactive System for Probing Evaluation Landscapes of Knowledge Graph Completion Models
papers.abstract: Knowledge graph completion (KGC) models are commonly evaluated using rank-based metrics such as MRR and Hits@K, despite different users often requiring different evaluation perspectives. In this demo, we present PROBE Web , an interactive system for probing diverse evaluation landscapes for KGC models. PROBE Web enables users to flexibly evaluate KGC models by adjusting two critical perspectives: (P1) predictive sharpness and (P2) popularity-bias robustness . Through a user-friendly GUI, users easily evaluate multiple KGC models and analyze their strengths and weaknesses. PROBE Web provides four key functionalities: (1) conventional evaluation toolkit, (2) flexible perspective-aware evaluation, (3) explainable case studies, and (4) evaluation landscape exploration. We believe that PROBE Web can help users better understand KGC models aligning with their objectives.

papers.title: SearchLog: A Web Browser Extension for Capturing Search Logs in Laboratory Studies
papers.abstract: Natural search logs are valuable for studying search behavior in information seeking settings. We present SearchLog, an easy-to-install web browser extension for collecting natural search logs during lab-based studies. SearchLog enables participants to search the open web in a browser while recording structured interaction data from the mouse, keyboard, search activity, and browser state modules. The extension captures clicks, scrolling, hovered text, typed words, search queries, result rankings, AI-generated summaries when available, tab activity, and window changes. A local Flask backend stores each session as an ordered JSON event stream, including HTML snapshots and preprocessed search result data for later analysis. These logs can be used to derive measures such as query reformulation, page visits, dwell time, scroll behavior, tab switching, search path complexity, and exposure to AI-generated search content. By supporting natural browser-based search with structured experimental metadata, SearchLog provides a reusable resource to study search behavior across traditional and AI-enhanced search interfaces. SearchLog is available at https://github.com/peanutH/SearchLog-chromium-extension.

papers.title: VietCheckMed: A Scalable Retrieval-Augmented Engine for Zero-Day Regulatory Oversight
affiliations: University of Science, Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City
University of Information Technology, Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City
papers.abstract: The exponential growth of adversarial multimedia in digital advertising poses a critical regulatory challenge, where malicious actors exploit cross-modal semantics to obfuscate unauthorized physical interventions. Conventional fact-checking systems, constrained by static weights and modality bias, suffer from legislative concept drift and multimodal camouflage. We present VietCheckMed, an interactive, retrieval-augmented platform that operationalizes training-free causal reasoning for high-throughput regulatory oversight. Architected as a dynamic Knowledge-as-a-Service (KaaS) ecosystem, it circumvents model retraining via dynamic axiom injection and hybrid retrieval. To dismantle cross-modal evasion, the backend orchestrates the MM-RegCheck algorithm, employing Training-Free Bayesian Evidence Aggregation (TF-BEAR) to mathematically isolate visual violations against retrieved statutory constraints. By synergizing a 9B-parameter backbone with advanced API context caching, VietCheckMed achieves a state-of-the-art 0.898 Macro-F1 score while aggressively amortizing inference costs to approximately $0.0004 per sample, establishing a highly scalable, economically viable blueprint for next-generation RegTech.

papers.title: TabgenQA: A Platform for Non-Relational, Multi-Tabular, Numerical QA Benchmark Generation and LLM Evaluation
affiliations: University of Modena and Reggio Emilia
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used for tabular data analysis, but their performance often does not transfer from standard Table QA benchmarks to real-world settings, where tables are typically non-relational , with hierarchical headers, merged cells, inconsistent units, noise, and implicit cross-table dependencies. We present TabgenQA, an interactive system for generating verifiable non-relational multi-table QA benchmarks and evaluating LLMs on them. Users configure domain-specific benchmark settings, inspect and refine generated instances, and compare API-based or locally deployed models through live leaderboards and error analysis views. Across procurement, failure diagnosis, and benchmark curation scenarios, TabgenQA provides an end-to-end workflow for deployment-oriented assessment of LLMs on real-world tabular data.

papers.title: TSGuard: A Real-Time Framework for Detecting and Imputing Missing Data in Streaming Time Series
affiliations: University of Hassiba Benbouali of Chlef
papers.abstract: Streaming sensor applications routinely suffer from delayed or missing observations caused by faults, communication losses, or environmental interference. Although recent imputation methods exploit temporal and spatial dependencies effectively, most either assume offline access to future observations or prioritize throughput without enforcing domain plausibility. We present TSGuard, a real-time demonstration system for monitoring, validating, and imputing missing values in streaming time series. TSGuard combines a lightweight graph-aware temporal imputation model with constraint-aware validation, fallback estimation, and operator-facing explanations. Rather than treating imputation as an isolated prediction task, TSGuard integrates it into a broader data-quality loop: detect problematic observations, impute missing values, validate estimated against physical and spatial constraints, and either retain the original value as a plausible anomaly or replace it when it violates domain constraints. Using environmental sensing as a motivating setting, the demo enables users to inspect delayed sensors, compare imputers, define constraints, and validate flagged values in real time. The combination of lightweight online spatiotemporal imputation, domain-aware validation, and explicit retain-or-replace decisions is our central contribution, while interactive explanations make these decisions inspectable and actionable. for operators.

papers.title: AwareML: Transparent, Controllable, and Sustainable Streaming AutoML
papers.abstract: Streaming AutoML has emerged as a powerful paradigm for building adaptive machine learning pipelines over non-stationary data, yet existing frameworks remain largely opaque: users cannot inspect why a framework was selected, how it responds to concept drift, or what its computational and environmental cost is. This opacity prevents domain experts from making principled deployment decisions and limits trust in automated model selection, particularly in resource-constrained, fairness-sensitive, or interpretability-critical settings. To address this, we developed a preference-aware meta-learning recommender that translates user-defined objectives into structured profiles for pre-run algorithm selection across accuracy, runtime, energy, and CO2 criteria. In this demonstration, we introduce AwareML, a web-based interactive platform that unifies five streaming AutoML frameworks—AutoStreamML, AutoClass, EvoAutoML, OAML, and ChaCha—under a single dashboard for transparent, controllable, and sustainable comparison. AwareML enables users to specify optimisation goals in natural language via LLaMA 3, monitor live temporal performance and concept-drift adaptation, inspect online fairness behaviour, receive streaming-window SHAP and LIME explainability summaries, and track energy and CO2 sustainability indicators via CodeCarbon. A usability study with 25 participants confirms an 80% task-completion rate across six representative tasks, with 73.3% of users reporting improved confidence in model-selection decisions, demonstrating AwareML's potential as a practical tool for transparent, fair, and sustainable streaming AutoML deployment.

papers.title: AgentPDM: Context-Driven Agentic Reasoning for Predictive Maintenance
papers.abstract: Predictive Maintenance (PDM) uses sensor signals to assess machine health and guide actions such as continued operation, monitoring, or repair. Existing data-driven classifiers and knowledge-driven condition-monitoring tools each capture only part of the expert diagnostic workflow, which also requires reasoning over sensing modality, operating context, bearing geometry, spectral signatures, model uncertainty, and maintenance implications. LLM/VLM agents offer a way to coordinate these heterogeneous inputs, but free-form fault prediction remains unreliable. We present Agentpdm, an interactive multi-agent system for context-aware bearing diagnosis. It combines a four-backbone signal ensemble, bearing-physics tools, structured visual evidence, a conservative Decision Agent, and fixed-label report generation. Agentpdm proposes fault hypotheses, verifies them against operating context, spectral evidence, and model disagreement, and then accepts, overrides, or escalates the diagnosis before reporting. On cross-domain scenarios from CWRU, HUST, and Paderborn, Agentpdm improves accuracy from 84.3% to 87.7% with zero correct-to-wrong regressions. These results show that LLM/VLM agents are most reliable in industrial PDM when embedded in a bounded diagnostic workflow rather than used as unconstrained fault predictors.

papers.title: Map of Science: Charting Worldwide Open Scientific Literature
papers.abstract: The increasing pace of scientific production makes tracking worldwide research trends and emerging fields a nearly Sisyphean task. To tackle this challenge, we develop the Map of Science, a visualization tool for analyzing clusters of global research to support identification of emerging scientific and technological areas. To build our tool, we group more than 144 million scholarly articles from 197 countries into over 91,000 research clusters using citations and text embeddings. Along with regularly updating research clusters as new scientific articles are published, we add LLM-enabled summarization, filtering capabilities, and extreme growth predictions. We visualize the resulting clusters in the interactive, publicly available Map of Science tool, available at https://sciencemap.eto.tech/. The tool demonstrates usability and monthly usage increases, with improved modularity, topic separation, entity resolution, and searching and sorting capabilities. The Map of Science and our clustering code are available for public use, and a short video demonstration is available https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EbTIqLgC3sY.

papers.title: ManipulativeAgent: A Multi-Agent System for Generating Interactive Mathematical Manipulatives
affiliations: Guangdong Institute of Smart Education, Jinan University
papers.abstract: Virtual interactive manipulatives help elementary students transition from concrete to abstract mathematical thinking through hands-on digital activities. However, creating them requires both pedagogical and programming expertise, while existing platforms only offer fixed templates that cannot adapt to individual teaching needs. We present ManipulativeAgent, a multi-agent system that allows teachers to create customized manipulatives from natural language descriptions of their instructional goals, with human-in-the-loop checkpoints for review and revision at each stage. Rather than relying on a single large language model (LLM) for end-to-end generation, ManipulativeAgent distributes the task across specialized agents that collaborate through a shared component library of pre-tested virtual tools. This design separates pedagogical reasoning from code implementation, enabling each agent to focus on its strength while the component library ensures interaction reliability. Evaluation on 40 real teaching scenarios shows improvements over commercial platforms and general-purpose LLMs, with the largest gain in interaction richness. A user study with 89 frontline teachers from 15 provinces shows that 92.1% would continue using the system for lesson preparation. A demonstration video is available at https://youtu.be/7eclhXhRy0A.

papers.title: Flagger: A Platform for Operationalizing AI-Driven Early Warning Predictions to Find Personalized Interventions Faster
papers.abstract: Student attrition in higher education remains a critical problem. While existing literature has began to explore automated inference of students at risk of adverse academic outcomes, flagging and intervention diagnosis remains tenuous in practice due to the tedious manual processes, and a lack of sophisticated AI methods and automated tooling. To address this, we propose Flagger, the first academic decision-support system co-designed with domain experts that integrates a novel AI–based risk prediction engine for early identification of at-risk students automatically sifting through students' transcripts. Flagger features innovations such as a bespoke Transformer Backbone addressing dual-heterogeneity of transcripts, Modular Prediction Heads addressing evolution of at-risk predictors, and a Transcript Drill-Down and Course Dependency Engine for derived evidence for insight explanation. In this demonstration, we will feature a live exploration of transcripts guided by AI to aid advisors in understanding context, in faster triaging, and in the design of appropriate intervention. Ultimately, Flagger has been shown to increase at-risk detection rates as much as 3x in a retrospective study of 1,800 WPI students compared to current processes.

papers.title: TS-Lens: A Zero-Shot Time-Series Pattern Search System with Inspectable Waveform Queries
papers.abstract: Time-series pattern exploration is central to energy monitoring, industrial diagnosis, environmental sensing, and anomaly analysis. In practice, analysts often know the pattern they want to find but do not yet have a representative query segment. Query-by-example assumes such a segment is available; sketch systems require users to draw the target shape; and recent language-based methods often depend on fixed query grammars or trained text–time-series retrievers. We present TS-Lens, an interactive web system for zero-shot time-series pattern exploration. Its core interaction is Describe–Generate–Search: rather than mapping a natural-language description directly to results or to an opaque embedding, a language model generates a normalized waveform that the user can visually inspect and edit before search, and conventional similarity search retrieves matching windows or segments. This inspectable intermediate representation sits between parse-based querying (a fixed shape grammar) and embed-based querying (a trained text–time-series space), handling the uncertainty of LLM output through user inspection instead of task-specific retriever training. The same workspace also supports sketch, sample, preset, and cluster-medoid queries, plus Time-Series-to-Text explanations and label-basket curation. Across ETT-h1, NREL Solar 2023, and UCI Air Quality scenarios, TS-Lens shows how linguistic intent and remembered visual shapes can become reusable time-series queries.

papers.title: Orbit: Open Re-implementation of Biomedical Literature APIs
papers.abstract: Information retrieval experimentation with biomedical literature, despite an important area of research that can have a high impact, is often gated by a high barrier of entry. This is due to a variety of reasons including the requirement of bespoke document processing pipelines, complex indexing pipelines, and domain-specific query languages. While biomedical literature databases with freely available API access do exist, e.g., the Entrez API for PubMed and the ClinicalTrials.gov API, the use of such APIs is limiting: rate limits, restrictions on the number of documents that can be retrieved per request, and no way to extend or add functionality. The usual option for overcoming these limitations is to scrape or download the data, index it with an off-the-shelf search engine, and use whatever query language is implemented by the search engine. These off-the-shelf options are insufficient for reproducing retrieval in biomedical tasks, such as, systematic reviews, clinical-trial design and evidence-based clinical decision-making, that require retrieval from multiple sources and complex query mechanisms. We provide a drop-in, extendable, and open-source clean room re-implementation of two commonly used biomedical literature APIs that dramatically lowers the barrier of entry to experimentation in retrieval-based biomedical tasks. An overview of the system with example usage and video showcase is available at https://orbit.health-nlp.com.

papers.title: PolyUQuest: Verifiable Structure-Aware Web RAG over Heterogeneous Graphs
papers.abstract: Existing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems treat web pages as flat text, losing the structural and semantic signals encoded in HTML. We present PolyUQuest, a verifiable, structure-aware web RAG framework built on a heterogeneous graph that unifies hyperlink topology between pages, DOM hierarchy within pages, and entity–relation knowledge across pages. A two-tier router dispatches each query to one of three retrieval modes matched to its structural need, including direct block retrieval, cross-page graph traversal, and multi-hop entity reasoning. Each answer carries traceable provenance: every cited block records its source page, heading path, and entity links, so users can inspect the structural evidence behind a claim. We evaluate on the official websites of the Hong Kong Polytechnic University (PolyU), comprising 4,240 pages, 31,086 DOM blocks, 29,119 entities, and 37,680 relations, together with a multi-type evaluation benchmark. PolyUQuest improves correctness, coverage, and faithfulness over the evaluated baselines while maintaining query-time token consumption comparable to ChunkRAG and substantially below the graph-based RAG baselines. The demonstration provides an interactive interface for inspecting cited answers, comparing retrieval traces across routing modes, and exploring evidence graph paths. PolyUQuest is being prepared for deployment as a student-facing QA service at PolyU. A demo video is available at https://youtu.be/thKWYaL_4rw.

papers.title: GraphCraft: Skill-Centric Curation of Evolving GraphRAG Pipelines
papers.abstract: GraphRAG pipelines build entity–relation graphs from text and use them for retrieval and question answering, but extraction noise, entity fragmentation, and unstable clustering can silently corrupt the evidence behind an answer. Correcting these errors is difficult to scale because their dominant forms depend on the corpus and repeated corrections remain manual. We present GraphCraft, an interactive system that records provenance-rich human corrections and compiles repeated corrections into reusable curation skills. Each skill identifies similar errors in subsequent corpus updates and proposes edits for curator review; proposals are previewed rather than applied automatically. The same journal links corrections and skill suggestions back to their graph context and source spans, while bi-temporal graph state distinguishes changes to the stored graph from changes in the underlying world. We evaluate a compiled skill on held-out ingestion batches and demonstrate the complete workflow from diagnosing an erroneous answer, through repairing its graph evidence, to reusing the correction on later data. GraphCraft is released as an open platform with offline deployment. Code and offline deployment: https://github.com/apsolutions/graphrag; demo video: https://vimeo.com/1141894235.

papers.title: DeepRepro: State-Aware Subplanning for Paper-to-Code Reproduction in Evolving Repositories
papers.abstract: Recent advances in agentic large language models (LLMs) have enabled increasingly autonomous software engineering workflows, yet automatic machine learning (ML) paper-to-code reproduction remains a challenging long-horizon problem. Unlike conventional code generation, this task requires constructing and maintaining a fully functional repository whose state continuously evolves during execution. Existing systems typically rely on static upfront planning followed by sequential file-level generation, which often leads to inconsistencies as dependencies, interfaces, and execution feedback change over time. We propose DeepRepro, a state-aware framework for paper-to-code reproduction based on execution-state-aware subplanning. DeepRepro dynamically transforms evolving repository states and runtime feedback into fine-grained implementation subplans, keeping planning aligned with execution throughout repository construction. The framework further incorporates repository-aware orchestration and a lightweight process-aware interface for transparent monitoring of long-horizon reproduction. Experiments on PaperBench Code-Dev show that DeepRepro consistently outperforms strong scientific and commercial code-agent baselines. Code and demo are available at https://github.com/ruyisy/DeepRepro and https://youtu.be/ZvmtVX7Rleo.

papers.title: 1ShotBench: Demonstrating One-Shot Prompt Reproducibility for Autonomous Coding Agents
papers.abstract: The growing use of LLM agents raises a reproducibility problem: given the same task specification, different agents may follow different workflows, consume different resources, and produce varying artifacts and outcomes. We introduce the concept of One-Shot Prompt Reproducibility (1SPR): the consistency of one-shot execution across different agents given a fixed specification, without iterative human guidance. To operationalize this, we present 1ShotBench, a toolkit that repeatedly executes the same product requirement document (PRD) across isolated agent workspaces, capturing full traces, artifacts, and metadata, along with an LLM judge to evaluate results. We demonstrate a case study using software engineering tasks built around the Anserini information retrieval toolkit, though our system itself supports arbitrary tasks. 1ShotBench allows users to compare runs side by side, inspect how execution and implementation paths diverge despite a shared specification, and analyze how workflow differences relate to cost, latency, and correctness. Our central contribution is a reproducibility-oriented lens for examining agentic software development.

papers.title: Preserving LLM Output Distributions for Probabilistic Query Evaluation
affiliations: DI ENS, ENS, CNRS, PSL University, Inria
papers.abstract: Language models can be used to augment databases; typically, when this is done, their top prediction is used while the uncertainty in this prediction is ignored. We propose a framework that preserves output distributions from language model predictions and uses them to evaluate SQL queries probabilistically. First, a language model is used to infer new features from existing ones. Second, ProvSQL, a PostgreSQL extension implementing a probabilistic database through data provenance, encodes the predictions as mutually exclusive events in a provenance circuit and evaluates probabilistic queries. We extend ProvSQL to support text-value comparisons and join operations on language model predictions. We demonstrate the framework on 10\,612 Amazon musical products and 230\,156 user reviews, locally augmented with the Llama 3.1 model. We show that probabilistic querying reveals contradictions between model predictions and existing labels, recovers data records otherwise missed, and propagates joint uncertainty across multi-table queries.

papers.title: EviMap: Evidence-Grounded Hierarchical Topic Maps for Exploring Unlabeled Corpora
papers.abstract: Research teams and organizations often explore unfamiliar free-text collections, from survey comments and reviews to reports and domain documents, before labels, queries or coding schemes exist. At this stage, the first thematic map shapes what users notice, prioritize and carry into downstream analysis, so it should be trusted only insofar as it can be verified. Existing options force a trade-off between scale and verifiability. Qualitative coding preserves evidence but is slow. Search presupposes a query. Clustering and topic models scale but produce labels users must interpret. One-shot large language model (LLM) summaries are fluent yet difficult to reproduce or audit. We present EviMap, an interactive system providing researchers and practitioners with an auditable thematic overview of such corpora. Guided by model-generated context describing the corpus and hypothesized stakeholder concerns, EviMap extracts within-document evidence phrases and organizes them, rather than whole documents, into a three-level map of aspects, groups and fine-grained topics. Embedding-based clustering narrows the search space for finer semantic judgments by the LLM. Each node traces back to supporting phrase spans, so documents link to topics through evidence they contain and users can audit labels against the original text. Users can start from a top-level corpus map, drill into topics, inspect highlighted evidence in original documents, and combine two topics to find documents discussing both. We demonstrate this workflow across six heterogeneous corpora spanning 2,108 to 101,699 documents, with a comparison against flat and hierarchical LLM baselines. By grounding every label in verbatim source spans, EviMap makes a topic map not just readable, but verifiable. Code, demo video, and interactive dashboard are available at https://github.com/zhiyintan/EviMap.

papers.title: SAFE-Cascade: Cost-Adaptive Vision-Language Routing for Chart Question Answering
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are powerful for chart question answering, but invoking a VLM for every query can be unnecessarily expensive when many questions are answerable from OCR text and lightweight language reasoning. We demonstrate SAFE-Cascade, an interactive system for cost-adaptive chart question answering. Given a chart image and a natural-language question, SAFE-Cascade first extracts chart text with OCR, obtains a provisional answer from a text-only language model, and then uses a learned router to decide whether to accept the text answer or escalate to a VLM. The demo exposes this decision process to users: OCR evidence, text-only answer, routing probability, escalation decision, final answer, estimated cost, and estimated latency are shown side by side. SAFE-Cascade is designed as a transparent interface for understanding when visual grounding is actually needed. Users can upload or select charts, ask questions, inspect the evidence used by each pathway, compare text-only and VLM answers, and adjust the escalation threshold to explore the accuracy-cost frontier. The system is implemented with Azure Document Intelligence for OCR, gpt-5-mini as the text-only model, gemini-2.5-flash-image as the VLM, and a Random Forest router trained on inference-time features. On a held-out ChartQA test split of 375 examples from a 2,500-example experiment, SAFE-Cascade achieves 69.1% unified accuracy with 73.1% VLM invocation, compared with 67.7% accuracy and 100% VLM invocation for the full-VLM baseline. The observed +1.4 percentage-point difference is statistically uncertain, so we interpret SAFE-Cascade as matching full-VLM performance while reducing VLM calls by 26.9% and estimated cost by 9.3%. The demonstration shows how selective modality routing can make multimodal knowledge systems more transparent, tunable, and cost-aware.

papers.title: Cali-Tree: Hierarchical Calibration for VLM Judges
papers.abstract: Delegation of image assessment tasks to vision-language models (VLMs) is becoming common practice in a wide variety of domains. However, for many use cases, a significant calibration gap remains between these VLM judges and human evaluators, raising concerns about the reliability of their integration into production systems. To solve this problem, we introduce Cali-Tree, a hierarchical calibration framework for VLM judges that systematically refines rubric prompts to better align with human assessments. Starting with individual leaf prompts tuned for particular training instances, Cali-Tree iteratively clusters semantically similar nodes and merges their specialized evaluation criteria into more general parent prompts. This hierarchical training process helps mitigate destructive interference common with alternative approaches that attempt to optimize across all training instances at once. In fact, our preliminary results show that Cali-Tree can achieve an improvement of up to 30 percentage points over a baseline optimized with TextGrad. This demo will highlight the key benefits of our approach by allowing participants to interact with the Cali-Tree training pipeline for real-world image assessment tasks.

papers.title: DEP: A Decentralized Evaluation Protocol and Toolkit for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: With the rapid development of Large Language Models (LLMs), a large number of evaluation benchmarks have been proposed. However, most benchmarks lack unified evaluation standards, requiring users to manually implement customized scripts, which leads to high usage costs and difficulties in ensuring the consistency of evaluation results. Existing evaluation frameworks are typically centralized, integrating scripts, datasets, and reference answers into a single system, which not only increases system complexity but also raises the risk of benchmark leakage. To address these issues, we propose the D ecentralized E valuation P rotocol ( DEP ), which decouples users, LLMs, and benchmarks. By associating each benchmark with a server script that can either be locally mounted or remotely deployed, DEP enables lightweight, plug-and-play, broadly compatible evaluations while preventing data leakage. Once adapted, the benchmark can be reused over the long term. To facilitate practical adoption, we developed the DEP Toolkit , a toolkit compatible with the DEP protocol that supports features such as resumable evaluation, concurrent requests, and congestion control, while also providing both a CLI and a GUI. In addition, we provide detailed documentation to guide benchmark adaptation for DEP. Using the DEP Toolkit, we validated the effectiveness of DEP in applications, demonstrating its ability to reduce the deployment cost of benchmark evaluation. As of May 2026, we have adapted more than 60 benchmarks and continue to promote community-driven collaboration to support unified evaluation across domains.

papers.title: AEQUITAS: A Toolkit for Stock Market Prediction and Portfolio Evaluation
affiliations: University of Modena and Reggio Emilia
papers.abstract: Stock market prediction has produced a large number of models: comparing them in practice remains difficult. Existing approaches are often released as isolated implementations, use different data construction and preprocessing pipelines, and report heterogeneous machine learning and portfolio metrics. As a result, analysts cannot easily determine whether observed performance differences are due to the models themselves or to differences in data preparation, experimental design, and evaluation protocols. To address these challenges, we present AEQUITAS, A n E valuation toolkit for QU ant I tative and T rading A naly S is. It supports the construction, storage, and reuse of heterogeneous financial datasets, integrates classification, regression, and ranking models under consistent settings, and links model outputs to standardized portfolio strategies.
