The demonstration showcases how users can configure stock prediction experiments, compare pipelines across horizons, investment universes, and portfolio settings, and interpret predictive and portfolio-level results through an interactive dashboard with LLM-based support.

papers.title: UniTor ESG Insights: An Interactive Human-in-the-Loop System for Traceable Sustainability Report Analysis
papers.abstract: We present UniTor ESG Insights, an interactive system for traceable sustainability report analysis. Starting from PDF reports, the system extracts paragraph-level textual units, preserves page-level provenance, and applies a set of ESG classification modules for sustainability relevance detection, GRI--SDG topic alignment, disclosure quality assessment, qualitative/quantitative evidence identification, and climate-related analysis. The system targets ESG analysts, auditors, regulators, and corporate sustainability managers who need to inspect and aggregate evidence from long and partially structured reports. Unlike approaches that return only document-level labels or aggregate ESG scores, UniTor ESG Insights follows a bottom-up workflow in which predictions are generated at paragraph level and higher-level summaries remain linked to the underlying textual evidence. Users can inspect extracted paragraphs, filter predictions, correct intermediate outputs, re-upload refined data, visualize distributions, and export structured results. The demonstration shows an end-to-end scenario in which a user uploads a sustainability report, explores paragraph-level ESG predictions, analyzes disclosure quality and evidence characteristics, and generates traceable analytical views through a Gradio interface deployed on Hugging Face Spaces.

papers.title: SAGE: A Guardrailed LLM Tutoring System with Scaffolded Self-Regulated Learning for Adult Education
papers.abstract: We present SAGE (Scaffolded, Audited, Guided Education), a deployable guardrailed LLM tutoring system for adult learners. Left unrestricted, chat assistants often hand over the answer, which can improve in-the-moment performance but may erode the self-regulation that supports durable learning. SAGE wraps a commercial LLM in interface-level guardrails that require learners to engage before the model answers: a lightweight intent classifier routes each turn to one of three self-regulated-learning scaffolds (write-your-approach-first, paraphrase-before-proceeding, attempt-before-reveal), so a request to "just give me the answer" is held behind a guided step rather than answered outright. As a secondary safeguard, an online counterfactual fairness audit checks whether the guardrailed tutor responds differently across age band, language dominance, prior education, and digital fluency, while an agentic rectifier regenerates any flagged turn; a pseudonymous interaction log supports per-cohort analytics. The demonstration runs the same business-education prompt through an unrestricted LLM and through SAGE side by side, allowing an attendee to watch the scaffold gate hold the answer, then exercise the counterfactual swap, inspect the per-attribute audit panel, and trigger the rectifier. The system is open-source and available at https://github.com/kwanhui/public-llmLearnFair-CIKM2026 to allow other groups to deploy and audit their own scaffolds.

papers.title: CORAL: COlonography Radiology Annotation Lab
affiliations: University of Nebraska Medical Center College of Dentistry
papers.abstract: CT colonography (CTC) interpretation hinges on three intertwined structures: the colonic lumen, intracolonic fluid pockets, and polyps. Constructing voxel-level ground truth for these structures is a persistent bottleneck for computer-aided diagnosis. We present CORAL , a browser-based CT colonography annotation environment that delivers an end-to-end workflow for joint lumen, fluid-pocket, and polyp annotation, and provides a slice-level free-text comment panel for radiologists to describe their findings. CORAL parses DICOM and NIfTI volumes entirely in the browser; all image processing runs on the client and no annotation data is uploaded to a remote server. It offers six label-aware brushes, four of which encode HU-based domain knowledge (edge-aware and a fluid brush family), four in-browser refinements (GrabCut-style, Random-Walker-style, Combined, and Fluid-aware GrabCut-style), slice-to-slice mask propagation, 3D mesh visualisation, and on-image measurement. The resulting environment pairs voxel-level CTC annotations with radiologists' free-text reasoning, supporting downstream research in dataset construction and explainable medical AI. A live demo and walkthrough video are linked from our open-source repository at https://github.com/catarina-moreira/CORAL. A demo video is publicly available at https://youtu.be/hq48kqLNLD0.

papers.title: PRISM: A Personalized News Recommendation System for Mitigating Political Echo Chambers
papers.abstract: Personalized news recommendation systems often reinforce users' pre-existing beliefs by limiting their exposure, contributing to political echo chambers. Existing mitigation approaches—such as rewriting biased text or diversifying recommendations—risk distorting article semantics or deepening polarization, while typically offering no rationale for why content is judged biased. We present PRISM, an interactive web-based news recommendation system that mitigates political echo chambers across three levels of granularity: feed level, article level, and event level. Building on KHAN (political stance prediction) and CROWN (personalized news recommendation) from our prior work, PRISM lets users monitor the political distribution of their reading history and current recommendations, inspect each article's predicted stance with bias-indicative keywords and natural-language rationales, and voluntarily explore cross-stance coverage of the same news event, preserving user autonomy in line with self-determination theory. PRISM is available at https://github.com/Hoyeol-Yang/PRISM, with a demonstration video at https://youtu.be/NbcvHME__cI.

papers.title: Didact: A Cross-Domain Capability Discovery System for Defence
papers.abstract: Policymakers in defence and defence-aligned sectors must monitor rapidly evolving research alongside sector priorities relevant to operational and strategic needs. In practice, these sources are fragmented across heterogeneous formats, disjoint repositories, making capability discovery slow and difficult to audit. We present Didact, a prototype that integrates two sources: publicly available defence reports and policy documents from Australia, and a purpose-built knowledge graph derived from Australian research publications. Didact provides natural language conversations for policy-oriented workflows, and devises a composite retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline that allows synthesis of information from both sources. A key feature of Didact is an interactive Evidence Rail that presents retrieved document evidence and, when research-graph retrieval is used, visualises relevant entities and relationships. Automated evaluation on DoRA-QnA50 characterises Didact's retrieval quality, response quality, and runtime. While Didact has been co-developed as an academia-industry project for the Australian defence context, it is adaptable to other domains where knowledge is similarly fragmented and reliability is critical. A demonstration video is available here: https://youtu.be/KRtlq3LQ9WA.

papers.title: Automatic Reference Scanner and Explainer: Don't Get Caught with Dirty References
papers.abstract: The growing use of large language models (LLMs) in academic writing has introduced a new failure mode: hallucinated references, citations to papers that do not exist or whose metadata is incorrect. Such fabricated references are easy to overlook during writing and review, yet they undermine the integrity of the scholarly record. The problem has reached a scale that program committees can no longer ignore: during camera-ready consistency checks for ACL 2026, over 100 already-accepted papers were found to cite non-existent literature and were rejected. We present the Automatic Reference Scanner and Explainer, a self-hostable system that parses the bibliography of a submitted PDF, cross-checks every reference against up to nine scholarly registries, and explains each verdict: every reference is labelled as matched, not found, or mismatched (e.g., incorrect authors, venue, or identifier), with the evidence per source and the reason stated explicitly, both in audit cards and as colour-coded highlights on the PDF itself. On 13 papers with all 460 references manually annotated, our tool catches 83% of fabricated references while only 1.5% of the references it clears are fabricated - turning hours of manual bibliography checking by authors, reviewers, and editors into minutes of targeted triage.

papers.title: ReLevel: A Framework for Adaptive Self-Reflection in Multi-Level Planning for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract: We present ReLevel, a framework for adaptive reflection-level selection that decides at which level of an agent's plan to reflect when a failure occurs. Modern agents decompose a complex task into a hierarchy of sub-tasks down to individual actions and reflect when an action fails. The choice of reflection-level is significant: reflecting at the failed action alone is cheap but lets errors propagate to sibling steps that share the same flawed assumption, while re-planning the whole task fixes the error but discards already completed work. ReLevel instead derives three signals from each failure to adaptively select the reflection-level: the scope of invalidated assumptions, the level the model's sampled attribution points to, and the cost--benefit of regenerating each candidate level. It treats each signal as a lower bound on how coarse the reflection must be and reflects at the tightest level that satisfies all three. The lowest common ancestor of the affected steps sets a correctness floor, raised only when confidence or cost--benefit shows that a globally unsound design or an unreliable local fix requires more. An accompanying interactive system visualizes the plan tree, the failure, the three signals, and the selected level, letting users compare action-level, plan-level, and adaptive strategies on the same failure. Across six language models, ReLevel matches the repair success of whole-plan re-planning while re-executing about a third of the actions, whereas action-level reflection leaves the failure unrepaired.

papers.title: Agent-R1: A Unified and Modular Framework for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
affiliations: State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, University of Science and Technology of China
papers.abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on reinforcement learning to improve multi-turn reasoning, tool use, and environment interaction. However, existing training pipelines often treat an agent trajectory as a flat token sequence or a reconstructed message trace, making it difficult to preserve rollout fidelity, manage long contexts, and inspect step-level credit signals. We present Agent-R1, an open-source modular framework for agentic reinforcement learning (RL). Agent-R1 uses interaction steps as the native unit for trajectory representation, replay, and environment interaction, and decouples exact trajectory storage from flexible context construction. The system supports context-management policies, step-level rollout inspection, action-mask visualization, tool-feedback analysis, and unified comparison of related RL algorithms. Through demonstrations on multiple tasks, Agent-R1 enables users to configure, train, inspect, and compare agentic RL workflows within a single interactive interface. Code and project resources are available at https://github.com/AgentR1/Agent-R1.

papers.title: Tracing the Chain Rule: Exploring Automatic Differentiation Inside a Code-Generating Database System
papers.abstract: Code-generating database systems improve the runtime for automatic differentiation by eliminating function calls and storing partial derivatives within registers for reuse. This work demonstrates our extension of forward and reverse mode automatic differentiation in LingoDB. In conjunction with implemented matrix operations, the operators compute the derivatives for in-database gradient descent even for simple neural networks based on matrix multiplication. We present dsql, an interactive web interface for writing SQL queries with lambda-based loss functions and for inspecting the generated MLIR code at every compilation stage. Side-by-side comparisons show the differences in generated code size, optimisation and execution time between forward and reverse mode differentiation. Pre-loaded example workloads for linear regression and neural network training allow users to explore the interplay between automatic differentiation and compiler optimisations interactively.

papers.title: ''Will This Data Break My Task?'' Interactive Synthesis of Task-Aware Data Unit Tests
papers.abstract: Data is a central resource for modern enterprises and institutions, and data errors propagating through data pipelines lead to serious impact in production. Therefore, data validation is essential for ensuring the reliability of downstream applications. This led to the development of data unit tests, executable programs that test data before moving it around through large data pipelines. However, existing frameworks derive data unit tests from observed data alone, ignoring the semantics of the code that consumes the data downstream. To this end, we present PrismaDV, a compound AI system that synthesizes task-aware data unit tests for tabular data by jointly analyzing data and downstream task code. PrismaDV decomposes the test generation into multiple LLM-powered steps: data profiling, detection of column accesses, data flow analysis in the task code, and the inference of implicit data assumptions. It subsequently synthesizes code for the data unit test, and maintains an internal “data-code assumption graph” that links generated data constraints back to the task's source code. We demonstrate PrismaDV through an interactive web-based interface where attendees run the system on five real-world datasets with 60 downstream tasks, synthesize, inspect and refine both natural language assumptions about the data and executable data constraints. The interface allows attendees to navigate the data-code assumption graph, compare task-aware data unit tests against task-agnostic baselines on erroneous data batches, and interactively edit assumptions and data constraints. Furthermore, attendees can observe how a custom prompt optimizer adapts the system to specific datasets over time.

papers.title: Tool-supported Expert Validation of CONTEXT-sensitive Data Extraction from Scientific Articles
papers.abstract: Extracting structured information from scientific literature (e.g., in life sciences) is a considerably valuable and knowledge-intensive task. Relevant target information is often highly context-sensitive and scattered across unstructured, heterogeneous documents spanning text, tables, figures, and supplementary materials. For instance, statistical measures may not be apparent in the text, requiring the interpretation of multiple methodological and experimental details across documents. Large Language Models (LLMs) offer promising support for automating this process, yet they remain prone to error, making expert curation essential. Validation is, however, expensive and time-consuming, since extracted values must be traced back to their precise location in long, multi-document sources. Here, we present CONTEXT, a domain-agnostic tool that enables in-context expert judgment over LLM-extracted outputs. Given a pipeline that returns, for each target field and scientific article, the identified value with its source location –file, section, subsection, and exact passage– our tool maps this output back to the original document, enabling efficient in-context assessment, robust to typical LLM noise such as paraphrasing and hallucination. We demonstrate CONTEXT's utility with a use case in genetics, involving the curation of metadata for polygenic risk score models. Validated extractions are exported as structured ground-truth records, providing a rich annotation format for downstream use in knowledge-intensive tasks. Demonstration video and source code are available.

papers.title: ESG-CRE: A Convert-Retrieve-Extract Framework with a Human-Guided Refinement Loop for ESG Reports
papers.abstract: Structured ESG information underpins sustainability analysis and regulatory reporting, yet ESG reports vary so widely in layout, terminology, and units that no fixed schema extracts them well. We present ESG-CRE, an interactive system for ESG report extraction built on a Convert–Retrieve–Extract pipeline: it converts PDF reports into layout-aware page artifacts, retrieves indicator-relevant contexts, and produces schema-guided, source-linked records. The core of ESG-CRE is a human-guided refinement loop that treats the schema as an editable, auditable artifact rather than a fixed input. Experts judge individual records against their source pages, and ESG-CRE compiles these judgements into versioned, additively merged schema updates that grow its domain knowledge without discarding prior rules. On public Taiwanese ESG reports, a single round of expert review yields measurable gains in extraction quality. Attendees can run the full extract–review–refine cycle live; a demo video is publicly available. (https://youtu.be/w1-iwK701Mo)

papers.title: CivicFlow: A Human-in-the-Loop Workbench for Evolving Civic-Report Taxonomies
papers.abstract: Large-scale classification of civic reports is not a fixed assignment problem. Label definitions and the taxonomy keep evolving with policy and citizen language, one report often spans several departments and hierarchical paths at once, and confirmed labels are revised as administrative staff renegotiate definitions. Ground truth is therefore ongoing human judgment, not a one-shot label. We present CivicFlow, a web-based human-in-the-loop workbench for evolving civic-report taxonomies. CivicFlow keeps human-confirmed ground truth separate from model predictions, updating it only through reviewer confirmation, while keyword/entity, classifier, and retrieval-augmented large language model (LLM) evidence stays read-only. It connects taxonomy editing, active-learning simulation, quality analysis, and cluster triage in one loop. On 35,843 usable labeled Korean safety reports, operators can estimate how active-learning strategies reduce label reveals and broaden the observed label-set space before live review.

papers.title: TonalKeys: Diacritic Input and Morphology-Aware Emoji Search for African Languages on the Web and Mobile
papers.abstract: Africa is home to more than 2,000 languages, yet support for these languages at the point of text input remains limited. Many African orthographies require diacritics and tone marks that standard keyboards do not provide, and emoji search in an African language finds little or nothing because the keyword data in Unicode CLDR remains uneven or absent. We demonstrate TonalKeys, a live input system that closes both gaps with two front-ends sharing one retrieval core. A publicly released Chrome extension works anywhere on the web, including canvas applications such as Google Docs where direct insertion is blocked, and a working Android keyboard prototype serves mobile-first settings. TonalKeys offers curated character entry for 18 languages across five regions and a morphology- and code-mix-aware emoji search that currently covers Swahili, with further languages planned. A hybrid stemmer pairs a lexicon derived from an existing Swahili verb-conjugation resource with rule-based affix peeling to reduce inflected and code-mixed queries to the roots under which emoji are annotated. We release the system openly with a first version of the annotated emoji dataset of 3,642 Swahili entries, documenting the annotation procedure and the current limits of the pipeline. Attendees install TonalKeys on their own laptop or phone, type in the supported languages, and run Swahili emoji search live.

papers.title: OriginBlame: Record- and Token-Level Data Provenance for AI Training Datasets
papers.abstract: Modern AI training datasets are assembled from thousands of sources through processing, tokenization, and packing—transformations that destroy the mapping between individual training records and their original contributors. When a contributor requests removal, audits demand license traceability, or quality issues require tracing specific data, this provenance gap forces trainers into catastrophic file-level over-deletion. We present OriginBlame (ob), a record- and token-level data provenance system that propagates author identity through data processing pipelines via a three-layer content-addressable architecture. ob resolves contributor-level queries into precise record sets through deterministic SHA-256 lookups, without model access or post-hoc inference. On a Chinese Wikipedia benchmark (220,000 pages, 482,543 contributors), record-level provenance reduces over-deletion from 2.8×–44.8× (file-level) to near-parity, while pipeline integration adds 1–21% throughput overhead (1–2% HuggingFace, 9–21% Datatrove). Provenance-based forget sets (training records targeted for removal) integrate with existing unlearning algorithms on a 1.7B model, though a gap remains: provenance identifies source records, but trained models store transformed knowledge beyond individual records. Our demonstration provides an interactive platform for real-time provenance queries, three-level revocation, and over-deletion comparison.

papers.title: Ed-Alpha: An Open Benchmark for Predicting Investment-Relevant Corporate Events from Open Data
papers.abstract: We present Ed-Alpha, an open benchmark platform for predicting and evaluating investment-relevant corporate events using public data. Existing event-driven investment research often relies on expensive, proprietary data, making methods difficult to reproduce or compare. Ed-Alpha addresses this challenge by providing a transparent and fully reproducible pipeline. Specifically, it uses regulatory filings from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) as ground-truth event labels and combines them with high-volume news signals from the GDELT project. Using Ed-Alpha, our initial analysis reveals that even state-of-the-art LLMs achieve only limited effectiveness in predicting corporate events; we therefore expect the platform to facilitate more efficient and transparent experimentation toward future improvements in effectiveness. The benchmark platform and a demonstration video, as well as all related code and methods, are available in our repository. https://e9technologies.github.io/ED-ALPHA https://github.com/E9Technologies/ed-alpha

papers.title: SoilCast: An Interactive Machine-Learning System for Forecasting Soil Health under Climate and Management Scenarios
affiliations: International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis
papers.abstract: We present SoilCast, an interactive machine-learning system for real-time exploration of long-term soil health outcomes under alternative climate and agricultural management scenarios across Europe. SoilCast replaces computationally expensive process-based environmental simulations with pretrained surrogate models learned from more than 15 million simulator-generated samples. The system employs CatBoost-based state-transition emulators that predict changes in soil organic carbon, soil nitrogen, and crop productivity over successive 20-year periods, enabling recursive multi-step forecasts through 2100. To support reliable scenario analysis, SoilCast visualizes uncertainty intervals derived from empirical rollout errors on held-out spatial test regions, capturing the accumulation of forecast error over time. The application demonstrates how scalable surrogate modeling can transform complex scientific simulators into responsive decision-support systems for sustainable land management.

papers.title: HINTLAB: An Interactive Tool for Hint Generation, Analysis and Evaluation
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in educational contexts, yet their default answer-centric interaction paradigm conflicts with established principles of effective learning. Direct solution delivery can reduce productive struggle and encourage cognitive offloading rather than deep understanding. To address this tension, we present HintLab, a visualization-driven, human-in-the-loop platform for generating, analyzing, and refining LLM-generated pedagogical hints. The system operationalizes five cognitively grounded evaluation dimensions—Convergence, Relevance, Readability, Familiarity, and Leakage Avoidance—and exposes them through interactive visual analytics that support comparative inspection, manual refinement, and scaffolded sequencing of hints. Unlike standard chat interfaces, HintLab enables structured multi-model comparison, answer-space reduction analysis, and convergence-based scaffolding design without requiring domain modeling or programming expertise. A human evaluation involving 901 generated hints demonstrates favorable ratings across multiple pedagogically motivated dimensions, while a hint-assisted question answering study shows that the generated hints substantially improve users' ability to answer previously unsolved questions. The system is publicly available, with source code accessible on GitHub, and a demonstration video online.

papers.title: ShanLiangRen: A Nutrition Agent for Personalized Daily Meal Planning
papers.abstract: Dietary nutrition planning plays an important role in chronic disease management and maintaining a healthy body. In applications, it must simultaneously satisfy personalized constraints and reasonable multidimensional nutritional goals. These two aspects often conflict, and user constraints evolve with feedback, resulting in a substantial gap between generic guidelines and executable plans. To bridge this gap, we first propose the personalized fully quantified multiobjective dietary planning problem (MDP). To tackle MDP, we develop a nutrition agent, ShanLiangRen. The system first transforms dietary specifications, nutrient data, user attributes and natural language requirements into an individualized constrained planning instance. It then employs an exact retrieval-augmented generation method to shrink the feasible candidate set from a large scale ingredient and recipe space. Finally, it adopts a refinement guided by Pareto principles, where an LLM iteratively revises candidate plans under deterministic nutrition computation and feedback from constraint verification. The system outputs fully quantified meal plans with explicit ingredients and portion sizes, together with reports on nutrition compliance that show constraint satisfaction and nutrient interval attainment. We have released the system online as a WeChat Program, ShanLiangRen. A demo video is available at https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=652OtY5VlGA.
